body.text: Ārya Saṃghāṭa Sūtra
body.translated_text: <s>Ārya Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>

body.text:
svastiḥ
namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
May there be well-being!
Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

body.text: [SaSū 1] evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / gṛddhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena / sārdhaṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 1] Thus have I heard: At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛddhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, together with

body.text: [SaSū 2] dvāviṃśatibhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ tadyathā āyuṣmatā cājñātakauṇḍinyena / āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyena / āyuṣmatā ca śāradvatīputreṇa / āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca rāhulena / āyuṣmatā ca bakkulena / āyuṣmatā ca bhadravāsena / āyuṣmatā ca bhadraśriyā / āyuṣmatā ca nandaśriyā / āyuṣmatā ca jāṅgulena / āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā / āyuṣmatā ca revatena / āyuṣmatā ca nandasenena / āyuṣmatā cānandena / evaṃpramukhairdvāviṃśatibhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 2] twenty-two thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>, namely: the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, the venerable <s>Bakkula</s>, the venerable <s>Bhadravāsa</s>, the venerable <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, the venerable <s>Nandaśrī</s>, the venerable <s>Jāṅgula</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Nandasena</s>, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>—headed by these, twenty-two thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>;

body.text: [SaSū 3] dvāṣaṣṭibhiśca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ tadyathā maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / sarvaśūreṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / kumāraśriyā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / kumāravāsinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / kumārabhadreṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / anūnena ca (nāma) bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / maṃjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / samantabhadrena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / sudarśanena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / bhaiṣajyarājena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / (vajrasenena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena /) evaṃpramukhairdvāṣaṣṭibhirbodhisattvasahasraiḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 3] and sixty-two thousand <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, namely: the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Kumāraśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Kumāravāsin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Kumārabhadra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Anūna</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sudarśana</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, (the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajrasena</s>)—headed by these, sixty-two thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>;

body.text: [SaSū 4] dvāṣaṣṭibhiśca devaputrasahasraiḥ tadyathā arjunena ca devaputreṇa / bhadreṇa ca devaputreṇa / subhadreṇa ca devaputreṇa / dharmarucinā ca devaputreṇa / candanagarbheṇa ca devaputreṇa / candavāsinā ca devaputreṇa / candanena ca devaputreṇa / candanasenena ca devaputreṇa / evaṃpramukhairdvāṣaṣṭibhirdevaputrasahasraiḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 4] and sixty-two thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), namely: the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Arjuna</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Bhadra</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Subhadra</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Dharmaruci</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Candanagarbha</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Candavāsin</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Candana</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Candanasena</s>—headed by these, sixty-two thousand <s>devaputras</s>;

body.text: [SaSū 5] aṣṭābhiśca devakanyāsahasraiḥ tadyathā mṛdaṃginyā ca devakanyāyā / prāsādavatyā ca devakanyāyā / mahātmasaṃprayuktayā ca devakanyāyā / varṣaśriyāyā ca devakanyāyā / (padmaśriyāya ca devakanyāyā /) prajāpativāsinyā ca devakanyāyā / balinyā ca devakanyāyā / subāhuyuktayā ca devakanyāyā / evaṃpramukhairaṣṭābhirdevakanyāsahasraiḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 5] and eight thousand <s>devakanyās</s> (celestial maidens), namely: the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Mṛdaṅginī</s>, the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Prāsādavatī</s>, the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Mahātmasaṃprayuktā</s>, the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Varṣaśrī</s>, (the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Padmaśrī</s>,) the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Prajāpativāsinī</s>, the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Balinī</s>, the <s>devakanyā</s> <s>Subāhuyuktā</s>—headed by these, eight thousand <s>devakanyās</s>;

body.text: [SaSū 6] aṣṭābhiśca nāgarājasahasraiḥ tadyathā apalālena ca nāgarājñā / elapatreṇa ca nāgarājñā / timiṅgilena ca nāgarājñā / kuṃbhasāreṇa ca nāgarājñā / kuṃbhaśīrṣeṇa ca nāgarājñā / sunandena ca nāgarājñā / suśākhena ca nāgarājñā / gavaśīrṣeṇa ca nāgārājñā / evaṃpramukhairaṣṭābhirnāgarājasahasrais
body.translated_text: [SaSū 6] and eight thousand <s>nāga</s> kings, namely: the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Apalāla</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Elapatra</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Timiṅgila</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Kumbhasāra</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Kumbhaśīrṣa</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Sunanda</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Suśākha</s>, the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Gavaśīrṣa</s>—headed by these, eight thousand <s>nāga</s> kings.

body.text: [SaSū 7] te sarve yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yena gṛddhrakūṭaḥ parvato yena ca bhagavāṃcchākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāmadupasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triṣpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ puratastasthire /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 7] All of them approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, <s>Gṛddhrakūṭa</s> mountain, and the Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One; having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood before the Blessed One.

body.text: [SaSū 8] (etadavocan deśayatu bhagavāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatu sugataḥ dharmaṃ yaṃ śrutvāsme kṣipramanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyema yena ca sarvasattvānāṃ karmāvaraṇakṣayo bhaveyāt) bhagavāṃśca tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati sma /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 8] (They said this: 'May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s>, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>, hearing which we may quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, and by which the <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations) of all beings may be exhausted.') The Blessed One consented through silence.

body.text: [SaSū 9] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat
body.translated_text: [SaSū 9] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One:

body.text: [SaSū 10] bahvyo bhagavan devakoṭyopsarakanyākoṭyo bodhisattvakoṭyaḥ bahvyo bhagavaṃcchrāvakakoṭyaḥ sannipatitāḥ sanniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya / tatsādhu bhagavan teṣāṃ yathāsannipatitānāṃ (sanniṣaṇṇānāṃ) tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastathārūpaṃ dharmanayapraveśaṃ deśayatu / yathaiṣāṃ syāddīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyānāṃ ca yathārūpeṇa dharmanayapraveśena deśitena vṛddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ saha śravaṇenaiva sarvakarmāvaraṇāni caiṣāṃ parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ daharāśca sattvāḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvabhiyujyamānā viśeṣāmadhigaccheyurna hīyeranna parihīyeran kuśalairdharmaiḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 10] 'Many <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of gods, O Blessed One, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, O Blessed One, have gathered and are seated for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, may the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, be pleased to teach such an entry into the method of <s>Dharma</s> to those assembled (and seated), so that it may be for their benefit, welfare, and happiness for a long time—for gods and humans—such that, by the entry into the method of <s>Dharma</s> thus taught, the <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations) of mature beings may go to complete exhaustion merely by hearing, and young beings, applying themselves to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, may attain distinction and may not diminish or decline in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 11] evamukte bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - sādhu sādhu sarveśūra sādhu khalu punastvaṃ sarvaśūra yastvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / tena hi tvaṃ sarvaśūra śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru................. te /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 11] When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: 'Well done, well done, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Well done indeed that you, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, consider this matter worthy of asking the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. Therefore, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, listen well and thoroughly, and attend with your mind... to you [I shall speak].'

body.text: [SaSū 12] evaṃ bhagavanniti sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pravyaśrauṣād /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 12] 'So be it, Blessed One,' said the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, and he listened to the Blessed One.

body.text: [SaSū 13] bhagavan asyaitadavocat asti sarvaśūra [(saddharmaparyāyo / yena dharmaparyāyeṇa sarvasatvānāṃ paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāvaraṇani kṣayaṃ ................... / tathānye ca karmāvaraṇāni kṣayaṃ gacchante / kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhayaṃteḥkataro bhagavaṃ saddharmaparyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 13] The Blessed One spoke thus: 'There is, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, [(a <s>dharma-paryāya</s> (discourse on Dharma), by which <s>dharma-paryāya</s> the <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> of the five heinous acts of all beings go to exhaustion... and other <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> also go to exhaustion, and one quickly attains unsurpassed perfect awakening.) What, Blessed One, is that <s>dharma-paryāya</s>?'

body.text: [SaSū 14] bhagavānāhaḥ) saṃghāṭo nāma dharmaparyāya / ya etarhi jambudvīpe pracariṣyati / yaḥ kaścit sarvaśūremaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati / tasya pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi parikṣayaṃ yāsyanti / avaivartikāśca bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 14] The Blessed One said:] 'It is the <s>dharma-paryāya</s> called <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>. It will circulate now in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Whoever, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, the five heinous <s>karmas</s> of that [person] will go to complete exhaustion. And they will become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-returners) in unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 15] tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra ya imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati / yathaikasya tathāgatasya [satkāraṃ kṛtvā] puṇyaskandhastathā tāvantaṃ puṇyaskandhaḥ sa sattva prasaviṣyatīti / naivaṃ sarvaśūra draṣṭavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 15] 'What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>? Whoever will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s>—just as is the aggregate of merit from [venerating] one <s>Tathāgata</s>, so great an aggregate of merit will that being generate.' 'It should not be seen thus, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 16] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha / yathā kathaṃ punarbhagavan draṣṭavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 16] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Then how, Blessed One, should it be seen?'

body.text: bhagavānāha / yathā gaṃgānadībālukāsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ (satkāraṃ kṛtvā) puṇyaskandhastāvantaṃ sarvaśūra te satvāḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti / ye sarvaśūra imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti te sarve avaivartikā bhaviṣyanti (anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodheḥ) / sarve ca tathāgataṃ drakṣyanti / sarve ca tathāgatadarśāvino bhaviṣyanti / sarve cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / adhṛṣyāśca bhaviṣyanti mārena pāpīmatā / te ca sarve tadeva kuśaladharmamanuprāpsyanti / ye sarvaśūra imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ śroṣyanti / te sarve utpādanirodhaṃ jñāsyanti /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'The aggregate of merit equal to [venerating] <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—so great an aggregate of merit, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will those beings generate who, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>. They will all become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-returners) in unsurpassed perfect awakening. And all will see a <s>Tathāgata</s>. And all will become seers of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And all will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And they will be indomitable by <s>Māra</s> the Evil One. And they will all attain that very wholesome <s>dharma</s>—all who, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>. They will all know arising and cessation.'

body.text: [SaSū 17] atha te sarve (yathāsannipatitā bodhisattvā mahāśrāvakā) devanāgamanuṣyāpsarakanyākoṭyastena kālena tena samayenotthāyāsanebhyaḥ ekāṃsānyuttarāsaṃgāni kṛtvā dakṣiṇāni jānumaṇḍalāni pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjalayaḥ praṇamayya (te sarve) bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti sma / kiyantaṃ bhagavannekasya tathāgatasya (satkāraṃ kṛtvā) puṇyaskandhaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 17] Then all of them—(the assembled <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great <s>śrāvakas</s>,) <s>koṭis</s> of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, humans, and <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs)—at that time, at that moment, rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, placed their right knees on the ground, joined their palms toward the Blessed One, and (they all) asked the Blessed One: 'How great, Blessed One, is the aggregate of merit from [venerating] one <s>Tathāgata</s>?'

body.text: [SaSū 18] bhagavān āha / śṛṇu kulaputrā; ekasya buddhasya puṇyaskandhasya pramāṇaṃ tadyathā mahāsamudre udakabindavaḥ yāvanto jaṃbudvīpe paramāṇavaḥ yathā gaṃgānadībālikāsamāḥ sattvāste sarve daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ yacca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ puṇyaskandhamato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhamekasya buddhasya (puṇyaskandham) / ataśca te sarvaśūra sattvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / yāvanna śakyaṃ gaṇanāyogena tasya puṇyaskandhasya paryantamadhigantuṃ / yasya sarvaśūra tasmin kāle tasmin samaye etad vacanaṃ śrutvā mahānutsāho bhaviṣyati sa evamaprameyaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 18] The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Listen, O son of noble family. The measure of the merit-aggregate of a single <s>Buddha</s> is as follows: as many water-drops as there are in the great ocean, as many atoms as there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, as many beings as equal the grains of sand of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — if all those beings were <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten stages, the merit-aggregate of a single <s>Buddha</s> would be even greater than the merit-aggregate of all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And moreover, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings who will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse of the Dharma) will generate even more merit than that. It is not possible by any calculation to reach the limit of that merit-aggregate. Whoever, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, at that time, at that moment, having heard these words, will have great enthusiasm — that person will generate such an immeasurable merit-aggregate.

body.text: [SaSū 19] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - katame te bhagavan sattvā ye dharmaparitṛṣitā bhaviṣyanti / evamukte bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - dvāvimau sarvaśūra sattvau dharmaparitṛṣitau / katamau dvau / yadutaikaḥ sarvaśūra sarvasattvasamacittaḥ dvitīyaḥ sarvaśūra yo dharmaṃ śrutvā sarvasattvānāṃ samaṃ prakāśayati (imau dvau dharmaparitṛṣitau) /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 19] Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: Who are those beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who will be thirsting for the Dharma? Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: There are these two kinds of beings, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who thirst for the Dharma. Which two? Namely, the first, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is one who has equal mind toward all beings; the second, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is one who, having heard the Dharma, illuminates it equally for all beings. These two are those who thirst for the Dharma.

body.text: [SaSū 20] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - katamaṃ bhagavan dharmaṃ śrutvā sarvasattvānāṃ samaprakāśanā; bhagavān āha - ekaḥ sarvaśūra dharmaṃ śrutvā bodhāya pariṇāmayaṃti / yadā ca bodhāya pariṇāmayati tadā sarvasattvā dharmaparitṛṣitā bhaviṣyanti / dvitīyassarvaśūra yo mahāyānamavagāhayati sa nityaṃ dharmaparitṛṣito bhavat /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 20] The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: Having heard which Dharma, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does one illuminate it equally for all beings? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: The first, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having heard the Dharma, dedicates it toward awakening. And when one dedicates it toward awakening, then all beings will become those who thirst for the Dharma. The second, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is one who plunges into the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) — that one is always thirsting for the Dharma.

body.text: [SaSū 21] atha te devanāgamanuṣyāpsarasakoṭya utthāyāsanād bhagavataḥ purataḥ prāṃjalayo bhūtvā bhagavantametadavocan vayaṃ bhagavan dharmaparitṛṣitāḥ paripūrayatu bhagavān asmākaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ cāśā /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 21] Then those tens of millions of <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), humans, and <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), rising from their seats, stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with palms joined together and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: We, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are thirsting for the Dharma. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> fulfill our wish and the wish of all beings.

body.text: [SaSū 22] atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāraḥ atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādyena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 22] Then at that moment the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat and extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition for the display of this smile?

body.text: [SaSū 23] atha khalu bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ āmantrayāmāsa / ye sarvaśūra sattvā ihāgatvā te sarve anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyante / sarve te tathāgatagocarapariniṣpattaye pariniṣpadyante /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 23] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: Those beings, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who have come here — they will all fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening). They will all attain the perfection of the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: [SaSū 24] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ yadete sattvā ihagatvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhyante bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu sarvaśūra yastvaṃ tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / tena hi sarvaśūra śṛṇu / iha sarvaśura pariṇāmanaviśeṣo draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 24] The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition by which these beings, having come here, will fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening)? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Excellent, excellent, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that you consider this matter worthy of asking the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, listen! Here, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the distinction of dedication is to be observed.

body.text: [SaSū 25] bhūtapūrvaṃ sarvaśūrātīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairyadāpi tena kālena tena samayena ratnaśrīrnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loko udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 25] Formerly, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, in a past age, innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) ago, at that time, at that moment, there appeared in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaśrī</s> (Jewel Splendor), an <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, a charioteer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: [SaSū 26] tena khalu punaḥ sarvaśūra kālenāhaṃ māṇāvako bhūvan ye sattvāḥ sāṃprataṃ mayā buddhajñāne pratiṣṭhapitāste sarve tena kālena tena samayena mṛgā abhūvan tena ca kālena tena samayenāhamevaṃ praṇidhānamakārṣīd ye kecin mṛgāḥ sāṃprataṃ duḥkhena paripīḍitāḥ ete sarve mama buddhakṣetra upapadyeran sarvāṃśca tānahaṃ buddhajñāne pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ te ca mṛgāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā evaṃ vācamabhāṣanta - evaṃ bhavatu; tena sarvaśūra kuśalamūlenaite sattvā ihagatvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 26] At that time, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I was a young student. Those beings whom I have now established in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — they were all deer at that time, at that moment. And at that time, at that moment, I made this aspiration: 'May all those deer who are now afflicted by suffering be reborn in my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), and may I establish them all in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' And those deer, having heard those words, spoke thus: 'So may it be!' By that root of merit, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings, having come here, will fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening).

body.text: [SaSū 27] atha khalu sarvaśuro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavato 'ntikāttadutsāhaṃ śrutvā bhagavantametadavocat - kiyantaṃ bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavān āha / caturaśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi teṣāṃ sattvānāmāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 27] Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having heard that account of enthusiasm from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: How long, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, will be the lifespan of those beings? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) will be the measure of the lifespan of those beings.

body.text: [SaSū 28] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - kiyantaṃ bhagavan kalpasya pramāṇaṃ / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu kulaputra / tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūra kaścideva puruṣo nagaraṃ kārayeddvādaśayojanāyāmavistāraṃ ūrdhvena trīṇi yojanāni pramāṇaṃ / tacca nagaraṃ tilaphalakaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ kuryāt (sa ca puruṣa śirajīvī syāt) atha sa puruṣo varṣaśatasyātyayāttatastilaphalakaiḥ paripūrṇānnagarād ekaṃ tilaphalakaṃ bahirnikṣipedanena paryāyeṇa sa puruṣaḥ sarvāṇi tāni tilaphalakāni kṣayaṃ kuryāt paryavadānaṃ kuryāt tacca nagaramamūlamapratiṣṭhānāṃ bhavenna cādyāpi ca kalpaṃ kṣīyeta //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 28] The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: How long, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the measure of a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon)? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Listen, O son of noble family. Suppose, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, a certain man were to build a city twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth, and three <s>yojanas</s> in height. And he were to fill that city completely with sesame seeds. And suppose that man were long-lived. Then, after every hundred years, that man were to cast out one sesame seed from that city filled with sesame seeds. By this method, that man would exhaust all those sesame seeds, bring them to an end, and that city would become empty and without foundation — yet even then, the <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) would not be exhausted.

body.text: [SaSū 29] punaraparaṃ sarvaśūra (aparāṃ te upamā kariṣyāmyasyaivārthasya prasiddhaye /) tadyathāpi nāma parvato bhavet paṃcaviṃśad yojanāni pramāṇena dvādaśa yojanānyūrdhvena / atha kaścideva puruṣastasya parvatasya pārśve gṛhaṃ kārayet sa dīrghasyādhvano varṣaśatasyātyayena kāśikena vastreṇaikavārā parimārjayedevaṃ kṛtvā tasya parvatasya kṣayo bhavenna ca kalpaṃ kṣīyeta / etatsarvaśūra kalpasya pramāṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 29] Furthermore, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I shall give you another simile for the understanding of this very meaning. Suppose there were a mountain, twenty-five <s>yojanas</s> in extent and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in height. And suppose a certain man were to build a house at the side of that mountain, and after every hundred years of a long passage of time, he were to wipe it once with a cloth from <s>Kāśī</s> (Varanasi). By doing so, that mountain would be worn away, yet the <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) would not be exhausted. Such, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is the measure of a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon).

body.text: [SaSū 30] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād (ekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya) bhagavantametadavocat - ekapariṇāmanayā bhagavannevaṃ bahu puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / yadutāśītiḥ kalpān sukhamāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / kaḥ punarvādo yastathāgataśāsane bahutaramadhikāraṃ kariṣyati / tasya kiyantamāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 30] Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: By a single dedication, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, one generates such a great merit-aggregate — namely, that one's lifespan will be eighty <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) of happiness. What then of one who will undertake greater service in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? How long will that one's lifespan be?

body.text: [SaSū 31] bhagavān āha - śṛṇu kulaputra ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ śroṣyati / tasya caturaśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / kaḥ punarvādo yaḥ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ likhāpayiṣyati vācayiṣyati / sa sarvaśūraḥ sattvo bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati / yaḥ sarvaśūra prasannacittaḥ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtramadhyāśayena namaskariṣyati sa paṃcanavati kalpāṃ jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati / ṣaṣṭi kalpasahasrāṇi rājā cakravartī bhaviṣyati / dṛṣṭeva dharme sarvaśūra sarveṣāṃ priyo bhaviṣyati manāpaḥ na sa sarvaśūra śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati / priyo bhaviṣyati manāpaḥ na sa sarvaśūra śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati / na viṣeṇa (nodakena nāgnau) kālaṃ kariṣyati / kākhordaṃ cāsya na kramiṣyati / maraṇakālasamaye carimanirodhe vartamāne navati buddhākoṭyaḥ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati / te ca sarvaśūra buddhā bhagavanta āśvāsayanti / mā bhaiḥ satpuruṣa tvayā saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ mahādharmaparyāyaṃ subhāṣitaṃ śrutaṃ śrutvā iyān puṇyaskandhaḥ prasūtaḥ teṣāṃ paṃcanavati buddhakoṭyaḥ pṛthak pṛthag lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavanto vyākariṣyanti / kaḥ punarvādaḥ sarvaśūra ya imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ mahādharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāptaṃ vistareṇa śroṣyati / (lekhayiṣyati vācayiṣyati bhāvayiṣyati //)//
body.translated_text: [SaSū 31] The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Listen, O son of noble family. Whoever will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, that person's lifespan will be eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). What then of one who will have the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> written down and recited? That being, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will generate even more merit. Whoever, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, with a clear mind and sincere intention pays homage to the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, that person will remember their past lives for ninety-five <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), birth after birth. For sixty thousand <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) that person will be a <s>Cakravartī</s> (wheel-turning monarch). In this very life, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that person will be dear and pleasing to all. That person, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will not die by weapons, will not die by poison, nor by water, nor by fire. No malicious sorcery will affect that person. At the time of death, when the final cessation is at hand, that person will see ninety <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s> face to face. And those <s>Buddhas</s>, those <s>Bhagavāns</s>, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will reassure that person: 'Fear not, O virtuous one! You have heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, the great discourse of the Dharma, well spoken. Having heard it, this much merit has been generated.' Those ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>, those <s>Bhagavāns</s>, in their respective world-realms, will each give prophecies of awakening. What then, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of one who will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, the great discourse of the Dharma, complete in its entirety in full detail, and will have it written down, recited, and cultivated?

body.text: [SaSū 32] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ahaṃ bhagavan saṃghāṭasūtraṃ mahādharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyāmi / kiyantaṃ (ahaṃ) bhagavan puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyāmi / bhagavānāha - yāvanto gaṃgānadībālikāsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ (satkāraṃ kṛtvā) puṇyaskandhastāvantaṃ sarvaśūra sa sattvaḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 32] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I, Blessed One, will hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, the great <s>dharma-paryāya</s>. How great an aggregate of merit, Blessed One, will I generate?' The Blessed One said: 'The aggregate of merit equal to [venerating] <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—so great, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, an aggregate of merit will that being generate.'

body.text: [SaSū 33] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - yadahaṃ bhagavan saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇomi nāhaṃ bhagavaṃstṛptiṃ saṃjānāmi / bhagavān āha - sādhu sādhu sarvaśūra yastvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ tṛptiṃ na saṃjānāni / ahamapi sarvaśūra dharmāṇāṃ tṛptiṃ na saṃjānāmi / kaḥ punarvādaḥ sarvaśūra yad bālapṛthagjanāstṛptiṃ jñāsyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 33] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'When I, Blessed One, hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s>, I do not feel satiated, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that you do not feel satiated with the <s>Dharma</s>. I too, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, do not feel satiated with the <s>Dharma</s>. What then to say, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that foolish ordinary beings will know satiation?'

body.text: [SaSū 34] yaḥ kaścit sarvaśūra kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā mahāyāne prasādaṃ janayiṣyanti / sa kalpasahasraṃ vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati / paṃca kalpasahasrāṇi tiryakṣurnopapatsyate / dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi durbuddhiṃ sa bhavisyati / aṣṭādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi pratyantime janapade nopapatsyate / viṃśati kalpasahasrāṇi pradānaśūro bhaviṣyati / paṃcaviṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi devaloke upapatsyate / paṃcatriṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyati / sa catvāriṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi niṣkrāntagṛhāvāso bhaviṣyati / paṃcāśat kalpasahasrāṇi dharmadharo bhaviṣyati / paṃcaṣaṣṭiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi maraṇānusmṛtiṃ bhāvayiṣyati / tasya sarvaśūra kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā na kiṃcit pāpakāni karmāṇi saṃvetsyante / na ca tasya māraḥ pāpīmānavatāraṃ lapsyate / na jātu mātukukṣāvupapatsyate / ye sarvaśūra imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / te yatra yatropapatsyante tatra tatra paṃcanavatyāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairvinipātaṃ na gamiṣyanti / aśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi śrutadharā bhaviṣyanti / kalpaśatasahasraṃ prāṇātipātāt prativiratā bhaviṣyanti navānavati kalpasahasrāṇi mṛṣāvādāt prativiratā bhaviṣyanti / trayodaśa kalpasahasrāṇi piśunavacanāt prativiratā bhaviṣyanti / durlabhāste sarvaśūra sattvā ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 34] 'Whoever, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family, will generate faith in <s>Mahāyāna</s>—for a thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will not fall into the lower realms. For five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will not be reborn as an animal. For twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will not be of poor intelligence. For eighteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will not be reborn in a border region. For twenty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be heroes in giving. For twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn in the god realms. For thirty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). For forty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be renouncers of household life. For fifty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>. For sixty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will cultivate the recollection of death. For that son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, no evil <s>karmas</s> will take effect. Nor will <s>Māra</s> the Evil One find an opening in them. They will never again be born from a mother's womb. Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, wherever they are reborn, in all those places, for ninety-five incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, they will not fall into the lower realms. For eighty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be retainers of what they have heard. For a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be restrained from taking life. For ninety-nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be restrained from false speech. For thirteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be restrained from divisive speech. Rare, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are those beings who will hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 35] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat - kiyantaṃ bhagavaṃ(ste sattvā) apuṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati / ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ pratikṣepsyanti / bhagavānāha - bahu sarvaśūra saddharmapratikṣepādapuṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 35] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'How great an aggregate of demerit, Blessed One, will (those beings) generate who will reject this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Great, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is the aggregate of demerit that will be generated from the rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 36] sarvaśūra āha - kiyantaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ pāpakaṃ karmaskandhaṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha - alamalaṃ sarvaśūra mā me pāpakaṃ karmaskandhaṃ paripṛcchaḥ api tu sarvaśūra śṛṇu nirdekṣyāmi teṣāṃ saddharmapratikṣepakānāṃ pāpakaṃ akuśalaskandhaṃ / yāvantaṃ te pāpakamakuśalaskandhaṃ pratigṛhīṣyanti / ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ pratikṣipanti / yaśca sarvaśūra dvādaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamānān tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike duṣṭacittamutpādayedyaścemaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ pratikṣipedayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ pāpakam (kuśalaskandha prādurbhaviṣyati / ataḥ sarvaśūra-m-) akuśalaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti / ataste sarvaśūra saddharmapratikṣepakā sattvāḥ bahutaramakuśalaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti ye mahāyāne āghātacittamutpādayiṣyanti / dagdhāste sarvaśūra sattvā dagdhā eva /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 36] <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'How great, Blessed One, will be the aggregate of evil <s>karma</s> of those beings?' The Blessed One said: 'Enough, enough, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Do not ask me about the aggregate of evil <s>karma</s>. But listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I shall explain the evil, unwholesome aggregate of those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>. As great as the evil, unwholesome aggregate they will receive who reject this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>—if, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, someone were to generate a hostile mind toward <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, and someone else were to reject this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>—this [latter person] would generate a far greater aggregate of evil (unwholesome) [karma] than that. Therefore, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings who reject the true <s>Dharma</s> will generate a far greater aggregate of unwholesome [karma]—those who will generate a hostile mind toward <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Burned, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are those beings—burned indeed!'

body.text: [SaSū 37] sarvaśūra āha - na te bhagavan sattvā śakyaṃ mocayituṃ / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu sarvaśūra; na śakyā mocayituṃ tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūra kaścideva puruṣaḥ kasyacit sattvasya śīrṣaṃcchiṃdyād atha sa puruṣaḥ kenacid bhaiṣajyena praliṃpena mākṣikena vā śarkarayā vā / guḍena vā ghṛtena vā tailena vā taṃ śīrṣaṃ pralepayet tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra śakyaṃ sa sattvaḥ punarapyutthāpayituṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 37] <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Those beings, Blessed One, cannot be saved.' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: they cannot be saved. It is just as if, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, a certain man were to cut off the head of a certain being, and then that man were to anoint that head with some medicine, or honey, or sugar, or molasses, or ghee, or oil. What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>—could that being be made to rise again?'

body.text: [SaSū 38] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - na śakyaṃ bhagavan na śakyaṃ sugata / bhagavān āha - (evameva sarvaśūra na śakya[ṃ]te sa sattvo mocayituṃ bahubhirupāyairyo mahāyānasyāgh[āta]cittam [u]t[p]ādayiti //)//
body.translated_text: [SaSū 38] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'It is not possible, Blessed One; it is not possible, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: '(Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that being cannot be saved by many means—one who generates a hostile mind toward <s>Mahāyāna</s>.)'

body.text: [SaSū 39]punaraparaṃ sarvaśūra / tadyathāpi nāma dvitīyaḥ puruṣo bhavet sa tīkṣṇena śastreṇāparasya sattvasya prahāraṃ dadyāt sa na śaknuyādekaprahāreṇa jīvitādvyavaropayituṃ / kiṃ cāpi sarvaśūra braṇamutpadyeta / atha ca punarbhaiṣajyayogaṃ kartavyaṃ tadā braṇāt parimucyate / yadā parimukto bhavati tadā duḥkhaṃ smarati / ahamidānīñjānāmi na kadācit punaḥ pāpakamakuśalaṃ karmābhisaṃskāraṃ kariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 39] Furthermore, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: it is just as if a second man were to strike another being with a sharp weapon. He might not be able to deprive him of life with a single blow. But, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, a wound would arise. And then, by the application of medicine, he would be freed from the wound. When he is freed, he would remember the suffering [and think]: 'Now I know—never again will I create evil, unwholesome <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 40] evameva sarvaśūra sa saddharmapratikṣepakaḥ puruṣo yadā narake duḥkhaṃ smarati tadā sarvapāpaṃ parivarjayati / yadā sarvapāpaṃ parivarjayati / tadā sarvadharmā āmukhīkariṣyati (yadā) sarvadharmā āmukhīkṛtvā (tadā) sarvakuśaladharmapāripūriṅ kariṣyati / tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūra mṛtasya puruṣasya mātāpitarau śocanti paridevanti na ca śaknuvanti trātumevameva sarvaśūra bālapṛthagjanāḥ sattvā na śaknuvantyātmahitaṃ parahitaṃ vā kartuṃ nirāśā iva mātāpitara gatā iti / evameva sarvaśūra nirāśā bhavanti te sattvā maraṇakālasamaye /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 40] Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, that man who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>, when he remembers the suffering in hell, then he avoids all evil. When he avoids all evil, then he turns to face all <s>dharmas</s>. When he has turned to face all <s>dharmas</s>, then he will accomplish the fulfillment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. It is just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the mother and father of a dead man grieve and lament but are unable to rescue him—just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, foolish ordinary beings are unable to accomplish their own welfare or the welfare of others; they are like hopeless parents who have departed. Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings become hopeless at the time of death.

body.text: [SaSū 41] dvāvimau sarvaśūra sattvānāṃ nairāśyau maraṇakālasamaye / katamau dvau / yadutaikaḥ sattvaḥ pāpaṃ karma karoti kārāpayati vā / dvitīyaḥ sarvaśūra saddharmaṃ pratikṣipati / imau dvau sattvānāṃ nairāśyau maraṇakālasamaye /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 41] There are these two [causes of] hopelessness for beings at the time of death, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>. What are the two? First, a being who commits evil <s>karma</s> or causes it to be committed. Second, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, one who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. These are the two [causes of] hopelessness for beings at the time of death.

body.text: [SaSū 42] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - kā bhadanta bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ gatiḥ ko 'bhisaṃparāyo bhavati / bhagavānāha - anantā gatiḥ sarvaśūra saddharmapratikṣepakānāṃ sattvānāṃ ananto 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ kalpameva te sarvaśūra raurave mahānarake duḥkhaṃ vedanāṃ vedayiṣyanti / kalpaṃ saṃghāte / kalpaṃ tapane kalpaṃ pratāpane / kalpaṃ kālasūtre mahānarake / kalpaṃ mahāvīcau mahānarake / kalpaṃ romaharṣe mahānarake / kalpaṃ hahe mahānarake / (kalpaṃ tapane mahānarake) imeṣvaṣṭasu mahānarakeṣu sarvaśūra aṣṭau kalpāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakaiḥ sattvairduḥkhamanubhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 42] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'What, venerable Blessed One, is the destiny of those beings, and what is their future state?' The Blessed One said: 'Endless is the destiny, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of beings who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>; endless is their future state. For an entire <s>kalpa</s>, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, they will experience painful sensations in the <s>Raurava</s> great hell. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Saṃghāta</s>. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Tapana</s>. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Pratāpana</s>. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Kālasūtra</s> great hell. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Mahāvīci</s> great hell. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Romaharṣa</s> great hell. For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Haha</s> great hell. (For a <s>kalpa</s> in <s>Tapana</s> great hell.) In these eight great hells, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, eight <s>kalpas</s> of suffering must be endured by beings who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 43]atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - duḥkhaṃ bhagavan duḥkhaṃ sugata notsahāmi śrotuṃ / atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣataḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 43] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'How painful, Blessed One! How painful, <s>Sugata</s>! I cannot bear to hear [more].' Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

body.text:
(1) yastvaṃ notsahase śrotumidaṃ vākyaṃ mahābhayam
narake yathaikāntaduḥkhe sattvā vindanti vedanāṃ
(2) yat karoti śubhaṃ karmaṃ sukhaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati /
yatkarotyaśubhaṃ karma duḥkhameva bhaviṣyati /
(3) jātasya maraṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ śokaṃ duḥkho 'tha bandhanaṃ
nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi bālasya sukhaheto na vetti yaḥ
(4) paṇḍitānāṃ sukhaṃ yo vai smarate buddhamuttamam
prasannāśca mahāyāne na te yāsyanti durgatim
(5) evameva sarvaśūra pūrvakarma pracoditaṃ /
alpaṃ hi kṛyate karma anantaṃ bhujyate phalaṃ /
(6) bījamalpaṃ yathā vāpya prabhūtaṃ labhate phalaṃ
buddhakṣetra tu sukṣetre uptādbījādmahāphalaṃ
(7) paṇḍitānāṃ sukhaṃ bhavati ramante jinaśāsane /
vivarjayanti pāpāni kurvanti kuśalaṃ bahu;
(8) vālamātraṃ pradāsyanti ye dānaṃ mama śāsane /

children.translated_text: for eighty thousand <s>kalpas</s> (eons) [they will be] of great enjoyment and great wealth.

children.text: (9) yatra yatropapadyante nityaṃ dānaṃ smaranti te /
children.translated_text: (9) Wherever they are reborn, they always remember giving.
Thus this is of great fruit — the profound offering to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text:
(1) You who cannot bear to hear this fearsome speech — how beings experience suffering in hell, the exclusive abode of suffering:
(2) Whoever performs wholesome <s>karma</s>, happiness will come to them; whoever performs unwholesome <s>karma</s>, only suffering will come.
(3) For one who is born, death is suffering, grief is suffering, and bondage — always is suffering for the fool who does not know the cause of happiness.
(4) The happiness of the wise: whoever remembers the supreme <s>Buddha</s>, and those who have faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — they will not go to unfortunate destinies.
(5) Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, impelled by former <s>karma</s> — a small <s>karma</s> is performed, yet the fruit experienced is infinite.
(6) Just as, having sown a small seed, one obtains abundant fruit — in the excellent field of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), from seed sown, great is the fruit.
(7) There is happiness for the wise; they delight in the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror); they abandon sins and perform much wholesome [action].
(8) Those who will give even a hair's measure of giving in my teaching —

body.text: [SaSū 44] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan bhagavataḥ śāsane dharmo jñātavyaḥ kathaṃ bhagavan saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā kuśalamūlaṃ parigṛhītaṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavān āha - yaḥ sarvaśūra dvādaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān sarvasukhopadhānairupatiṣṭheta / yaścemaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇuyādevameva tasya puṇyaskandho jñātavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 44] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'How, Blessed One, should the <s>Dharma</s> be known in the teaching of the Blessed One? How, Blessed One, will the wholesome root be grasped upon hearing the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Whoever, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, were to attend upon <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, with all provisions of comfort — and whoever hears this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> — the aggregate of merit of the latter should be known as equal [to the former].'

body.text: [SaSū 45] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - kathaṃ bhagavan kuśalamūlaparipūriḥ kartavyāḥ evamukte bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - yat sarvaśūra kuśalamūlaṃ tat tathāgatasamaṃ jñātavyaṃ sarvaśūra āha - katamacca bhagavan kuśalamūlaṃ tathāgatasamaṃ jñātavyaṃ / bhagavān āha - dharmabhāṇakaḥ sarvaśūra tathāgatasamo jñātavyaḥ sarvaśūra āha - katamo bhagavan dharmabhāṇakaḥ bhagavān āha - yaḥ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ śrāvayati sa dharmabhāṇakaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 45] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'How, Blessed One, should the fulfillment of wholesome roots be accomplished?' When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: 'That which, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is a wholesome root — that should be known as equal to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'And which, Blessed One, is the wholesome root to be known as equal to the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'A <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of Dharma), <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, should be known as equal to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Which, Blessed One, is the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'One who causes others to hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> — that is the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 46] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - ye bhagavan saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / te īdṛśaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti / kaḥ punarvādo ye likhiṣyanti (svayaṃ vā likhiṣyanti) vācayiṣyanti / kiyantaṃ te bhagavan puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu sarvaśūra / tadyathā caturṣu dikṣvekaikasyān diśi dvādaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamāṃstathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā dvādaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamān kalpān avatiṣṭhanto dharmaṃ deśayeyurasya saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya puṇyaskandhaṃ varṇayeyurlekhayatastasya puṇyaskandhasya na śakyaṃ paryantamadhigantuṃ vācayā vā vyāhartuṃ / aṣṭācatvāriṅśadbhirapi gaṃgānādibālikāsamairbuddhairbhagavadbhirna śakyaṃ likhyamānasya yatpuṇyaskandhaṃ tadvyāhartuṃ kaḥ punarvādo ye vācayiṣyanti cintayiṣyanti vā ye vā dharmadhyānā bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 46] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Those, Blessed One, who will hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> — they will generate such an aggregate of merit. How much more so those who will copy it (or will copy it themselves) [and] recite it! How great, Blessed One, an aggregate of merit will they generate?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Suppose that in the four directions, in each direction, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, were to remain for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> and praising the aggregate of merit of this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> — [even then] one could not reach the limit of the aggregate of merit of one who copies it, nor express it in speech. Even forty-eight [times as many] <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, could not express the aggregate of merit of one who copies it. How much more so those who will recite it, contemplate it, or engage in <s>dharma-dhyāna</s> (meditation on the Dharma)!'

body.text: [SaSū 47] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - kiyantaṃ bhagavan vācayamānāḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti // atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣatāḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 47] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'How great an aggregate of merit will those who recite it generate?' Then at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:

body.text:
(10) catuṣpadāyāṃ gāthāyāṃ vācitāyāṃ tu yacchubhaṃ /
caturaśīti gaṃgāyā bālikā syuḥ samā jināḥ
(11) te vācitasyeha yatpuṇyaṃ kathayeyuraviṣṭhitāḥ
na ca kṣīyeta tatpuṇyaṃ yāvad vyākaraṇaṃ bhavet
(12) buddhānāṃ koṭayo 'śītistiṣṭheyuḥ kalpatāttakān
mahāyānaguṇāḥ sarve varṇayeyurdaśo diśaḥ
(13) saṃghāṭasya ca yatpuṇyaṃ tat kṣayaṃ naiva ca vrajet
buddhānān durlabhā evamanantā dharmadeśanāḥ
body.translated_text:
(10) When a single verse of four lines is recited, the merit thereof — even if <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) as numerous as the sands of eighty-four <s>Gaṅgās</s>
(11) were to speak unceasingly of the merit of the one who recites, that merit would not be exhausted until the prophecy [of Buddhahood] is given.
(12) Eighty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s> might remain for <s>kalpas</s> as many as stars, praising all the virtues of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in the ten directions —
(13) yet the merit of the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> would never reach exhaustion. Thus, the <s>Dharma</s> teachings of the <s>Buddhas</s> are indeed rare and infinite.

body.text: [SaSū 48] tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena caturaśītirdevaputrakoṭiśatasahasrāṇi yena tathāgato yena ca saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyanirdeśaṃ tenāṃñjalayaḥ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocan - sādhu sādhu bhagavan yena bhagavatā īdṛśaṃ dharmanidhānaṃ jaṃbudvīpe sthāpitaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 48] Then at that time, at that moment, eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), approaching the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the place where the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> was being expounded, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! The Blessed One has established such a treasury of <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>!'

body.text: (49) anye cāṣṭādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi nigranthānāṃ yena bhagavāmstenopasaṃkrāmanupasaṃkramya bhagavantamevamāhuḥ jaya bhoḥ śramaṇo gautama; bhagavānāha - tathāgato nityameva jayati / bho nigranthatīrthikāḥ kathaṃ yuṣmākaṃ tīrthikānāṃ jayaṃ te 'vocan jayatu jayatveva śramaṇo gautama; bhagavānāha - nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ jayaṃ paśyāmi / āha ca -
body.translated_text: (49) And another eighteen <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain ascetics) approached the Blessed One, and having approached, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Victory, O <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is always victorious. O <s>Nirgrantha</s> sectarians, how is victory for your sect?' They said: 'Victory, indeed victory to <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'I do not see your victory.' And he said:

body.text: (14) viparītā sthitā yūyaṃ bhaviṣyati jayaḥ kathaṃ

children.text: yūyaṃ śṛṇutha nigranthā vakṣyāmi bhavatāṃ hitaṃ
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Nirgranthas</s>, I will speak for your benefit:

children.text: (15) bālabuddheḥ sukhaṃ nāsti kiṃ jayaṃ vo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: (15) For one of foolish understanding there is no happiness — how will there be victory for you?
I will show the profound path through the eye of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: (14) You stand in error — how will there be victory?

body.text: [SaSū 50] atha te nigranthā bhagavato 'ntike kruddhā aprasādacittamutpādayāmāsuḥ tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena śakro devānāmindro (tasyāṃ parṣadiḥ sannipatito bhūt sanniṣaṇṇaḥ sa tānanyatīrthikānigranthāṃ bhagavato 'ntike kruddhānabhivīkṣya) vajraṃ parāhanat
body.translated_text: [SaSū 50] Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s> became angry toward the Blessed One and generated a mind of displeasure. Then at that time, at that moment, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, (who was present in that assembly, seated [there], seeing those heterodox <s>Nirgranthas</s> angry toward the Blessed One,) struck his <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt).

body.text:
[SaSū 51] atha te 'ṣṭādaśa koṭyo nigranthānāṃ bhītāstrastā mahātā duḥkhadaurmanasyenārtā asrukaṇṭhā paridevanti / tathāgataśca svakamātmānamantardhitaṃ darśayati sma /
atha te nigranthā asrumukhā rudanti tathāgataṃ apaśyantaśca gāthāṃ babhāṣire /
body.translated_text:
[SaSū 51] Then those eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nirgranthas</s>, frightened, terrified, afflicted with great suffering and mental anguish, with tears in their throats, lamented. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> made his own body disappear from sight.
Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s>, with tearful faces, weeping, not seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, spoke this verse:

body.text:
(16) nāsti kaścidiha trāṇāṃ na mātā na pitā tathā /
atavīmiha paśyāma śūnyāgārāṃ nirālayāṃ /
(17) udakaṃ caiva naivāsti na vṛkṣā na ca pakṣīṇāḥ

children.text: janaṃ cātra na paśyāma anāthā duḥkhavedanāṃ
children.translated_text: we see no person [here]; helpless, we experience suffering.
(18) We experience great terror, not seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

children.text: (ko nu syāccharaṇaṃ nātho yena trāyena mahābhayāt //)//
children.translated_text: (Who could be a refuge, a protector, by whom we might be saved from this great fear?)

body.text: [SaSū 52] tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena te 'ṣṭādaśa koṭyo nigranthānāṃ utthāyāyanebhyo jānudvayaṃ bhūmau nipātya śabdamudīrayanti ghoṣamanuśrāvayanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 52] Then at that time, at that moment, those eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nirgranthas</s>, rising from their seats, placing both knees on the ground, raised their voices and cried out:

body.text:
(19) tathāgataḥ kāruṇikaḥ saṃbuddhi dbipadottamaḥ
kuruṣva hitamasmākaṃ trāyasva kṛpaṇaṃ jagat
body.translated_text:
(19) The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the compassionate one, the Perfectly Awakened, the best of bipeds —
act for our benefit, save this wretched world!

body.text: [SaSū 53] atha bhagavān smitaṃ prāduṣkṛtvā sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati / gaccha sarvaśūra nigranthānāmanyatīrthikānān dharman deśaya / evamukte sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - nanu bhagavan kālaparvatāḥ sumeroḥ parvatarājasya śirasā praṇamanti / tiṣṭhati tathāgate 'haṃ dharman deśayāmi / bhagavān āha - alaṃ kulaputra bahu tathāgatānāmupāyakauśalyaṃ gaccha sarvaśūra vyavalokaya daśa diśi lokadhātūn paśya kva tathāgataṃ paśyasi / kutra vā tathāgatasyāsanaṃ prajñaptaṃ (paśyasi) / ahameva sarvaśūra svayaṃ nigranthānāṃ anyatīrthikānāṃ dharman deśayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 53] Then the Blessed One, displaying a smile, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: 'Go, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Nirgranthas</s> and other sectarians.' When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Surely, Blessed One, the <s>Kāla</s> mountains bow their heads before <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains! While the <s>Tathāgata</s> is present, shall I teach the <s>Dharma</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Enough, son of good family! Many are the skillful means of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Go, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, survey the world-realms in the ten directions; see where you see a <s>Tathāgata</s>, or where you see a seat prepared for a <s>Tathāgata</s>. I myself, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Nirgranthas</s> and other sectarians.'

body.text: [SaSū 54] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha - kasya bhadanta bhagavan ṛddhyānubhāvena gacchāmi / svaṛddhervā / atha vā tathāgatasya ṛddhyānubhāvena gacchāmi / bhagavān āha - svakena sarvaśūra ṛddhibalādhiṣṭhānena gacchaḥ punareva sarvaśūra tathāgatasya ṛddhyānubhāvenāgacchaḥ atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇikṛtya tatraivāntardhitaḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 54] The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'By whose miraculous power, venerable Blessed One, shall I go? By my own miraculous power? Or shall I go by the miraculous power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Go, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, by your own miraculous power and spiritual authority; but return again, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, by the miraculous power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, circumambulating the Blessed One, vanished right there.

body.text: [SaSū 55] atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ anyatīrthikānāṃ dharman deśayati / jātirmārṣā duḥkhaṃ jātireva duḥkhaṃ jātasya sato bahūni bhayānyutpadyante / jātasya vyādhibhayamutpadyate vyādherjarābhayamutpadyate / jīrṇasya mṛtyubhayamutpadyate / ta āhuḥ katamad bhagavāñjātasya bhayaṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 55] Then the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those non-Buddhist ascetics: 'Birth, O monks, is suffering. Birth itself is suffering. For one who is born, many fears arise. For one who is born, the fear of disease arises; from disease, the fear of old age arises. For one who is aged, the fear of death arises.' They said: 'What, Blessed One, is the fear for one who is born?'

body.text: [SaSū 56] bhagavān āha - jātaṃ jātamiti nāma / jātasya puruṣasya bahūni bhayāṇi jāyante rājabhayaṃ jāyate corabhayaṃ jāyate / agnibhayaṃ jāyate / viṣabhayaṃ jāyate / udakabhayaṃ jāyate / vāyubhayaṃ jāyate / āvartabhayaṃ jāyate / svakṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ bhayaṃ jāyate / evaṃ bhagavatā jātinidānaṃ bahuprakāraṃ dharman deśayataḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 56] The Blessed One said: 'Birth is called "birth." For a person who is born, many fears arise: fear of kings arises, fear of thieves arises, fear of fire arises, fear of poison arises, fear of water arises, fear of wind arises, fear of whirlpools arises, fear of one's own self-created <s>karmas</s> (actions) arises.' Thus the Blessed One, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> with birth as its cause in many ways —

body.text: [SaSū 57] tena kālena tena samayena teṣāmanyatīrthikānāṃ nigranthānāṃ (śrutvā) mahāsantrāso bhavadevaṃ cāhuḥ na bhūyo vayaṃ bhagavannutsahāmahe jatiduḥkhamanubhavituṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 57] at that time, at that moment, great terror arose in those non-Buddhist <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetics upon hearing [this], and they said thus: 'No longer, Blessed One, are we able to endure the suffering of birth!'

body.text: [SaSū 58] asmin khalu punaḥ saṃghāṭe dharmaparyāye bhagavatā bhāṣyamāṇe te 'ṣṭādaśa koṭyo nigranthā anyatīrthikāḥ pariniṣpannā abhūvannanuttarasyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ svakāye cāṣṭādaśa bodhisattvasahasrāḥ daśamahābhūmipratiṣṭhitāḥ / sarve nānārdhivikurvitāni (svakāyamanekaprakāraṃ) sandarśayāmāsuḥ tadyathā aśvarūpaṃ / hastirūpaṃ / siṃharūpaṃ vyāghrarūpaṃ garuḍarūpaṃ sumerurūpaṃ nandikarūpaṃ kecid vṛkṣarūpaṃ / te sarve padmāsane paryaṃkena niṣīdanti / nava koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvānāṃ bhagavato dakṣiṇe pārśve niṣīdanti / nava koṭīsahasrāṇi (bodhisattvānāṃ) bhagavato vāme pārśve niṣīdanti / tathāgatastu nityasamāhitaḥ upāyakauśalyena sattvānāṃ dharman deśayan saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 58] Moreover, when this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> (discourse on Dharma) was being spoken by the Blessed One, those eighteen <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Nirgrantha</s> non-Buddhist ascetics became fully accomplished in unsurpassed perfect awakening, and in their own bodies, eighteen thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> became established on the ten great <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). They all displayed various miraculous transformations [of their own bodies in many forms], such as: the form of a horse, the form of an elephant, the form of a lion, the form of a tiger, the form of a <s>Garuḍa</s>, the form of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the form of <s>Nandika</s>, and some the form of a tree. They all sat in the lotus posture cross-legged. Nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> sat on the right side of the Blessed One. Nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> sat on the left side of the Blessed One. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, however, being ever absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), appeared teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>).

body.text: [SaSū 59] yāvat saptame rātṛdivasena tathāgataḥ pāṇitalaṃ prasārayati / jānāti ca bhagavān yaḥ sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāḥ padmottarāyā lokadhātorihāgacchatīti / yadā ca sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gatastadā sapta rātrindivasaistāṃ padmottarāṃ lokadhātumanuprāptaḥ svaṛddhibalādhiṣṭhānena / yadā ca bhagavān bahuṃ prasārayati / tadā sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ purata sthitaḥ bhagavantaṃ saptakṛt pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādayamāno yena tathāgatastenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat -
body.translated_text: [SaSū 59] Then, on the seventh day-and-night, the <s>Tathāgata</s> extended his palm. And the Blessed One knew: 'The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> is coming here from that <s>Padmottarā</s> world-realm.' And when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> had gone, he reached that <s>Padmottarā</s> world-realm in seven day-and-nights by the power of his own miraculous ability (<s>ṛddhi</s>). And when the Blessed One extended [his hand], the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, standing before the Blessed One, having circumambulated the Blessed One seven times, generating faith in the presence of the Blessed One, joining his palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, spoke thus to the Blessed One:

body.text: [SaSū 60] gato 'smi bhagavan daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu dṛṣṭāni me bhagavan navānavati koṭīsahasrāṇi (lokadhātunāṃ / dṛṣṭāni ca me bhagavan navati koṭīsahasrāṇi) buddhakṣetrāṇāmekayā ṛddhyāḥ dvitīyayā ṛddhyā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ koṭīśatasahasraṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 60] 'I have gone, Blessed One, to all world-realms in the ten directions. I have seen, Blessed One, ninety-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> [of world-realms. And I have seen, Blessed One, ninety thousand <s>koṭis</s>] of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) by the first miraculous power, and by the second miraculous power, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of blessed <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 60] gato 'smi bhagavan daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu dṛṣṭāni me bhagavan navānavati koṭīsahasrāṇi (lokadhātunāṃ / dṛṣṭāni ca me bhagavan navati koṭīsahasrāṇi) buddhakṣetrāṇāmekayā ṛddhyāḥ dvitīyayā ṛddhyā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ koṭīśatasahasraṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 60] 'I have gone, Blessed One, to all world-realms in the ten directions. I have seen, Blessed One, ninety-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> [of world-realms. And I have seen, Blessed One, ninety thousand <s>koṭis</s>] of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) by the first miraculous power, and by the second miraculous power, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of blessed <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 61] yāvat saptame rātṛdivase tāṃ padmottarāṃ lokadhātumanuprāptaḥ atrāntaraṃ akṣobhyakoṭīsahasraṃ buddhakṣetrāṇāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tato 'haṃ teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmṛddhiṃ paśyāmi / dvānavatiṣu buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu tathāgatā dharman deśayanti / aśītiṣu koṭīśatasahasreṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tatraiva divase aśīti koṭīśatasahasrāṇi tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ loka utpannāni / sarvāṃśca tānahaṃ tathāgatān vanditvā punareva prakrāntaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 61] 'On the seventh day-and-night, I reached that <s>Padmottarā</s> world-realm. In the intervening [space], I saw a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Akṣobhya</s> <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>. Then I beheld the miraculous power of those blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. In ninety-two <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousand <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> were teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. In eighty <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, on that very day, eighty <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, arose in the world. And having venerated all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I proceeded onward.'

body.text: [SaSū 62] tatraiva divase bhagavannekonacatvāriṃśatsu buddhakṣetrakoṭīsahasrāṇyatikramya sarveṣu ca teṣvekūnacatvāriṃśatsu buddhakṣetrakoṭīsahasreṣvekūnacatvāriṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvānāṃ niṣkramya tatraiva divase 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ vanditāśca me bhagavan te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstṛguptaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ṛddhyā cāntardhitaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 62] 'On that very day, Blessed One, I traversed thirty-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>. And in all those thirty-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, thirty-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> had gone forth and, on that very day, had fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And I venerated those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, Blessed One, circumambulated them three times with reverence, and disappeared by miraculous power.'

body.text: [SaSū 63] ṣaṣṭikoṭiṣu bhagavan buddhakṣetreṣu buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyāmi / vanditāni ca me bhagavan tāni buddhakṣetrāṇi te ca buddhā bhagavantastataścāhaṃ prakrāntaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 63] 'In sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, Blessed One, I beheld blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. And I venerated those <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, Blessed One, and those blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, and from there I proceeded onward.'

body.text: [SaSū 64] anyeṣu ca bhagavan koṭīśateṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tathāgatāḥ parinirvāyamāṇān paśyāmi / vanditāśca me te tathāgatāstataścāhaṃ prakrāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 64] 'And in other <s>koṭi</s>-hundreds of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, Blessed One, I beheld <s>Tathāgatas</s> who were passing into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). And I venerated those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and from there I proceeded onward.'

body.text: [SaSū 65] dṛṣṭaṃ ca me bhagavannapareṣu paṃcanavatikoṭiṣu buddhakṣetreṣu saddharmamantardhāyantaṃ / cittāyāso me bhagavaṃstatra jātaḥ asrūṇi ca pramuṃcāmi / anyāṃśca rodamānān bahūn devanāgayakṣarākṣasān kāmarūpinaśca mahatā śokaśalyasamarpitān paśyāmi / evamaparaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ niravaśeṣaṃ dagdhaṃ sasamudraṃ sasumeruṃ sapṛthivīpradeśaṃ tamapi bhagavan vanditvā nirāśībhūtaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 65] 'And I saw, Blessed One, in yet other ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s> (sacred teaching) disappearing. Mental anguish arose in me there, Blessed One, and I shed tears. And I saw many others weeping — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and shape-shifters — pierced by great grief. Furthermore, [I saw] another <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> completely burnt, together with its oceans, together with its <s>Sumeru</s>, together with its regions of earth — and even that, Blessed One, having venerated it, I became free from expectation.'

body.text: [SaSū 66] prakrānto 'smi yāvadahaṃ bhagavan tāṃ padmottarāṃ lokadhātumanuprāptaḥ tasyāṃ ca bhagavan padmottarāyāṃ lokadhātau paṃca koṭīśatasahasrāṇyāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi / dakṣiṇasyān diśi koṭīśatasahasrāṇyāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi / vāmena pārśvena koṭīśatasahasramāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi / pūrvasyān diśi koṭīśatasahasramāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi / paścimāyān diśi koṭīśatasahasramāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi / ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi koṭīśatasahasramāsanānāṃ prajñaptān paśyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 66] 'I proceeded onward until, Blessed One, I reached that <s>Padmottarā</s> world-realm. And in that <s>Padmottarā</s> world-realm, Blessed One, I saw five <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of seats prepared. In the southern direction, I saw <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of seats prepared. On the left side, I saw a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand seats prepared. In the eastern direction, I saw a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand seats prepared. In the western direction, I saw a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand seats prepared. In the upward direction, I saw a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand seats prepared.'

body.text: [SaSū 67] sarvāṇi ca bhagavan tānyāsanāni saptaratnamayāni / sarveṣu ca teṣvāsaneṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā niṣaṇṇā dharman deśayanti / tatrāhaṃ bhagavannāścaryaprāptastāṃstathāgatān abhivandya paripṛcchāmi / kinnāmeyaṃ bhagavan lokadhātuḥ / te tathāgatā āhuḥ padmottarā nāmeyaṃ kulaputra lokadhātuḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 67] 'And all those seats, Blessed One, were made of the seven precious substances. And on all those seats, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones were seated, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. There, Blessed One, I was struck with wonder and, having venerated those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, I asked: "What is the name of this world-realm, Blessed One?" Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> said: "This world-realm, O son of good family, is called <s>Padmottarā</s>."'

body.text: [SaSū 68] tato 'haṃ bhagavaṃstān pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punarapi tāṃstathāgatān paripṛcchāmi - kinnāma iha buddhakṣetre tathāgataḥ te tathāgatā āhuḥ padmagarbho nāma kulaputra tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho ya iha buddhakṣetre buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / tatastān ahametadavocat - bahūni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi dṛśyante / tanna jānāmi katama sa padmagarbho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti / te tathāgatā āhuḥ vayan te kulaputra taṃ padmagarbhaṃ tathāgataṃ darśayiṣyāma / yaḥ sa padmagarbho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 68] 'Then, Blessed One, having circumambulated them, I again asked those <s>Tathāgatas</s>: "What is the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in this <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>?" Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> said: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Padmagarbha</s>, O son of good family, performs the work of a <s>Buddha</s> in this <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>." Then I said to them: "Many <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s> are seen. I do not know which one is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Padmagarbha</s>." Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> said: "We, O son of good family, shall show you that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmagarbha</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Padmagarbha</s>."'

body.text: [SaSū 69] atha tatkṣaṇādeva te sarve tathāgatakāyā antardhitāḥ sarve ca bodhisattvarūpāṇi sandṛśyante / ekameva tathāgataṃ paśyāmi / yathāhaṃ tasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya purataḥ sthitaḥ āsanaṃ ca prādurbhūtaṃ / sa ca māṃ tathāgata evamāha / niṣīda kulaputrātra āsane /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 69] 'Then, at that very instant, all those <s>Tathāgata</s>-bodies disappeared and all appeared in <s>Bodhisattva</s> forms. I saw only one <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then I, having venerated the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s> with my head, stood before him, and a seat appeared. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> spoke to me thus: "Sit here, O son of good family, on this seat."'

body.text: [SaSū 70] athāhaṃ tasminnāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ tadā ca bhagavannanekānyāsanāni prādurbhūtāni / na ca kaścit teṣvāsaneṣu niṣaṇṇaṃ paśyāmi / (tadahaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmi / na bhagava eṣvāsaneṣu ekaṃ api sattvaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ paśyāmi /) sa bhagavān māmevamāha / nākṛtakuśalamūlāḥ kulaputra sattvā eṣvāsaneṣu śaknuvanti niṣattum tamahaṃ taṃ tathāgatamidamavocat - kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan sattvāḥ kuśalamūlaṃ kṛtvā / eṣvāsaneṣu niṣīdanti / sa maṃ bhagavannevamāha / śṛṇu kulaputra ye sattvāḥ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / te tena kuśalamūlena eṣvāsaneṣu niṣatsyante / kaḥ punarvādo ye likhiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti / tvayā sarvaśūra saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutaṃ yastvamatrāsane niṣīdita / anyatra kastaveha buddhakṣetre 'bhyaṃntarapraveśaṃ dadyāt
body.translated_text: [SaSū 70] Then I sat upon that seat, and at that time, O Blessed One, many seats appeared, yet I did not see anyone seated upon those seats. (Then I asked the <s>Tathāgata</s>: "Blessed One, I do not see even a single being seated upon these seats.") That Blessed One spoke to me thus: "Son of good family, beings who have not created roots of merit are unable to sit upon these seats." I then said to that <s>Tathāgata</s>: "What kind of roots of merit, O Blessed One, must beings have created to sit upon these seats?" That Blessed One spoke to me thus: "Listen, son of good family — those beings who will hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>sūtra</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), by that root of merit they shall sit upon these seats. What need to speak of those who will write it down or recite it! O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, you have heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, therefore you are seated upon this seat. Who else besides you could be granted entry into this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field)?"

body.text: [SaSū 71] evamukte tena bhagavatā ahaṃ taṃ bhagavantametadavocat - kiyantaṃ bhagavan sa sattvaḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati / atha sa bhagavāṃ padmagarbhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ praduṣkārṣīt tadahaṃ bhagavan smitakāraṇaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ paripṛṣṭavān ko bhagavan hetuḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yat tathāgataḥ smitaṃ prāduṣkaroti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 71] When this was spoken, I said to that Blessed One: "How great a mass of merit, O Blessed One, will that being generate who hears this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>?" Then that Blessed One, <s>Padmagarbha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, at that moment displayed a smile. Then, O Blessed One, I asked that Blessed One about the cause of his smile: "What is the reason, O Blessed One, what is the cause, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> displays a smile?"

body.text: [SaSū 72] sa bhagavānāha / śṛṇu kulaputra sarvaśūraḥ (bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāsthāmaprāptaḥ) tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva rājā bhaveccakravarttī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ sa caturṣu dvīpakṣetreṣu tile vāpayet tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra bahūni tasya bījānyutpadyeran sarvaśūra āha / bahūni bhagavan bahūni sugata /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 72] That Blessed One said: "Listen, son of good family — (<s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>) — suppose, son of good family, there were a king, a <s>cakravartī</s> (universal monarch), lord of the four continents, and he were to sow sesame seeds across the four continental realms. What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — would many seeds be produced?" <s>Sarvaśūra</s> replied: "Many, O Blessed One! Many, O <s>Sugata</s>!"

body.text: [SaSū 73] sa bhagavānāha / tataḥ sarvaśūra kaścit sattvo bhaved yastāni tilaphalakānyekarāśiṃ kuryādanyatarāḥ puruṣastatastilaphalarāśercaikaṃ tilaphalakaṃ gṛhya dvitīye pārśve sthāpayet tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra śaknuyāt sa sattvastāni tilaphalakāni gaṇayituṃ vopamāṃ kartum sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha / no hīdaṃ bhagavan no hīdaṃ sugata; na śakyaṃ tāni tilaphalakāni gaṇayituṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 73] The Blessed One said: "Then, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, suppose some being were to gather all those sesame fruits into a single heap, and then another person were to take one sesame fruit from that heap and place it on a second side. What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — would that being be able to count those sesame fruits or make a comparison?" <s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied: "No indeed, O Blessed One! No indeed, O <s>Sugata</s>! It is not possible to count those sesame fruits."

body.text: [SaSū 74] bhagavān āha - evameva sarvaśūrāsya saṃghāṭasya dharmaparyāyasya yatpuṇyaskandhaṃ tanna śakyamanupamyaṃ kartumanyatra tathāgatena / tadyathā sarvaśūra yāvantaste tilaphalakāstāvāntastathāgatā bhaveyuḥ te sarve 'sya saṃghāṭasya dharmaparyāyasya śravaṇakuśalamūlapuṇyaṃ parikīrtayeyurna copamayāpi puṇyasya kṣayo bhavet kaḥ punarvādo yo likhiṣyati / vācayiṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 74] The Blessed One said: "Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the mass of merit of this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> cannot be compared by anyone other than a <s>Tathāgata</s>. That is to say, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, as many as those sesame fruits are, so many <s>Tathāgatas</s> there would be, and even if all of them were to proclaim the merit of the root of goodness from hearing this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, there would still be no exhaustion of the merit even by comparison. What need to speak of one who will write it down or recite it!"

body.text: [SaSū 75] sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha / kiyantaṃ bhagavan likhataḥ puṇyaṃ bhavati ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ likhayati / bhagavān āha / śṛṇu kulaputra / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva puruṣo bhaved yastrisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau tṛṇaṃ vā kāṣṭhaṃ vā taṃ sarvamaṃgulimātraṃcchindyāt
body.translated_text: [SaSū 75] <s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "How much merit, O Blessed One, accrues to one who writes this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>?" The Blessed One said: "Listen, son of good family. Suppose, son of good family, there were a person who, throughout the great trichiliocosm, were to cut all the grass and wood into pieces the size of a finger-joint —"

body.text: [SaSū 76] dvitīyāmupamāṃ śṛṇu sarvaśūra; tadyathāpi nāma yāvantastrisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau śilān vā prapātān vā mṛttikān vā paramāṇurajo vā te sarve rājānaścakravartino bhaveyuścaturdvīpeśvarāḥ saptaratnasamanvāgatāḥ tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra yasteṣāṃ tāvatāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ na śakyaṃ tasyopamāṃ kartuṃ sarvasattvairapi / sarvaśūro bodhisattva āha / na śakyaṃ bhagavannanyatra tathāgatāt
body.translated_text: [SaSū 76] "Hear a second simile, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>. Suppose that as many as all the stones, cliffs, clods of earth, and atoms of dust in the great trichiliocosm — all of those were to become <s>cakravartī</s> kings, lords of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures. What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — the mass of merit of that many <s>cakravartī</s> kings — could a comparison be made to it by all beings?" <s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied: "It is not possible, O Blessed One, except by a <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.text: [SaSū 77] bhagavān āhaivameva sarvaśūra na śakyaṃ saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya likhyamānasya puṇyaskandhopamāṃ kartumyāvantasteṣāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ puṇyamato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ya ito dharmaparyāyādekākṣaramapi likhitvā sthāpayedbahutaraṃ tasya puṇyaṃ vadāmi na tveva teṣāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 77] The Blessed One said: "Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, it is not possible to make a comparison to the mass of merit from writing the <s>Saṃghāṭasūtra</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. The merit of all those <s>cakravartī</s> kings — far greater merit than that does one generate who writes down even a single syllable from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> and preserves it. I declare that one's merit to be far greater, not at all equal to that of those <s>cakravartī</s> kings."
