body.text: [SaSū 78] evameva sarvaśūra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāyānasaddharmadhārakasya pratipattisthitasya yatpuṇyaṃ tanna śakyaṃ rājabhiścakravartibhirabhibhavituṃ evamevāsya saṃghāṭasya dharmaparyāyasya lekhanādyatpuṇyaṃ tanna śakyamupamāṃ kartuṃ / imaṃ sarvaśūra saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ puṇyanidhānāni darśayati / sarvakleśānupaśamayati / sarvadharmolkāṃ jvālayati / sarvamārān pāpīmataḥ parājayati / sarvabodhisattvabhavanānyujvālayati / sarvadharmanirhārānabhinirharati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 78] "Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the merit of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who upholds the <s>Saddharmā</s> (true Dharma) of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and abides in practice — that cannot be surpassed by <s>cakravartī</s> kings. In the same way, the merit from writing this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> cannot be compared. This <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>sūtra</s>, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, reveals the treasuries of merit, pacifies all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), kindles the torch of all <s>dharmas</s>, defeats all <s>Māras</s> the evil ones, illuminates the abodes of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and accomplishes the delivery of all <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: [SaSū 79] evamukte sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - iha bhagavan brahmacaryaṃ paramaduṣkaracaryāḥ tatkasya hetoḥ durlabhā bhagavaṃstathāgatacaryāḥ evameva durlabhā brahmacaryāḥ yadā ca brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyati / tadā tathāgataṃ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati / rātṛndivaṃ ca tathāgatadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / yadā ca tathāgataṃ paśyati tadā pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paśyati / yadā pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paśyati / tadā sarvadharmanidhānāni paśyati / yadā sarvadharmanidhānāni paśyati / tadāsya maraṇakālasamaye trāsaṃ notpadyate na sa jātu mātuḥ kukṣāvupapatsyate / na tasya jātu śoko bhaviṣyati / na ca tṛṣṇāpāśena baddho bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 79] When this was spoken, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> said to the Blessed One: "Here, O Blessed One, the holy life is a supremely difficult practice. For what reason? Because rare, O Blessed One, is the conduct of a <s>Tathāgata</s>. Just so, rare is the holy life. When one practices the holy life, then one will see the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face. Day and night there will be the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. When one sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>, then one sees the purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field). When one sees the purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, then one sees all the treasuries of the <s>Dharma</s>. When one sees all the treasuries of the <s>Dharma</s>, then at the time of death, no terror arises. Such a one will never be reborn in a mother's womb. For that one there will never be grief, nor will one be bound by the snare of craving."

body.text: [SaSū 80] evamukte bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra nanu durlabhastathāgatānamutpādaḥ āha / durlabho bhagavan durlabhaḥ sugata; bhagavān āha / evameva sarvaśūra durlabho yaṃ saṃghāto dharmaparyāyaḥ yeṣāṃ khalu punaḥ sarvaśūrāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotrāvabhāsamāgamiṣyati / so 'śītiḥ kalpāṃ jātyā jātismaro bhaviṣyati / ṣaṣṭi kalpasahasrāṇi cakravartirājyaṃ pratilapsyate / aṣṭau kalpasahasrāṇi śakratvaṃ pratilapsyate / paṃcaviṃśatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi śuddhāvāsakāyikānān devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyāṃ upapatsyate / aṣṭātṛṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi mahābrahmā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 80] When this was spoken, the Blessed One said to <s>Sarvaśūra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>: "What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — is not the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> rare?" He replied: "Rare, O Blessed One! Rare, O <s>Sugata</s>!" The Blessed One said: "Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rare is this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Moreover, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those for whom this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> shall reach the range of hearing — they shall remember their past births for eighty <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). For sixty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall obtain the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartī</s> king. For eight thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall obtain the lordship of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra). For twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be reborn in the company of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods (deities of the Pure Abodes). For thirty-eight thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be <s>Mahābrahmā</s>."

body.text: [SaSū 81] navānavatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati / kalpaśatasahasraṃ preteṣu nopapatsyate / aṣṭāviṃśati kalpasahasrāṇi tiryakṣurnopapatsyate / trayodaśa kalpasahasrāṇyasurakāyikeṣu nopapatsyate / na śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati (na viṣeṇa nāgninā na cāsya paropakramabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati) /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 81] For ninety-nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not fall into the lower realms. For a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts). For twenty-eight thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn as animals. For thirteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn among the <s>asuras</s>. They shall not meet death by weapons, (nor by poison, nor by fire, nor shall there be for them any fear of harm from others.)

body.text: [SaSū 82] paṃcaviṃśatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi na duṣprajño bhaviṣyati / sapta kalpasahasrāṇi prajñācarito bhaviṣyati / nava kalpasahasrāṇi prāsādiko bhaviṣyati / darśanīyaḥ yathā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya rūpakāyapariniṣpattistathā tasya bhaviṣyati / paṃcadaśa kalpasahasrāṇi na strībhāveṣūpapatsyate / ṣoḍaśa kalpasahasrāṇi vyādhiḥ kāye nākramiṣyati / paṃcatṛṃśatkalpasahasrāṇi divyacakṣurbhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 82] For twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be lacking in wisdom. For seven thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be one whose conduct is guided by wisdom. For nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be gracious and pleasing to behold — just as is the perfection of the form-body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, so shall theirs be. For fifteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in female form. For sixteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> no illness shall afflict their body. For thirty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall possess the divine eye.

body.text: [SaSū 83] ekonaviṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi nāgayoniṣu nopapatsyate / ṣaṭ kalpasahasrāṇi na krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati / sapta kalpasahasrāṇi daridrakuleṣu nopapatsyate / aśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi dvau dvīpau paribhuṃkte / yadā daridro bhavati tadā īdṛśaṃ sukhaṃ pratilapsyate / dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi andhayoniṣu nopapatsyate / trayodaśa kalpasahasrāṇi apāyeṣu nopapatsyate / ekādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi kṣāntivādī bhaviṣyati / maraṇakālasamaye carimavijñānanirodhe vartamāne na viparītasaṃjñī bhaviṣyati / na ca krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 83] For nineteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will not be reborn in <s>nāga</s> (serpent) wombs. For six thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will not be overcome by anger. For seven thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will not be reborn in destitute families. For eighty thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will enjoy two continents. Whenever one becomes poor, one will attain such happiness. For twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will not be reborn in blind wombs. For thirteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will not be reborn in the lower realms. For eleven thousand <s>kalpas</s> one will be an advocate of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience). At the time of death, when the final consciousness is ceasing, one will not have distorted perceptions. Nor will one be overcome by anger.

body.text: [SaSū 84] sa pūrvasyān diśi dvādaśa gaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhan drakṣyati / dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi viṃśatirbuddhakoṭī saṃmukhan drakṣyati / paścimasyān diśi paṃcaviṃśatirgaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati / uttarasyān diśi viṃśatirgaṃgānadībālukāsamān buddhāṃ bhagavataḥ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati / urdhvāyāṃ diśi navati koṭīsahasrāṇi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati / adhastāddiśi koṭīśataṃ gaṃgānadībālukāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhan drakṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 84] In the eastern direction, he will see face-to-face twelve <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. In the southern direction, he will see face-to-face twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. In the western direction, he will see face-to-face twenty-five <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. In the northern direction, he will see face-to-face twenty <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. In the upward direction, he will see face-to-face ninety thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. In the downward direction, he will see face-to-face a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river.

body.text: [SaSū 85] te ca sarve tathāgatāstaṃ kulaputramāśvāsayanti / mā bhaiḥ kulaputra tvayā saṃghāṭaṃ (sūtran) dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā iyantaḥ sāṃparāyikāni guṇānuśaṃsamukhāni ca bhaviṣyanti / paśyasi tvaṃ bhoḥ kulaputremānyanekāni gaṃgānadībālikāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi / āha / paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata / (bhagavān) āha / ete bhoḥ kulaputra tathāgatāstava sakāśamupasaṃkrāntā darśanāya / āha / kiṃ mayā kuśalakarma kṛtaṃ yeneme bahavastathāgatā āgatā /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 85] And all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> console that son of good family: 'Do not fear, son of good family! By having heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> (<s>sūtra</s>) <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, such future qualities and benefits will be yours. Do you see, dear son of good family, these many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river?' He said: 'I see them, Blessed One; I see them, <s>Sugata</s>.' (The Blessed One) said: 'These <s>Tathāgatas</s>, dear son of good family, have approached your presence to see you.' He said: 'What wholesome <s>karma</s> have I done that these many <s>Tathāgatas</s> have come?'

body.text: [SaSū 86] āha / śṛṇu kulaputra tvayā mānuṣyakamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhya saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrotrāvabhāsamāgataṃ / tena tvayā etāvat puṇyaskandhaṃ prasūtaṃ / (sarvaśūra) āha / yadi mama bhagavanna etāvān puṇyaskandhaḥ kaḥ punarvādo yaḥ sakalasamāptaṃ śroṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 86] He said: 'Listen, son of good family. By having obtained a human existence and having come within earshot of the <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, you have generated this great aggregate of merit.' (<s>Sarvaśūra</s>) said: 'If I, Blessed One, have this great an aggregate of merit, what then to say of one who will hear it in its entirety?'

body.text: [SaSū 87] (bhagavān) āhālaṃ bhoḥ kulaputra śṛṇu catuṣpadikāyā gāthāyā (śrutāyāḥ) puṇyaṃ varṇayāmi / tadyathā kulaputra trayodaśa gaṃgānadībālikāsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ yaḥ puṇyasakandhastato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / yaścatuṣpadikāmapi gāthāmito dharmaparyāyācchroṣyati / yaśca trayodaśa gaṃgānadībālukāsamāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān pūjayati / yaścetaḥ saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāṃ śroṣyati / ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati / kaḥ punarvādo yaḥ sakalasamāptaṃ śroṣyati / na tasya puṇyaskandhasya śakyamupamāṃ kartum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 87] (The Blessed One) said: 'Enough, dear son of good family. Listen—I shall describe the merit of (hearing) a single four-line verse. Son of good family, the aggregate of merit from [venerating] <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of thirteen <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers—one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that, whoever will hear even a four-line verse from this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>. And whoever worships <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of thirteen <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers—whoever will hear even a four-line verse from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, this one will generate a far greater aggregate of merit than that. What then to say of one who hears it in its entirety? No comparison can be made for that aggregate of merit.'

body.text: [SaSū 88] śṛṇu kulaputra yaścemaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ (nāma) sūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāptaṃ vistareṇa śroṣyati / yaśca sarvasyāṃ tṛsāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau tilaṃ vāpayedyāvantaste tilaphalakāstāvanto rājānaścakravartino bhaveyuratha kaścideva puruṣo bhavedāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ atha khalu sa puruṣasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ yathākāmikaṃ dānan dadyāt tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūrāpi tu sa puruṣastatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasaved āha / bahu bhagavan bahu sugata; bhagavān āha - yāvantaḥ kulaputra teṣāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ dānan dadataḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ yaścaikasya srotaāpannasya dānan dadyādayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 88] 'Listen, son of good family. Whoever will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> (<s>sūtra</s>) <s>dharma-paryāya</s> in its entirety in detail—and if someone were to sow sesame in the entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasrī</s> (billion-world) realm, and as many as those sesame fruits, so many <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) kings there would be, and then a certain man, wealthy, of great riches, of great enjoyment, were to give gifts to all those <s>cakravartin</s> kings as they desire—what do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, would that man generate much merit from that?' He said: 'Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Son of good family, as great as is the aggregate of merit of one giving gifts to those <s>cakravartin</s> kings—one who gives a gift to a single <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that.'

body.text: [SaSū 89] ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau sattvāste sarve srotaāpanā bhaveyusteṣāṃ sarverṣāṃ dānan dadato yatpuṇyaskandhaṃ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / ya ekasya sakṛdāgāmino dānan dadyād ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryām lokadhātau sattvāste sarve sakṛdāgāmino bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ ayan tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / ya ekasyānāgāmino dānān dadyād ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau sattvāste sarve nāgāmino bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasyārhato dānan dadyād ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau sattvāste sarve 'rhanto bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / ya ekasya pratyekabuddhasya dānan dadyād ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau sattvāste sarve pratyekabuddhā bhaveyusteṣān sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasya bodhisattvasya dānan dadyād ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau sattvāste sarve bodhisattvā bhaveyusteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / ya ekasya tathāgatasya cittaṃ prasādayed
body.translated_text: [SaSū 89] 'If all the beings in the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasrī</s> (billion-world) realm were all <s>srotaāpannas</s> (stream-enterers), the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this [hearer] generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who gives a gift to a single <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner). If all the beings in the billion-world realm were all <s>sakṛdāgāmins</s>, the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who gives a gift to a single <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner). If all the beings in the billion-world realm were all <s>anāgāmins</s>, the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who gives a gift to a single <s>arhat</s>. If all the beings in the billion-world realm were all <s>arhats</s>, the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who gives a gift to a single <s>pratyekabuddha</s>. If all the beings in the billion-world realm were all <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who gives a gift to a single <s>bodhisattva</s>. If all the beings in the billion-world realm were all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the aggregate of merit from giving gifts to all of them—this one generates a far greater aggregate of merit than that; one who generates faith in a single <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 90] yaśca trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau tathāgataparipūrṇāyāṃ cittaṃ prasādayed yaścemaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhiṣyati / kimaṃga punaḥ sarvaśūra ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati / śrutvā ca dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati / kaḥ punarvādaḥ sarvaśūra ya imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ cittaprasādena namaskariṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 90] 'And one who generates faith in a billion-world realm filled with <s>Tathāgatas</s>—and one who will write this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s>—how much more, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, one who will hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, and having heard it, will retain it, recite it, master it, and explain it in detail to others! What then to say, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of one who will pay homage to this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> with a mind of faith!'

body.text: [SaSū 91] tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra śakyamidaṃ sūtraṃ bālapṛthagjanaiḥ śrotuṃ āha / no hīdaṃ bhagavan āha / ye ca śroṣyanti na ca prasādamutpādayiṣyanti / śṛṇu sarvaśūra santi kecit sarvaśūra bālapṛthagjanāḥ sattvāḥ ye śaknuyurmahāsamudre gādhaṃ labdhum āha / no hīdaṃ bhagavan
body.translated_text: [SaSū 91] 'What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>—can this <s>sūtra</s> be heard by foolish ordinary beings?' He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' He said: 'And those who hear it but do not generate faith—listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: are there, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, any foolish ordinary beings who could find the bottom of the great ocean?' He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One.'

body.text: [SaSū 92] (bhagavān) āha / asti punaḥ sarvaśūra kaścit sattvo ya ekapāṇitalena samudraṃ kṣapayed āha / no hīdaṃ bhagavan no hīdaṃ sugata / bhagavān āha / yathā sarvaśūra nāsti sa kaścit sattvo yaḥ śaknuyādekapāṇitalena / mahāsamudraṃ śoṣayituṃ / evameva sarvaśūra ye hīnādhimuktikāḥ sattvāḥ na śakyaṃ tairayan dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotuṃ yaiḥ sarvaśūrāśītirgaṃgānadībālukāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi na dṛṣṭāni / na taiḥ śakyamayaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhituṃ / yairnavati gaṃgānadībālikāsamāni tathāgatāni na dṛṣṭāni na taiḥ śakyamayan dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 92] (The Blessed One) said: 'Is there moreover, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, any being who could dry up the ocean with a single palm?' He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One; no indeed, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, there is no being who could dry up the great ocean with a single palm—just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings of inferior aspiration cannot hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>. Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who have not seen eighty <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>—they cannot write this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>. Those who have not seen ninety <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand <s>Tathāgatas</s>—they cannot hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 93] yena tathāgatakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi na dṛṣṭāni ta iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā pratikṣipanti / yaiḥ sarvaśūra gaṃgānadībālukāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīśatāni dṛṣṭāni ta iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā prasādacittamutpādayanti harṣayanti yathābhūtaṃ prajānanti / ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ yathābhūtaṃ śaddadhanti na pratikṣipanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 93] 'Those who have not seen hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having heard this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, reject it. Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who have seen hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river—having heard this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, they generate a mind of faith, rejoice, and know it as it truly is. Those who truly believe in this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> and do not reject it.'

body.text: [SaSū 94] śṛṇu sarvaśūra ye kecid asmāt saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyadekākṣarāmapi catuṣpadikāṃ gāthāṃ likhiṣyanti teṣāṃ sarvaśūra sattvānāṃ tataḥ paścāt paṃcanavati koṭīsahasrāni lokadhātunāmatikramya yathā sukhāvatīlokadhātustathā teṣāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati / teṣāṃ ca sarvaśūra sattvānāṃ caturaśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 94] Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Whoever will write even a single syllable or a verse of four lines from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> (discourse on Dharma) — for those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, after that, having traversed ninety-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of world-realms, their <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) will be just like the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm. And the lifespan of those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will be eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages).

body.text: [SaSū 95] śṛṇu sarvaśūra ye bodhisattvā mahāsattvā asmāt saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpadikāmapi gāthāṃ śroṣyanti / badyathā sarvaśūra kaścit sattvo bhaved (raudraḥ sāhasikaḥ saddharmavimukhaḥ paralokanirapekṣaḥ pāpakārī) yaḥ paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kuryāt kārayed vā kriyamāṇāni vānumodet sacet sa itaḥ saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyaccatuṣpadikamapi gāthāṃ śṛṇuyāt tasya tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 95] Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who will hear even a verse of four lines from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> — suppose, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, there were a being (cruel, reckless, averse to the true <s>Dharma</s>, heedless of the next world, an evildoer) who were to commit, or cause to be committed, or rejoice in the commission of the five heinous <s>karmas</s> (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) — if he were to hear even a verse of four lines from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, those five heinous <s>karmas</s> of his would go to complete exhaustion.

body.text: [SaSū 96] śṛṇu sarvaśūra / punaraparaṃ guṇamāmantrayāmi / tadyathāpi kaścit sattvo bhavedyaḥ stūpabhedaṃ kārayet saṃghabhedaṃ ca / bodhisattvaṃ samādheruccālayet buddhajñānasyāntarāyaṃ kuryāt mātāpitaraṃ jīvitādvyāvaropayed
body.translated_text: [SaSū 96] Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! Furthermore, I shall proclaim another quality. Suppose there were a being who would cause the destruction of a <s>stūpa</s> and the splitting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, who would disturb a <s>Bodhisattva</s> from <s>samādhi</s> (meditation), who would create an obstruction to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, and who would deprive his mother and father of life —

body.text:
atha sa sattvaḥ paścādvipratisārībhūtaḥ śoceta parideveta naṣṭo 'ham anena kāyena naṣṭaṃ me paralokamiti / kalpaṃ evāhaṃ naṣṭaḥ tato 'sya mahācittāyāsaṃ bhaveta duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeta / kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeta / tasya sarvaśūra sattvasya sarvasattvāḥ parivarjayanti jugupsanti (ca) / dagdho naṣṭa eṣā sattva laukikalokottarāddharma naṣṭo 'nekāni kalpāni yathā dagdhasthūṇaṃ /
[SaSū 97] evamevāyaṃ puruṣaḥ yathā sucitraṃ gṛhaṃ dagdhasthūṇaṃ na śobhate / evamevāyaṃ sa puruṣa iha loke na śobhate / yatra yatra ca gacchati tatra tatra sattvaiḥ paribhāṣyate praharanti ca; kṣutpipāsārdito 'pi na kiṃcillabhate / tato duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati /
body.translated_text:
then that being, becoming remorseful afterward, would grieve and lament: 'I am ruined with this body! My next world is ruined! For an entire <s>kalpa</s> I am ruined!' Then great mental anguish would arise in him; he would experience painful sensations; he would experience bitter sensations. All beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, shun and abhor that being. 'This being is burnt, ruined from both worldly and supramundane <s>Dharma</s>, ruined for countless <s>kalpas</s>, like a burnt pillar.'
[SaSū 97] Just as a beautifully decorated house with a burnt pillar is not beautiful, just so that man is not beautiful in this world. And wherever he goes, there he is reviled by beings and struck; even though afflicted by hunger and thirst, he obtains nothing. Then he experiences painful sensations.

body.text: [SaSū 98] sa kṣutpipāsāhetunā paribhāṣāhetunā prahārahetunā stūpabhedaṃ ca paṃcānantaryāṇi ca karmāṇi samanusmarati / sa tato duḥkhaṃ nirvedacittamutpādayati / kutrāhaṃ yāsyāmi ko me trāta bhavisyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 98] He, on account of hunger and thirst, on account of reviling, on account of being struck, recollects the destruction of the <s>stūpa</s> and the five heinous <s>karmas</s>. Then, out of suffering, he generates a mind of disenchantment: 'Where shall I go? Who will be my protector?'

body.text: [SaSū 99] sa evaṃ cintayati gamiṣyāmyahaṃ parvatagirikandareṣu praviśāmi tatra me kālakriyā bhaviṣyati na ca me iha kaści trātāsti / āha ca //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 99] He thinks thus: 'I shall go into mountain caves and caverns; there my death will occur. For here there is no protector for me.' And he said:

body.text: (20) kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma dagdhasthūnaṃ nirantaram

children.text: nemaṃ loke śobhayiṣye na śobhayiṣyāmi paratra caḥ
children.translated_text: I shall not be beautiful in this world, nor shall I be beautiful in the next.

children.text: (21) antargṛhe na śobhāmi na śobhāmi ca bāhira /
children.translated_text: (21) I am not beautiful within the house, nor am I beautiful outside;
(I am not beautiful anywhere at all, for such a sinner am I.)

body.translated_text: (20) I have committed evil <s>karma</s> — like a burnt pillar, continuously,

body.text:
(22) doṣahetoḥ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena yāsyāmi durgatim
paratra duḥkhitaḥ kutra vasiṣyāmi ha durgatau //
body.translated_text:
(22) Due to [my] fault, evil has been done; by that I shall go to an unfortunate destiny.
In the next world, afflicted with suffering, where shall I dwell in that miserable state?

children.translated_text: (23) The goddesses hear his voice as he weeps with tears choking his throat:
'Alas! Hopeless, I shall depart to the next world, to an unfortunate destiny!'

body.text:
taṃ devatā āhuḥ
(24) mūḍho 'si gaccha puruṣa maivaṃ cintaya duḥkhitaḥ
śaraṇaṃ na ca me trāṇaṃ duḥkhāṃ vindāmi vedanām
(25) mātṛghāṭaṃ pitṛghāṭaṃ paṃcānantaryāñca me kṛtaṃ
parvate mūrdhni gacchāmi tata ātmā tyajāmyaham
(26) mā gaccha mūḍhapuruṣa karma mā kuru pāpakaṃ /
bahu tvayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vyāpannena hi cetasā
(27) kurvanti ye ātmaghātaṃ narakaṃ yānti duḥkhitāḥ
tataḥ patanti bhūmīṣu krandanti śokavedanāḥ
(28) na tena vīryeṇa bhavanti buddhā
bhavanti naivāpi na śrāvakaṃ labhyati mokṣayānam
anyasya vīryasya kuruṣva yatham
(29) gacchasya taṃ paravata yena so ṛṣi gatvā ca taṃ dṛṣṭva ṛṣirmahātmā /
vanditvā pādau śirasā ca tasya trāṇaṃ bhavāhī mama agrasattva
(30) deśehi dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ muhūrttam bhāto 'smi trasto ati[[rivā]]duḥkhapīḍitaḥ
(tato gataḥ sa puruṣu bhītabhītas) (taṃ parvataṃ yatra riśirmahātmā /)
(31) (vanditvā pādau hi tadā mahārṣeḥ) (provāca vākyaṃ samudīraṃ yā gīrā /)
(deśehi dharmaṃ mama pāpakāriṇaḥ) (kṛpāṃ janitvā paraduḥkhitasya //)//
body.translated_text:
The goddesses said to him:
(24) 'You are deluded — go, O man! Do not think thus in your suffering.
There is no refuge for me, no protection; I experience painful sensations.
(25) Matricide, patricide, and the five heinous [acts] have been committed by me.
I go to the mountain summit; from there I shall cast myself down.'
(26) 'Do not go, O deluded man! Do not commit [more] evil <s>karma</s>!
Much evil has been committed by you with a corrupted mind.
(27) Those who commit self-destruction go to hell, afflicted with suffering;
from there they fall upon [lower] grounds, wailing with grief and pain.
(28) Not by that kind of exertion do <s>Buddhas</s> come into being,
nor do <s>Śrāvakas</s> arise, nor is the vehicle of liberation obtained.
Make effort with a different kind of exertion!
(29) Go to that mountain where that <s>Ṛṣi</s> (sage) dwells! Having gone and seen that great-souled <s>Ṛṣi</s>,
having bowed at his feet with your head: "Be my protector, O foremost being!
(30) Teach the <s>Dharma</s> — the wholesome — even for a moment! I am frightened, terrified, exceedingly afflicted with suffering."
(Then that man went, frightened and trembling,) (to that mountain where the great-souled <s>Ṛṣi</s> was.)
(31) (Having bowed at the feet of that great <s>Ṛṣi</s> then,) (he spoke these words, uttering this speech:)
("Teach the <s>Dharma</s> to me, a sinner,) (generating compassion for one who suffers in another's plight.")'

body.text:
(32) ṛṣirvadantaṃ śṛṇu sattvasāra niṣadya cintasya kṣaṇaṃ kuruṣva /
(śṛṇuṣva vākyaṃ mama duḥkhitasya) (śrutvā hyupāyaṃ paricintayasva /)
(33) bhītaḥ sa trasto ati [[rivā]] duḥkhapīḍitas tato niṣaṇṇaḥ kṣaṇa [[vara]] taṃ muhūrtam deśemi pāpaṃ kṛta yan mayā bahū ṛṣe hi vācaṃ idamabravīti /
body.translated_text:
(32) The <s>Ṛṣi</s> [said]: 'Listen, O essence of beings! Sit down, reflect, and take a moment.
(Listen to my words, O suffering one;) (having heard the means, contemplate it well.)
(33) Frightened, terrified, and exceedingly afflicted with suffering, having sat down for a moment, [I shall say:]
"I shall confess the evil committed by me in great measure" — thus to the <s>Ṛṣi</s> he spoke these words.'

body.text:
ṛṣirāha /
(34) bhuṃśāhi taṃ bhojanu yaddadāmi duḥkhena ca krandasi śokapīḍitaḥ
kṣudhā pipāsāya ca pīḍītastvaṃ nirāśakaśca tribhavādbhaviṣyasi /
(35) bhojanānyupanāmitvā ṛṣiḥ sattva prasādayan
mṛṣṭaṃ bhuṃja manāpaṃ ca śarīre tarpanārthikaṃ /
(36) paścāt te dharma bhāṣāmi sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram
tasya tadbhojanaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ muhūrtaṃ bhuktavān asau /
(37) bhuktvā hastau ca prakṣālya kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ ṛṣiṃ /
paryaṃkena niṣīditvā vadat yat pāpakaṃ kṛtam
(38) mātṛghātaṃ pitṛghātaṃ stūpabhedaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ /
bodhisattvasya buddhatve antarāyaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā /

children.translated_text: (39) Having heard those words, the <s>Ṛṣi</s> then spoke these words:

children.text: asādhustava [[bho]] puruṣa yat kṛtaṃ pāpakaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: 'Wicked you are, O man, for the evil committed by you!

children.text: (40) deśehi pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ kārāpitaṃ ca yat //
children.translated_text: (40) Confess the evil <s>karma</s> — that which was committed and caused to be committed.'

body.translated_text:
The <s>Ṛṣi</s> said:
(34) 'Eat this food that I give you. You weep with suffering, pierced by grief;
you are afflicted by hunger and thirst, and you will become hopeless from the three worlds of existence.
(35) Having offered food, the <s>Ṛṣi</s>, gladdening the being [said]:
"Eat this fine and agreeable food, nourishing for the body.
(36) Afterward I shall teach you the <s>Dharma</s> that destroys all evil."
That one ate the fine food for a moment.
(37) Having eaten and washed his hands, having circumambulated the <s>Ṛṣi</s>,
having sat cross-legged, he spoke of the evil he had committed:
(38) "Matricide, patricide, and the destruction of a <s>stūpa</s> have been committed by me;
an obstruction to a <s>Bodhisattva's</s> <s>Buddhahood</s> has been created by me."'

body.text: atha khalu tasmin kāle sa puruṣaḥ śokaśalyasamarpita bhītastrasta udvigna ko me trātā bhaviṣyatītyāha ca //
body.translated_text: Then, at that time, that man, pierced by the arrow of grief, frightened, terrified, and anxious, [cried]: 'Who will be my protector?' And he said:

children.text: (41) kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma duḥkhāṃ vetsyāmi vedanāṃ /
children.translated_text: (41) 'I have committed evil <s>karma</s>; I shall experience painful sensations

children.text: narake raurave ghore tathaiva ca pratāpane //
children.translated_text: in hell, in the terrible <s>Raurava</s>, and likewise in <s>Pratāpana</s>.'

body.text:
atha khalu sa puruṣastasya ṛṣerjānudvayaṃ bhūmau nipātyāha ca /
(42) deśeyaṃ pāpakaṃ karma yatkṛtaṃ kāritaṃ mayā /
māphalaṃ pāpakaṃ bhotu mā me syā duḥkhavedanāṃ /
(43) ṛṣistrāṇaṃ bhaven mahyamāsanne haṃ bhaven tava
niṣkaukṛtyasya śāntasya śamyantaṃ pāpakān mama;
body.translated_text:
Then that man, casting both knees upon the ground before the <s>Ṛṣi</s>, said:
(42) 'I confess the evil <s>karma</s> that was committed and caused to be committed by me.
May the evil [karma] not bear fruit! May painful sensations not befall me!
(43) May the <s>Ṛṣi</s> be my protector! May I be near you,
free from remorse, at peace — may my evils be pacified!'

body.text: [SaSū 100] atha khalu sa riṣistena kālena tena samayena taṃ puruṣametadavocat - evaṃ cāśvāsayati / mā bhaiḥ kulaputrāhaṃ te trāṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmyahan te gatirahaṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmi / saṃmukhaṃ dharma śṛṇu śrutaṃ tvayā kiṃcit saṃghāṭaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ / sa āha / na me kadācicchrutaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 100] Then that <s>Ṛṣi</s>, at that time, at that moment, spoke thus to that man — and consoled him thus: 'Do not be afraid, O son of good family! I shall be your protector; I shall be your refuge and final resort. Listen to the <s>Dharma</s> face to face. Have you ever heard the <s>dharma-paryāya</s> (discourse on Dharma) called <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>?' He said: 'I have never heard it.'

body.text: ṛṣirāha - ko 'gnidagdhasya sattvasya dharman deśayatyanyatra yaḥ karuṇāvihāritayā sattvānāṃ dharman deśayati / āha / śṛṇu kulaputra
body.translated_text: The <s>Ṛṣi</s> said: 'Who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to a being who is burnt by fire, except one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings by dwelling in compassion?' He said: 'Listen, O son of good family!'

body.text: [SaSū 101] bhūtapūrvaṃ (mayā) asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairyadāsītteno kālena tena samayena vimalacandro nāma rājābhūddhārmiko dharmarājā / tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputra rājño vimalacandrasya gṛhe putro jātaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 101] 'Formerly, in incalculably more than incalculable <s>kalpas</s> ago, at that time, at that moment, there was a king named <s>Vimalacandra</s>, a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king. And in the household of that king <s>Vimalacandra</s>, O son of good family, a son was born'

body.text: [SaSū 102] atha sa rājā vimalacandro lakṣaṇanaimittikāṃcchāstrapāṭhakān brāhmaṇān sannipātya kumāramupadarśyaivamāha - kiṃ brāhmaṇa kumārasya nimittaṃ paśyatha śobhanamaśobhanaṃ veti / tatraiko naimittiko brāhmaṇaḥ kathayatyasādhurayaṃ mahārāja kumāro jātaḥ āsādhuriti / rājā śrutvā sasaṃbhrama papraccha / kimidaṃ brāhmaṇā naimittikaḥ kathayatyayaṃ deva rājakumāro yadi sapta varṣāṇi jīvati sa eṣa mātāpitaraṃ jīvitādvyāvaropayiṣyati / tato 'sa rājā evamāha / varaṃ me jīvitāntarāyo bhavatu māccāhaṃ putraṃ vadheyaṃ / tatkasmāt kadācit karhacilloke manuṣyotpādaṃ labhyate / nāhaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi / yadimaṃ mānuṣyakaṃ kāyaṃ virāgayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 102] Then King <s>Vimalacandra</s>, having assembled the sign-reading, omen-interpreting, scripture-reciting <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, showed them the prince and said: 'What sign, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, do you see for the prince — auspicious or inauspicious?' Thereupon one omen-reading <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'This prince, O great king, has been born inauspicious — inauspicious indeed.' The king, hearing this, asked in alarm: 'What is this, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>?' The omen-reader said: 'This royal prince, O lord, if he lives seven years, will deprive his parents of life.' Then that king said: 'Better that there be an obstacle to my own life than that I should kill my son! For only rarely does one obtain a human birth in this world. I will not act thus — [rather] I will become dispassionate toward this human body.'

body.text: [SaSū 103] atha sa kumāro vardhate yadanya varṣadvayena vardhante tadāsāvekena māsena vardhate / jānāti ca sa rājā vimalacandro yaṃ kumāro mama karmopacayena vardhate / tato rājā tasya kumārasya paṭṭamābandhyaivamāha / tava rājyaṃ bhavatu vipulaṃ ca kīrtirājyabhogaiśvaryaṃ ca kāraya dharmeṇa mā adharmeṇa / tatastasya rājā paṭṭaṃ badhvā rājeti nāmadheyamakarot sa ca rājā vimalacandro na bhūyaḥ svaviṣaye rājyaṃ kārayaty
body.translated_text: [SaSū 103] Then that prince grew — what another [child] grows in two years, he grew in a single month. And King <s>Vimalacandra</s> knew that the prince was growing by the accumulation of his [own past] <s>karma</s>. Then the king, binding the royal turban upon that prince, said: 'May the kingdom be yours, with abundant glory and the enjoyment and sovereignty of the kingdom; rule with <s>dharma</s>, not with <s>adharma</s>.' Having thus bound the turban and given him the title 'King,' King <s>Vimalacandra</s> himself no longer ruled in his own realm.

body.text: [SaSū 104] atha te triṃśadamātyakoṭyo yena sa rājā vimalacandrastenopasaṃkrāntā upetya taṃ rājānaṃ vimalacandramevamāhuḥ kasmāt tvaṃ bhoḥ mahārāja svaviṣaye na bhūyo rājyaṃ kārayasi / rājāha - bahūnyasaṃkhyeyāni kalpāni / yanmayā rājyabhogaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritaṃ na ca me kadācid viṣayeṣu tṛptirāsīttena ca kālena tena samayena na cireṇa kālāntareṇa sa putrastaṃ mātāpitaraṃ jīvitādvyāvaropayati / tena ca tatra paṃcānantaryāṇi karmānyupacitāni / ahaṃ ca bhoḥ puruṣa tāvacciraṃ kālasamayamanusmarāmi / yathādya śvo vā /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 104] Then thirty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of ministers approached King <s>Vimalacandra</s> and said to him: 'Why, O great king, do you no longer rule in your own realm?' The king said: 'For many incalculable <s>kalpas</s> I have exercised kingship, enjoyment, sovereignty, and dominion, yet I never had satisfaction in sense-objects. And at that time, at that moment, not long after, the son will deprive his parents of life. And thereby the five heinous <s>karmas</s> (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) will be accumulated. And I, O good man, remember that long time and that occasion as if it were today or tomorrow.'

body.text: [SaSū 105] yadā tasya rājño duḥkhā vedanā utpannāḥ tadā sa rājā vipratisārībhūto srukaṇṭhaḥ paridevati pāpaṃ me karma kṛtamiti / avīcau mahānarake duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhaviṣyāmīti tato 'haṃ kāruṇyacittamutpādya tatra gatvā tasya rājño dharman deśayitavān atha sa rāja taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tasya tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṣipraṃ niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ gatāni /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 105] When painful sensations arose for that king, then he, overcome with remorse, with tears in his throat, lamented: 'Evil <s>karma</s> was done by me! I will experience painful sensations in <s>Avīci</s>, the great hell!' Then I, generating a mind of compassion, went there and taught the <s>Dharma</s> to that king. And that king, having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, those five heinous <s>karmas</s> of his quickly went to complete exhaustion without remainder.

body.text:
āha ca /
(44) saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrarājaṃ mahātapāḥ
ye śroṣyanti iman dharman padaṃ prāpsyantyanuttaram
(45) sarvapāpakṣayaṃ bhavati / sarvakleśāṃcchamiṣyati /
śṛṇu dharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena kṣipraṃ vimokṣase /
(46) catuṣpadāyāṃ gāthāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇaṃ nirantaraṃ
sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā srotāpanno bhaviṣyasi /
(47) tato dānaṃ udānemi sarvapāpapramocanaṃ /
vimocitā duḥkhitā sattvā nārakādbhayabhairavāt

children.translated_text: (48) Then that man, rising from his seat, with palms joined,
bowing his head, gives his applause:
(49) Excellent are the spiritual friends! Excellent is the destroyer of sin!
Excellent is the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> teaching — those who will hear this great doctrine!

body.translated_text:
And [he] said:
(44) The <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, the king of <s>sūtras</s>, O great ascetic — those who will hear this <s>Dharma</s> will attain the unsurpassed state.
(45) All sin is destroyed; all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) will be pacified. Hear the <s>Dharma</s> I will declare, by which you will quickly be liberated!
(46) When a verse of four lines is being spoken without interruption, having destroyed all sin, you will become a <s>Srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer).
(47) Then I give the gift of complete liberation from all sin; liberated are the suffering beings from hell, [that place] of fearful terror.

body.text: [SaSū 106] atha khalu tena kālena tena samayenoparyantarikṣe sthitāni dvādaśa devaputrasahasrāṇi kṛtāṃjalipuṭāni tam ṛṣimupagamya pādau śirasā praṇamyaivamāhuḥ bhagavan kevacciraṃ smarasi mahātapaḥ evaṃ catvāri koṭī nāgarājñāmāgatya aṣṭādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi yakṣarājñāmāgatya yena sa ṛṣistenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmyaivamāhuḥ kevacciraṃ smarasi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 106] Then at that time, at that moment, twelve thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), standing in the sky above, with palms joined, approached that <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), bowed their heads at his feet, and said: 'Blessed One, how long do you remember, O great ascetic?' Likewise, four <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nāga</s> kings arrived, and eighteen <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>yakṣa</s> kings arrived, and approaching that <s>ṛṣi</s>, with palms joined in reverence, said: 'How long do you remember?'

body.text:
[SaSū 107] mahātmā ṛṣirāha /
śatamasaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutasahasrāṇi samanusmarāmi / āha / kena kuśalakarmaṇā / muhūrtamātreṇaivaṃ pāpaṃ karma (sarvapāpakarma) praśāntam (āha / saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā) (anena kuśalakarmaṇā sarvapāpakarma praśāntam)
body.translated_text:
[SaSū 107] The great-souled <s>ṛṣi</s> said:
'I remember a hundred incalculable <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>.' [They] said: 'By what wholesome <s>karma</s>?' [He said:] 'In a mere moment, such evil <s>karma</s> (all evil <s>karma</s>) was pacified.' (He said: 'Having heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> — by this wholesome <s>karma</s>, all evil <s>karma</s> was pacified.')

body.text: [SaSū 108] ye ca tatra sattvāḥ sannipatitāḥ yairimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā śraddadhānatā vā kṛtā pattīyanaṃ vā / te sarve vyākriyante 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / yena ca puruṣeṇa tāṇi paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāni / tenemaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā muhūrtamātreṇa tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ kṛtāṇi / tasyānekāni kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvadurgatidvārāṇi pithitāni bhavanti / dvātriṃśaddevalokadvārāṇyapāvṛtāni bhavanti / ya itaḥ saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpadikāmapi gāthāṃ śroṣyati / tasyetādṛśāni kuśalamūlāni bhaviṣyanti / kaḥ punarvādo yaḥ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati / puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhirvādyāṃjalikarmapraṇāmaṃ vā kariṣyati / ekāṃ vārāṃ anumodiṣyatyevaṃ ca vakṣyati / sādhu subhāṣitamiti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 108] And those beings who had assembled there, who upon hearing this <s>dharma-paryāya</s> generated faith or conviction — they were all given a prophecy of unsurpassed perfect awakening. And that man by whom the five heinous <s>karmas</s> had been committed — having heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, in a mere moment those five heinous <s>karmas</s> went to complete exhaustion and elimination without remainder. For him, for many <s>kalpa-koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands, the doors to all unfortunate destinies became closed, and the doors to the thirty-two heavenly realms became opened. Whoever will hear even a single verse of four lines from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, for that [person] such wholesome roots will arise. How much more so for one who will honor, revere, esteem, and worship the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> — with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, powder, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants, or will perform [offerings of] music, palms-joined reverence, or prostration — or will rejoice even once and say: 'Well spoken!'

body.text: [SaSū 109] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kiyantaṃ bhagavannañjalipraṇāmāt puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati / ye te saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣyamāṇaṃ śrutvāñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamanti / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu kulaputra yena paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāṇi kāritāni kriyamāṇāni vānumoditāni bhaveyuḥ yadi sa itat saṃghāṭāddharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpadikāmapi gāthāṃ śrutvāñjaliṃ praṇāmayiṣyati / tasya (tāni) sarvāṇi paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṣayaṃ gatāni bhaviṣyanti / kaḥ punarvādaḥ sarvaśūra yaḥ sakalasamāptamevāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyatyayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 109] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'How great an aggregate of merit, Blessed One, does one generate from joining the palms and bowing — those who, having heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> being spoken, join their palms and bow?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, son of good family! One by whom the five heinous <s>karmas</s> have been committed, caused to be committed, or are being committed, or have been approved — if that one, having heard even a single verse of four lines from this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, will join palms and bow, all those five heinous <s>karmas</s> of that [person] will have gone to exhaustion. How much more, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, one who will hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s> complete in its entirety — that one will generate a far greater aggregate of merit.'

body.text: [SaSū 110] upamāṃ te kulaputra kariṣyāmi / asya saṃghāṭasūtrārthasya vijñaptaye / tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūrānavataptasya nāgarājasya bhavane na kadācit sūryo vabhāsayati / tataśca paṃca mahānadyaḥ pravahanti / atha kaścideva puruṣo bhaved yastāsāṃ paṃcānāṃ mahānadīnāmudakasya bindūni gaṇayet tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra śakyaṃ teṣāmudakavindunāṃ gaṇanāyogena paryantamadhigantum āha / no hīdaṃ bhagavan no hīdaṃ sugata, bhagavān āha - evameva sarvaśūra na śakyaṃ saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya kuśalamūlaṃ kalpena vā kalpaśatena vā kalpasahasreṇa vā kalpaśatasahasreṇa vā kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṇa vā gaṇanayā paryantamadhigantuṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 110] 'I will give you an analogy, son of good family, for the understanding of the meaning of this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>. Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the sun never shines in the abode of the <s>nāga</s> king <s>Anavataptā</s>, and from there five great rivers flow — suppose some person were to count the water-drops of those five great rivers. What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>? Could the limit of those water-drops be reached by counting?' He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One! No indeed, <s>Sugata</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the wholesome root of the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s> cannot be reached by counting — not in a <s>kalpa</s>, nor in a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, nor in a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, nor in a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, nor in a <s>kalpa-koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousand.'

body.text: [SaSū 111] tatkiṃ manyase sarvaśūra duṣkaraṃ tasya ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ muhūrtaṃ prakāśayeta / āha - duṣkaraṃ bhagavaṃ duṣkaraṃ sugata, bhagavān āha - ataḥ suduṣkarataraṃ sarvaśūra tasya ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śākṣyati śrotum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 111] 'What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>? It is a difficult deed for one who would illuminate this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> even for a moment.' He said: 'It is difficult, Blessed One! It is difficult, <s>Sugata</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'Even more difficult than that, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is it for one who will be able to hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 112] tadyathā anavataptāt (mahāsarasaḥ) paṃca mahānadyaḥ pravahanti / tāsāṃ paṃcānāṃ mahānadīnāṃ pravahatāmudakavindūnna śakyaṃ kenacidgaṇakena vā gaṇakamahāmātrena vā gaṇanayā paryantamadhigantumevamevāsya dharmaparyāyasya puṇyaskandhasya na śakyaṃ paryantamadhigantum sarvaśūra āha - katamāstā bhagavan paṃca mahānadya / bhagavān āha - tadyathā / gaṃgā sītā vakṣuḥ yamunāścandrabhāgā ca / imā sarvaśūra paṃca mahānadyo mahāsamudre praviśanti / ekaikā ca mahānadī paṃcamahānadīśataparivārāḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 112] 'Just as five great rivers flow from [Lake] <s>Anavataptā</s> (the great lake) — the limit of the water-drops of those five great rivers as they flow cannot be reached by any accountant or chief accountant through counting — just so, the limit of the aggregate of merit of this <s>dharma-paryāya</s> cannot be reached.' <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Which, Blessed One, are those five great rivers?' The Blessed One said: 'They are: <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Vakṣu</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and <s>Candrabhāgā</s>. These, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are the five great rivers that enter the great ocean. And each great river is accompanied by five hundred great rivers.'

body.text: [SaSū 113] punaraparaṃ sarvaśūra paṃcemā mahānadyaḥ ākāśe pravahanti / yā satatasamitamudakavindubhiḥ prajāṃ plāvayanti / tāśca paṃca mahānadyaḥ ekaikā sahasraparivārāḥ āha - katamāstā bhagavan paṃca mahānadyaḥ sahasrāparivārāḥ yā ākāśe pravahanti / bhagavān āha - sundarī nāma (nadī) sahasraparivārā, śaṃkhā nāma (nadī) sahasraparivārā, vahantī nāma (nadī) sahasraparivārā, citrasenā nāma (nadī) sahasraparivārā, dharmavṛttā nāma (nadī) sahasraparivārā, imāstā sarvaśūra paṃca mahanadyaḥ sahasraparivārā yā jaṃbūdvīpe autsukyamāpadyante / yāḥ kālena kālaṃ jaṃbūdvīpe bindubhirvarṣadhārāḥ pramuṃcanti / tena puṣpaphalasasyānyabhiruhyanti / yadā jaṃbūdvīpe (vindūbhi) varṣadhārāḥ prapatanti / tadā udakaṃ jāyate / jātaṃ codakaṃ sarvakṣetrārāmāṇi saṃtarpayati sukhaṃ ca kārayati / tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūra prajāpati sarvajaṃbūdvīpe sukhaṃ kārayati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 113] 'Furthermore, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, these five great rivers flow in the sky, which constantly and continuously flood the people with drops of water. And these five great rivers are each accompanied by a thousand [tributaries].' He said: 'Which, Blessed One, are those five great rivers with a thousand attendants that flow in the sky?' The Blessed One said: 'The river named <s>Sundarī</s>, with a thousand attendants; the river named <s>Śaṅkhā</s>, with a thousand attendants; the river named <s>Vahantī</s>, with a thousand attendants; the river named <s>Citrasenā</s>, with a thousand attendants; the river named <s>Dharmavṛttā</s>, with a thousand attendants. These, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are the five great rivers with a thousand attendants that produce eagerness in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; which from time to time release streams of rain with drops upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. By that, flowers, fruits, and crops grow. When streams of rain (with drops) fall upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, then water is born. And the water that is born refreshes all fields and gardens and produces happiness. Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> (the lord of creatures) produces happiness in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>—'

body.text: [SaSū 114] evaṃ eva sarvaśurāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāya bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya jaṃbūdvīpe prakāśitaḥ yathā (ca sarvaśūra) devānāṃ trāyastiṃśānāmāyuṣpramāṇaṃ na tathā manuṣyāṇāṃ / (tatra) katame ca sarvaśūra trāyastriṃśā devāḥ yatra śakro devānāmindraḥ prativasati / te trāyastriṃśā nāma devāḥ santi (tadyathā)sarvaśūra sattvāḥ ya ekaṃ vāksucaritaṃ bhāṣante / teṣāṃ na śakyaṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartuṃ / (yan te devamanuṣyeṣvanupamaṃ saukhyamanubhavanti /)
body.translated_text: [SaSū 114] 'just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> has been revealed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the benefit and happiness of the many. And (as for, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>,) the measure of the lifespan of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods—it is not so for humans. (And therein) which, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods where <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, dwells? Those gods called <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> are (as follows): <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings who speak a single well-spoken word—the comparison for their aggregate of merit cannot be made. (For they experience incomparable happiness among gods and humans.)'

body.text: [SaSū 115] santi sarvaśūra sattvāḥ ya ekaṃ vagduścaritaṃ bhāṣante na śakyaṃ teṣāṃ narakatiryakṣūpamāṃ kartum yat te sattvāḥ narakatiryakpretaduḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti / na (ca) kaścit teṣāṃ trātā bhavati tatra te nirāśāḥ paridevante narakeṣu prapatamānāḥ tad akalyāṇamitravaśena draṣṭavyaṃ / ye sattvā vāksucaritaṃ bhāṣante teṣāṃ na śakyaṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartuṃ / tat kalyāṇamitravaśena draṣṭavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 115] 'There are, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings who speak a single ill-spoken word—the comparison to their [experience in] hells and animal realms cannot be made, the painful sensation of hells, animal realms, and <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) [realms] that those beings experience. And no one becomes their rescuer. There they lament hopelessly while falling into the hells. That should be seen as due to the influence of evil companions. Those beings who speak well-spoken words—the comparison for their aggregate of merit cannot be made. That should be seen as due to the influence of virtuous companions.'

body.text: [SaSū 116] yadā kalyāṇamitraṃ paśyati tadā tathāgato dṛṣṭo bhavati / yadā tathāgataṃ paśyati / tadā (tasya) sarvapāpakṣayo bhavati / yadā sarvapāpakṣayo bhavati / tadā prajāpatirjaṃbūdvīpe autsukyaṃ karoti / yadā prajāpatirjaṃbudvīpe autsukyaṃ karoti / tadā jaṃbūdvīpakanāṃ sattvānāṃ sukhasya na śakyamupamāṃ kartumevamevāyaṃ sarvaśūra saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāya jaṃbūdvīpakānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / tadā na śakyaṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 116] 'When one sees a virtuous companion, a <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen. When one sees a <s>Tathāgata</s>, the exhaustion of all evil occurs for that [person]. When the exhaustion of all evil occurs, <s>Prajāpati</s> produces eagerness in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. When <s>Prajāpati</s> produces eagerness in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the comparison for the happiness of the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> cannot be made. Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> performs the <s>Buddha's</s> work for the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Then the comparison for the aggregate of merit of those beings cannot be made.'

body.text: [SaSū 117] tadyathāpi nāma sarvaśūra yatremāḥ paṃca mahānadyaḥ saṃbhedaṃ samavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti / tatra na śakyamudakasya pramāṇamudgrahītuṃ / etāvadudakakuṃbhā vā udakakuṃbhaśatāni vā udakakuṃbhasahasrāṇi vā udakakuṃbhaśatasahasrāṇi vā / api tu bahutvādudakasya mahān udakaskandha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 117] 'Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, where these five great rivers reach their confluence and meeting—there the measure of water cannot be grasped: so many water-pots, or hundreds of water-pots, or thousands of water-pots, or hundreds of thousands of water-pots. But due to the great quantity of water, it is counted as a great mass of water.'

body.text: [SaSū 118] evameva sarvaśūra yadā jaṃbūdvīpakā sattvā imaṃ saṃghātaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / śrutvā codgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti / vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti / pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti pratipatyā ca saṃpādayiṣyanti / tadā na śakyaṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ puṇyaskandhasya pramāṇaṃ udgrahītumapi tu bahutvāt puṇyasya mahān puṇyaskandha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 118] 'Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, when the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, explain it in detail to others, and realize it through practice—then the measure of the aggregate of merit of those beings cannot be grasped. But due to the great quantity of merit, it is counted as a great aggregate of merit.'

body.text: [SaSū 119] ye sarvaśūra sattvāḥ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ na śroṣyanti na taiḥ śakyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum na śakyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayitum na śakyaṃ dharmagaṇḍī parāhanitum na śakyaṃ tairdharmasiṃhāsanamabhiroḍhuṃ na śakyaṃ (tai) nirvāṇadhātumanupraveṣṭuṃ / na śakyamaprameyai raśmibhiravabhāsayitum ya imaṃ sarvaśūra saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ na śroṣyanti na śakyaṃ tairbodhimaṇḍe niṣattuṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 119] 'Those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who will not hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>—they cannot fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening; they cannot turn the <s>Dharma</s> wheel; they cannot strike the <s>Dharma</s> gong; they cannot ascend the <s>Dharma</s> lion-throne; they cannot enter the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; they cannot illuminate with immeasurable rays. Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who will not hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>—they cannot sit at the seat of awakening.'

body.text:
[SaSū 120] sarvaśūra āha - pṛcchāmi bhagavaṃ pṛcchāmi sugata, kaṃcideva kautuhalam bhagavān āha - pṛccha tvaṃ sarvaśūra yad yad evākāṃkṣasyahaṃ te niṣkāṃkṣaṃ kariṣyāmi (sarvaśūra) āha - katamaḥ sa bhagavan ṛṣirabhūd yena te sattvāḥ paṃcabhirānantaryaiḥ karmabhiḥ parimokṣitāḥ avaivarttikabhūmau ca pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ bhagavān āha -
(50) sūkṣmaṃ vacana buddhānāṃ sarvaśūra śṛṇohi me
saṃghāṭadarśanaṃ sūtraṃ ṛṣirūpeṇa darśitaṃ

children.translated_text: (51) 'The <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> reveals the <s>Buddha's</s> form out of compassion;'
'just as [the river] <s>Balikā Gaṅgā</s> reveals [its] form, even so.'

children.text: (52) buddho darśayate rūpaṃ dharman deśayate svayam
children.translated_text: (52) 'The <s>Buddha</s> reveals [his] form and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> himself;'
'whoever wishes to see the <s>Buddha</s>, (the Protector of the World, the Supreme Conqueror,)'

body.translated_text:
[SaSū 120] <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'I ask, Blessed One; I ask, <s>Sugata</s>—about a certain curiosity.' The Blessed One said: 'Ask, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, whatever you wish; I shall remove your doubt.' (<s>Sarvaśūra</s>) said: 'Who, Blessed One, was that <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) by whom those beings were liberated from the five heinous <s>karmas</s> and established on the irreversible stage?' The Blessed One said:
(50) 'Hear me, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the subtle speech of the <s>Buddhas</s>:
The <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> was shown in the form of a <s>ṛṣi</s>.'

body.text:
(53) (saṃghāṭastena śrotavyaḥ) saṃghāṭaṃ buddhasādṛśaṃ /
buddhas tatra bhaven nityaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati /
body.translated_text:
(53) '(should hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>,) the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> is equal to the <s>Buddha</s>;
the <s>Buddha</s> is always present there, wherever the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> abides.'

body.text: [SaSū 121] bhagavān āha - śṛṇu kulaputra / bhūtapūrvaṃ sarvaśūrātīte dhvani navānavatyasaṃkhyeyaṅ kalpān anusmarāmi / (tatra) dvādaśa buddhakoṭya babhūvan ratnottamanāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ahaṃ tena kālena tena samayena pradānaśūro bhūvaṃ candra nāma / te ca me dvādaśa buddhakoṭya paryupāsitāḥ khādanīyabhojanīyamālyagandhavilepanena yathāsukhaṃ / praṇītenāhāreṇa sarvasukhopadhānenopasthitāḥ upasthāpya ca tatraiva mayā sarvaśūra vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham
body.translated_text: [SaSū 121] The Blessed One said: 'Listen, son of good family. In the past, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, in a past age, I recall ninety-nine incalculable <s>kalpas</s>. (There) twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> arose, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Ratnottama</s>. I, at that time, at that moment, was a hero of giving, named <s>Candra</s>. Those twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were attended upon by me with food, drink, garlands, fragrances, and ointments, as they wished, with excellent nourishment and all provisions of comfort. And having attended them, right there, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I received the prediction for unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 122] abhijānāmyahaṃ sarvaśūrāṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭya sarve ratnāvabhāsanāmānastathāgatā loka utpannā abhūvan tatrāhamapi pradānaśūro bhūvan garbhaseno nāma / te cāṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyo mayā paryupāsitāḥ pūjitāśca / yathā tathāgatānāṃ pratyarhaṃ gandhamālyavilepanālaṃkāravibhūṣaṇaiḥ tatra ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 122] 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, all named <s>Ratnāvabhāsa</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arose in the world. There too I was a hero of giving, named <s>Garbhasena</s>. Those eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were attended upon and worshipped by me, as befitting <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with fragrances, garlands, ointments, ornaments, and adornments. And there too I received the prediction for unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 123] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra viṣmaśatirbuddhakoṭyaḥ śikhisaṃbhavanāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta, pūjitā me te buddhā bhagavanto yathā pratyarheṇa pūjasatkāreṇa tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham na cādyāpi kālasamayamabhūdvyākaraṇāya //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 123] 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, twenty [times] a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Śikhisaṃbhava</s>, arose in the world. Those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, were worshipped by me with appropriate worship and veneration. And right there I received the prediction for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Yet even now the time and occasion for the [fulfillment of the] prediction has not come.'

body.text: [SaSū 124] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra viṃśatyeva buddhakoṭyaḥ kāśyapa nāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyantaḥ tatrāhamapi pradānaśūro bhūvan kṛtaṃ me teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmupasthānaṃ / gandhena mālyena vilepanena tathāgatagurūpasthānenopasthitāḥ yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurugauravaṃ kartavyaṃ tathā kṛtaṃ / tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 124] 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, exactly twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, arose in the world. There too I was a hero of giving. I performed attendance upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>—with fragrance, garlands, ointments, and respectful service to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-teachers, doing the honor and reverence that should be done to <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And right there I received the prediction for unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 125] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra ṣoḍaśa buddhakoṭyo bhūvan vimalaprabhāsanāmāna tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ tena ca kālena tena samayenāhaṃ gṛhapatirabhūvadāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ sarvasvaparityāgī (mahātyāgī /) / te ca mayā ṣoḍaśa buddhakoṭyaḥ pūjitā āstaraṇaprāvaraṇena gandhena mālyena vilepanena vibhūṣaṇācchādanena ca / yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurūpasthānaṃ (kartavyaṃ tathā ca mayā) kṛtaṃ / tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ / na ca me kālaṃ na samayamabhūdvyākaraṇāya //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 125] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, sixteen <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s> who existed — <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Vimalaprabhāsa</s>. At that time, at that moment, I was a householder, wealthy, of great riches, of great enjoyments, one who relinquishes all possessions (a great renouncer). Those sixteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped by me with bedding, coverings, perfumes, garlands, unguents, ornaments, and clothing. Just as the devoted service of <s>Tathāgatas</s> (should be performed, so it was performed by me). And right there I received my prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But the time and the occasion for [the fulfillment of] my prediction had not yet come.

body.text: [SaSū 126] śṛṇu sarvaśūrānusmarāmyahaṃ paṃcanavatirbuddhakoṭyo loka utpannānyabhūvan sarve śākyamunisahanāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena ca rājā bhūddhārmiko dharmarājā, paryupāsitā me (te) paṃcanavatirbuddhakoṭyaḥ śākyamunināmadheyāstathāgatāḥ gandhena mālyena vilepanenāstaraṇapravaraṇena cchatradhvajapatākābhiśca / tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 126] Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! I recollect ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> who had arisen in the world, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, bearing the name <s>Śākyamuni</s>. At that time, at that moment, I was a king, righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king. Those ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> were attended upon by me and worshipped with perfumes, garlands, unguents, bedding, coverings, parasols, banners, and pennants. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: [SaSū 127] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra navatirbuddhakoṭyaḥ krakatsudanāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta, ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena brāhmakumāro 'bhūva āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ pradānadātā sarvasvaparityāgī / te ca mayā tathāgatā sarve upasthitāḥ gandhena mālyena vilepanenāstarāṇaprāvaraṇena vibhūṣaṇācchādanena / yādṛśaṃ ca tathāgatānāmupasthānaṃ (tathā teṣāṃ mayā pratyarhamupasthānaṃ) kṛtaṃ tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇaṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ na ca me kālaṃ na samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 127] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, ninety <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Krakatsuda</s> — who had arisen in the world. At that time, at that moment, I was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> youth, wealthy, of great riches, of great enjoyments, a generous giver, one who relinquishes all possessions. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were all attended upon by me with perfumes, garlands, unguents, bedding, coverings, ornaments, and clothing. And such service as is befitting for <s>Tathāgatas</s> (such worthy service was performed by me for them). And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But the time and the occasion for my prediction had not yet come.

body.text: [SaSū 128] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūrāṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyaḥ loka udapadyanta ; sarve kanakamunināmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena pradānaśūro bhūvan paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pujitāśca gandhena mālyena vilepanenāstaraṇaprāvaraṇena vibhūṣaṇena / yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurupasthānāṃ tathā me upasthitāḥ tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ na ca me kālaṃ na samayaṃ vyākaraṇāyai /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 128] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> who had arisen in the world, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Kanakamuni</s>. At that time, at that moment, I was <s>Pradānaśūra</s> (a hero of generosity). Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones were attended upon by me and worshipped with perfumes, garlands, unguents, bedding, coverings, and ornaments. Just as the devoted service of <s>Tathāgatas</s> [should be], so were they attended upon by me. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But the time and the occasion for my prediction had not yet come.

body.text: [SaSū 129] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra trayodaśa buddhakoṭyo loka udapadyanta; sarve vabhāsaśirnāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ te ca me tathāgatāḥ pūjitā āstaraṇaprāvaraṇena gandhena mālyena vilepanācchādanavibhūṣaṇena / yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurūpasthānaṃ kṛtaṃ tadṛśamupasthānamupasthitāḥ taiśca tathāgatairnānādharmamukhāni bhāṣitāni arthavinayaviniścayā tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ na cādyāpi samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 129] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, thirteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> who had arisen in the world, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Vabhāsaśir</s>. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were worshipped by me with bedding, coverings, perfumes, garlands, unguents, clothing, and ornaments. Just as the devoted service of <s>Tathāgatas</s> [should be], such service was performed. And those <s>Tathāgatas</s> taught many gateways of <s>Dharma</s> and determinations of meaning and discipline. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But even now the occasion for my prediction has not come.

body.text: [SaSū 130] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra paṃcaviṃśatirbuddhakoṭyaḥ puṣyanāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapādyanta; ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena prabrajito 'bhūvam paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā yathā ānandaitarhi mamopasthāyakaupasthānamupatiṣṭhati / tādṛśaṃ ca me te tathāgatā upasthitāḥ tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ na cādyāpi me samayamabhūdvyākaraṇāya /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 130] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Puṣya</s> — who had arisen in the world. At that time, at that moment, I had gone forth as a renunciant. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were attended upon by me just as <s>Ānanda</s> now attends upon me as my attendant. Such was my service to those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But even now the occasion for my prediction has not come.

body.text: [SaSū 131] anusmarāmyahaṃ sarvaśūra aṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyo vipaśyināmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta; paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ābharaṇaprāvaraṇenācchādanagandhamālyavilepanena yathā tathāgatopasthānaṃ tathā (me) upasthitā / ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena prabrajito 'bhūvan tatraiva ca (me) vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhavān na cādyapi samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya na cireṇa kālena /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 131] I recollect, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, named <s>Vipaśyin</s> — who had arisen in the world. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones were attended upon by me and worshipped with ornaments, coverings, clothing, perfumes, garlands, and unguents — just as the service of <s>Tathāgatas</s> [should be], so were they attended upon by me. At that time, at that moment, I had gone forth as a renunciant. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But even now the occasion for my prediction has not come, [even after] a long time.

body.text: [SaSū 132] yaḥ paścimako vipaśyi loka utpannaḥ sa imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣitavān tamahaṃ jñātvā tasmin samaye jaṃbudvīpe saptaratnavarṣaṃ pravṛṣṭavān tadā te jāṃbudvīpakāḥ sattvā adaridrā saṃvṛttāḥ tatraiva cāhaṃ vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhavān tataścireṇa kālasamayenādyāpi (ca) māṃ na vyākaroti (anutpattikadharmakṣāntivyākaraṇena /)
body.translated_text: [SaSū 132] The last <s>Vipaśyin</s> who had arisen in the world — he had spoken this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>. Knowing that, at that time, I caused a rain of the seven precious substances to fall upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Then the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became free from poverty. And right there I received my prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But even after a long time, even now, he does not give me the prediction (the prediction of <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> — patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas).

body.text: [SaSū 133] āha / katamaḥ sa bhagavān kālaḥ katamaḥ sa samayaḥ bhagavān āha - śṛṇu sarvaśūra tato dvyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairdīpaṃkaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi / tato 'haṃ sarvaśura tena kālena tena samayena megho nāma aṇavako bhūvan yadā ca bhagavan dīpaṃkarastathāgato loka utpannaḥ tadāhamapi tasmin kāle tasmin samaye brahmacaryamacārṣaṃ māṇavakarūpeṇa tato 'haṃ bhagavantan dīpaṃkaran tathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā prasāda pratilabdhaḥ saptabhirutpalairavakīrṇavāṃ tacca tathāgatāvaropitaṃ kuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitam sa ca mān dīpaṃkarastathāgato vyākārṣīdbhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇavakānāgate 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 133] [<s>Sarvaśūra</s>] said: 'What was that time, Blessed One? What was that occasion?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>! After two incalculable <s>kalpas</s> from then, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> arose in the world. Then, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, at that time, at that moment, I was a young student named <s>Megha</s>. And when the blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> arose in the world, at that very time, at that moment, I practiced the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the form of a young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> student. Then, having seen the blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, I obtained faith and scattered seven blue lotuses [upon him]. And that wholesome root (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) planted before the <s>Tathāgata</s> was dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> gave me the prediction: "You, young student, in the future, after incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>."'

body.text: [SaSū 134] tato 'haṃ sarvaśūra dvādaśatālamātraṃ vihāyasamantarīkṣe sthitvānutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabdhavān yacca me sarvaśūrāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ / yacca pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ tatsarvamāmukhībhūtamivānusmarāmi yathādya śvo vā / tatra mayā sarvaśūrānekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni / kaḥ punarvāda sarvaśūra ya etarhyahama anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ sarvasattvahitaiṣiṇaḥ kāruṇikaḥ sattvānāṃ nirodhadharman deśayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 134] 'Then, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having risen twelve palm-tree heights into the sky, I obtained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). And whatever holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) I practiced over incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, and whatever wholesome root connected with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — all of it I recollect as if it were just before my very face, as if today or yesterday. Therein, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, many <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of beings were established by me in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. What more need be said, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>? Now that I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, compassionate, desiring the welfare of all beings, shall I teach beings the <s>Dharma</s> of cessation?'

body.text: [SaSū 135] naitatsthānaṃ vidyate / tatkasya hetoḥ bahuprakāraṃ cāhaṃ sarvaśūra sattvānān dharman deśayāmi / yathārūpavainayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathārūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi / devarūpeṇa devaloke (devānāṃ) dharman deśayāmi / nāgabhavaṇe nāgarūpeṇa (nāgānānaṃ) dharman deśayāmi / yakṣabhavane yakṣarūpena (yakṣānāṃ) dharman deśayāmi / pretabhavane pretarūpeṇa (pretānāṃ) dharman deśayāmi / manuṣyaloke manuṣyarūpena (manuṣyāṇāṃ) dharman deśayāmi / buddhavainayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddharūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi / bodhisattvāvainayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi / śrāvakavainayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ śrāvakarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi / yena yena rūpeṇa sattvā vinayaṃ gacchanti tena tena rūpeṇāhaṃ sattvānān dharman deśayāmi / evaṃ bahuprakāram ahaṃ sarvaśūra sattvānān dharman deśayāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 135] 'That is impossible! For what reason? Because I, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in many ways. To those beings who are to be trained in a particular manner, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in that very manner. In the form of a god, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the gods in the celestial realm. In the <s>nāga</s> realm, in the form of a <s>nāga</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> (to the <s>nāgas</s>). In the <s>yakṣa</s> realm, in the form of a <s>yakṣa</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> (to the <s>yakṣas</s>). In the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realm, in the form of a <s>preta</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> (to the <s>pretas</s>). In the human world, in human form, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> (to humans). To those beings who are to be trained by a <s>Buddha</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Buddha</s>. To those beings who are to be trained by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. To those beings who are to be trained by a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. In whatever form beings are to be trained, in that very form I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Thus in many ways, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, do I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings.'

body.text: [SaSū 136] tatkasya hetoryathaiva sarvaśūra sattvā bahuprakāraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti / tathaiva te sattvasārāḥ bahuprakāraṃ sattvānān dharman deśayanti / te ca sattvāsteṣu tathāgateṣu kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti / dānāni ca dadanti / puṇyāni ca kurvanti / svārthe ca pratijāgaranti / maraṇānusmṛtiṃ ca bhāvayiṣyanti / te caivaṃrūpaṃ kuśalaṃ karmābhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskariṣyanti / tenaiva ca dharmaśravaṇakuśalamūlahetunā tat pūrvakaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ saṃsmariṣyanti / teṣāṃ tad bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / evaṃ hi sarvaśūra saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya sahaśravaṇamātreṇaivamaprameyā(-m-asaṃkhyeyā) guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 136] For what reason? Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings hear the <s>Dharma</s> in many ways, so too those best of beings teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in many ways. And those beings plant wholesome roots in those <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they give gifts; they make merit; they are vigilant in their own welfare; and they will cultivate the recollection of death (<s>maraṇānusmṛti</s>). And they will form such wholesome <s>karmic</s> formations. And by that very cause of wholesome root from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, they will remember those prior wholesome roots. And that will be for their long-term benefit, welfare, and happiness — for gods and humans. Thus, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, merely from hearing the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra dharma-paryāya</s>, there will be such immeasurable (and incalculable) benefits and advantages.

body.text: [SaSū 137] atha te sattvāḥ parasparamevamāhuḥ astyanyaḥ kaścit kuśalo dharmaphalavipākaḥ yasya kṛtatvādupacitatvādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhyate sarvasattvāhitaiṣiṇaśca bhavanti //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 137] Then those beings said to one another: 'Is there some other wholesome fruition and ripening of <s>Dharma</s>, by doing and accumulating which one awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening and becomes one who desires the welfare of all beings?'

body.text: [SaSū 138] atha bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tānetadavocat - asti kulaputrā ye dharmaṃ pattīyanti te evaṃ vakṣyanti asti dharmo yathābhūtaḥ teṣāṃ mahāphalaṃ sukhavipākamanuttaraṃ dharmasukhaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 138] Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the mental deliberation of those beings, spoke thus to them: 'There are, sons of good family, those who have conviction in the <s>Dharma</s>. They will say thus: "The <s>Dharma</s> exists as it truly is." For them, there will be great fruit, pleasant ripening, and unsurpassed happiness of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 139] ye sattvā mohamūḍhāsta evaṃ vakṣyanti / na santi dharmāḥ na santi dharmānāṃ pāragaḥ sa teṣāṃ mahāphalaṃ kaṭukavipākamapāyeṣupapatsyate / punaḥ punaśca te (mohapuruṣā) apāyabhūmiparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 139] 'Those beings who are deluded by ignorance will say thus: "There are no <s>dharmas</s>; there is no one who has gone beyond <s>dharmas</s>." For them, the great fruit of bitter ripening will lead to rebirth in unfortunate destinies. Again and again those (deluded persons) will be destined for the realms of misfortune.'

body.text: [SaSū 140] aṣṭau kalpān nairāyikān duḥkhaṃ vedanāmanubhaviṣyanti / dvādaśa kalpāni pretayoniṣu duḥkhaṃ vedanāṃ vedayiṣyanti / ṣoḍaśa kalpānyasureṣūpapatsyante / nava kalpasahasrāni bhūtapiśācayoniṣūpapatsyante / caturdaśa kalpasahasrāṇi ajihvakā bhaviṣyanti / ṣoḍaśa kalpasahasrāṇi mātugarbhe kālaṃ kariṣyati / dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi māṃsapiṇḍā bhaviṣyanti / ekādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi jātyandhabhūtāḥ prajāsyanti / duḥkhām vedanāṃ vedayamānā / (jātyandhaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā)
