body.translated_text: [SaSū 140] 'For eight <s>kalpas</s> they will experience painful sensations in the hells; for twelve <s>kalpas</s> they will experience painful sensations in the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realms; for sixteen <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn among <s>asuras</s>; for nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn in the realms of <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>piśācas</s> (demons and ghouls); for fourteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be tongueless; for sixteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will die in the mother's womb; for twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be lumps of flesh; for eleven thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be born blind from birth, experiencing painful sensations. (And having seen one blind from birth,)

body.text: [SaSū 141] tadā mātāpitṛbhyāmevaṃ bhaviṣyati / nirāsvādamasmābhirduḥkhamanubhūtaṃ nirāsvādamasmākāṃ putro 'jātaḥ nirāsyādaṃ navā māsāḥ kukṣau dhāritaḥ śītoṣṇāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānaiḥ kṣutpipāsāsuḥkhāṇi ca pratyanubhūtāni / bahūni ca dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyāni duḥkhāni dṛṣṭvā putro 'jātaḥ na ca gṛhe mātāpitrāvutsukau kṛtau na svakāyaṃ / tato mātāpitṛbhyāṃ mahatī nirāśatā bhaviṣyati / evameva sarvaśūra nirāśāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakāḥ sattvāḥ narakatiryakpretaparāyaṇāḥ te ca tasmin maraṇakālasamaye mahatā śokāśalyasamarpitā bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 141] then the mother and father will think thus: "We have experienced tasteless suffering; our son was born tasteless; tasteless were the nine months he was carried in the womb — experiencing sensations of cold and heat, and suffering the pains of hunger and thirst. Having seen many sufferings to be experienced in this very life, a son was born, yet in the house neither mother nor father were made anxious, nor [did he care for] their own bodies." Then the mother and father will have great despair. Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, those beings who reject the true <s>Dharma</s> are despairing, destined for hell, animal, and <s>preta</s> realms. And at the time of death, they will be pierced by the great arrow of grief.

body.text: [SaSū 142] ye sarvaśūra sattvā evaṃ vāgbhāṣante asti dharmaḥ asti dharmāṇāṃ pāragaḥ te tena kuśalamūlena viṃśāti kalpāṇyuttarakuruṣūpapatsyante / paṃcaviṃśati kalpasahasrāṇi trāyastriṃśānān devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyāmupapatsyante / trayastriṃśadbhyo devebhyaścyavitvā uttarakuruṣupapatsyante / na ca mātuḥ kukṣāvupapatsyante / lokadhātuśatasahasraṃ ca drakṣyanti / sarve (ca tāṃ lokadhātavaḥ) sukhāvatīnāmānaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrasandarśanan dṛṣṭvā tatraiva pratiṣṭhānāṃ kṛtvā tatraiva bodhimabhisambhotsyante /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 142] 'Those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who speak thus: "The <s>Dharma</s> exists; there is one who has gone beyond <s>dharmas</s>" — by that wholesome root they will be reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s> for twenty <s>kalpas</s>; for twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn in the company of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods (the Thirty-three gods); and having fallen from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, they will be reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. And they will not be reborn in a mother's womb. And they will see a hundred thousand world-realms; and all (those world-realms) will be named <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. Having seen the display of all <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), and having established themselves there, they will awaken to awakening right there.'

body.text: [SaSū 143] evaṃ hi sarvaśūra mahāprabhāvo yaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyaḥ ye 'smiṃścittaprasādaṃ kariṣyanti / na te jātu viṣamaparihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyanti / pariśuddhaśīlasamavāgatāste (sattvā) bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 143] 'Thus, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s> is of such great power. Those who will generate faith in it will never die by adverse circumstances. Those (beings) will be endowed with pure moral conduct.'

body.text: [SaSū 144] santi sarvaśūra sattvā ya evaṃ vaksyanti rātrindivaṃ tathāgato bahūni sattvāni parimocayanti / adyāpi sattvadhātuḥ kṣayaṃ na gacchanti / bahavo bodhāya praṇidhānaṃ kurvati / bahavaḥ svargaloka upapadyante / bahavo nirvṛtimanuprāpnuvanti / atha kena hetunā sattvānāṃ kṣayo na bhavati //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 144] 'There are, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings who will say thus: "Day and night the <s>Tathāgata</s> liberates many beings, yet even now the realm of beings does not go to exhaustion. Many make aspirations for awakening; many are reborn in the heavenly worlds; many attain <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). Then for what reason is there no diminution of beings?"'

body.text: II. maitreyaparipṛcchā /
body.translated_text: II. The Inquiry of <s>Maitreya</s> (<s>Maitreyaparipṛcchā</s>)

body.text: [SaSū 145] athānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānāmetadabhavat gamiṣyāmo vayaṃ śramaṇena gautamena sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ atha khalu caturnavati brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakāḥ anekāni ca nigranthaśatāni yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāmanti / tena ca kālena tena samayena bhagavān smitāṃ prāduṣcakāra; //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 145] Then the thought occurred to the heterodox wanderers, mendicants, and <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetics: 'We will go and engage in debate with the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>!' Then ninety-four [groups of] <s>brāhmaṇa</s> heterodox wanderers and mendicants, and many hundreds of <s>Nirgranthas</s>, approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. And at that time, at that moment, the Blessed One displayed a smile.

body.text: [SaSū 146] atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya / nāhetuṃ nāpratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā smitaṃ prāduṣkurvanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 146] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the display of a smile? Not without cause, not without condition do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile.'

body.text: [SaSū 147] bhagavānāha - śṛṇu kulaputrādyeha rājagṛhe mahānagare mahāsannipāto bhaviṣyati / āha / ke bhagavan ihāyāsyanti / devā vā nāgā vā yakṣā vā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā / bhagavānāha - sarva ete maitreyādyehāgamiṣyanti / devanāgayakṣamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ caturaśītiṃ ca sahasrāṇi brāhmaṇānāmihāyāsyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 147] The Blessed One said: 'Listen, son of good family — today here in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a great assembly will gather.' He said: 'Who, Blessed One, will come here? Gods, or <s>nāgas</s>, or <s>yakṣas</s>, or humans, or non-humans?' The Blessed One said: 'All of these, <s>Maitreya</s>, will come here today — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, humans, and non-humans. And eighty-four thousand <s>brāhmaṇas</s> will come here.'

body.text: [SaSū 148] navati koṭīsahasrāṇi tīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānāmihā yāsyanti / te mayā sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kariṣyanti / teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vivādaśamanāya dharman deśayiṣyāmi / sarve ca te brāhmaṇā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpādayiṣyanti / navati koṭīśatasahasrāṇyanyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthāḥ sarve srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāpsyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 148] 'Ninety <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of heterodox wanderers, mendicants, and <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetics will come here. They will engage in debate with me. I will teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the pacification of all their disputes. And all those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> will generate the mind [set upon] unsurpassed perfect awakening. Ninety <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of heterodox wanderers, mendicants, and <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetics will all attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>).'

body.text: [SaSū 149] aṣṭādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi nāgarājñāmāgamiṣyanti / ye mamāntikāddharmaṃ śroṣyanti / śrutvā ca (tā) sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 149] 'Eighteen <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>nāga</s> kings will come, who will hear the <s>Dharma</s> from me. And having heard, they will all generate the mind [set upon] unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 150] ṣaṣṭi koṭīsahasrāni śuddhāvāsakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāmāgamiṣyanti / dvātriṃśadbhiḥ koṭīsahasrairmāraḥ pāpīyān saparivāra āyāsyati / dvādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi asurarājñāmāgamiṣyanti / paṃcamātrāṇi (ca) rājaśatāni saparivārāṇyāyāsyanti dharmaśravaṇāya / te sarve mamāntikāddharmaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayiṣyanti //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 150] 'Sixty <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) <s>devaputras</s> will come. <s>Māra</s> the Evil One will come with his retinue of thirty-two <s>koṭi</s>-thousands. Twelve <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>asura</s> kings will come. And approximately five hundred kings with their retinues will come for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. They will all, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from me, generate the mind [set upon] unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: [SaSū 151] atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ (tṛṣ) pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā tatraivāntardhitataḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 151] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulating the Blessed One (three times), vanished right there.

body.text: III. sarvaśūraparipṛcchā (2)
body.translated_text: III. The Second Inquiry of <s>Sarvaśūra</s> (<s>Sarvaśūraparipṛcchā</s>)

body.text: [SaSū 152] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat - kinnāmo bhagavan paṃcamātrāṇi rājaśatāni /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 152] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What are the names, Blessed One, of the approximately five hundred kings?'

body.text: [SaSū 153] bhagavān āha - śṛṇu sarvaśūra nado nāma rājā sunando nāma rājā / upanando nāma rājā / jinarṣabho nāma rājā / brahmaseno nāma rājā / brahmaghoṣo nāma rājā / sudarśano nāma rājā / jayaseno nāma rājā / nandaseno nāma rājā / biṃbisāro nāma rājā / prasenajinnāma rājā / virūḍhako nāma rājā / evaṃpramukhāni paṃcamātrāṇi rājaśatāni / ekaiko rāja viṃśatikoṭīsahasraparivāraḥ te sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ sthāpayitvā rājā virūḍhakaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 153] The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>. There is a king named <s>Nada</s>, a king named <s>Sunanda</s>, a king named <s>Upananda</s>, a king named <s>Jinarṣabha</s>, a king named <s>Brahmasena</s>, a king named <s>Brahmaghoṣa</s>, a king named <s>Sudarśana</s>, a king named <s>Jayasena</s>, a king named <s>Nandasena</s>, a king named <s>Bimbisāra</s>, a king named <s>Prasenajit</s>, a king named <s>Virūḍhaka</s> — headed by these, approximately five hundred kings. Each king has a retinue of twenty <s>koṭi</s>-thousands. They have all set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, except King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 154] pūrvasyān diśi tṛṃśatkoṭīsahasrāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / (dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśāyāṃ paṃcāśatkoṭīsahasrāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti; paścimāyān diśāyāṃ ṣaṣṭi koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti /) uttarasyān diśi aśīti koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvānām āgacchanti / adhastāddiśi navati koṭīsahasrāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / ūrdhvāyān diśi śata koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / sarve ca daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitāḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 154] From the eastern direction, thirty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come. (From the southern direction, fifty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come. From the western direction, sixty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come.) From the northern direction, eighty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come. From the downward direction, ninety thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come. From the upward direction, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> come. And all are established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).

body.text: [SaSū 155] atha te sarve bodhisattvā yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yena ca gṛddhrakūṭaparvato yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntā bhagavato darśanāya (;vandanāya) / sarve ca te bodhisattvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃprasthitāḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 155] Then all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, <s>Gṛddhrakūṭa</s> mountain, and the Blessed One—for the seeing (and honoring) of the Blessed One. And all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> had set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: [SaSū 156] atha khalu bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati (sma;) gaccha tvaṃ sarvaśūra daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu bodhisattvānāṃ evaṃ vada / adya tathāgato rājagṛhe mahānagare dharman deśayati / tadyūyaṃ sarve daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu sthitā añjalīn praṇāmayatha; anuśrāvya ca muhūrtamātreṇa ca punarevāgaccha dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 156] Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: 'Go, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, to the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all world-realms in the ten directions and say thus: "Today the <s>Tathāgata</s> is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Therefore, all of you established in the world-realms of the ten directions, join your palms [in reverence]." And having proclaimed this, return in merely a moment for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 157] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ (tṛṣ) pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ṛddhibalenāntardhitaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 157] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, rising from his seat, bowing his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulating the Blessed One (three times), disappeared by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous ability).

body.text: [SaSū 158] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gatvā bodhisattvānāmārocayati / adya mārṣā śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau rājagṛhe mahānagare sattvānān dharmaṃ deśayati / tadyūyaṃ sādhukāramanuprayacchath; tadyuṣmākamadyaiva hitāya sukhāya mahālābho bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 158] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having gone to the world-realms in the ten directions, announced to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>: 'Today, venerable ones, <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Therefore, give your approval! Today itself there will be great gain for your benefit and happiness.'

body.text: [SaSū 159] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gatvā sarvabuddhān paryupāsya bodhisattvānāmārocayati / tadyathāpi nāma balavān puruṣo cchaṭāsaṃghāṭaṃ kuryādatrāntare sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yena ca bhagavāṃstenāgatya bhagavataḥ purata sthitaḥ tatra ca sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthā sannipatitāḥ bahavaśca devanāgamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ paṃcamātrāṇi ca rājaśatāni saparivārāṇi sannipatitāni / trayastriṃśatkoṭīsahasrāṇi mārāṇāṃ pāpīyasāṃ saparivārāḥ sannipatitā /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 159] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having gone to the world-realms in the ten directions, having attended upon all the <s>Buddhas</s>, announced to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Just as a strong man might snap his fingers—in that interval, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having come to the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and the Blessed One, stood before the Blessed One. And there all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other-sectarian wanderers, <s>cārakas</s>, <s>parivrājakas</s>, and <s>nirgranthas</s> had assembled, and many gods, <s>nāgas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and five hundred kings with their retinues had assembled. And thirty-three thousand <s>koṭis</s> of evil <s>Māras</s> with their retinues had assembled.

body.text: [SaSū 160] atha khalu punaḥ tena samayena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ prakaṃpitam atha khalu daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣi divyaṃ candanacūrṇaṃ pravarṣitaṃ / divyaṃ ca puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣitaṃ / tad bhagavato mūrdhasandhau kūṭāgāraḥ saṃsthitaḥ tena khalu punaḥ samayena tathāgatasya purataḥ śakro devānāmindro vajraṃ parāhanat
body.translated_text: [SaSū 160] Then at that time, the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> trembled. Then in the world-realms of the ten directions, divine sandalwood powder rained down, and divine flower-rain rained down. A mansion appeared at the crown-joint of the Blessed One. And at that time, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, struck his <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) before the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: [SaSū 161] atha khalu tasmin samaye caturdiśaṃ catvāro vātarājanaḥ saṃkṣubdhāḥ pravānti / yena ca rājagṛhe mahānagare saṃkarā vā paṃsavo vā bālikā vā tatsarvaṃ nagarādbahiḥ prakṣipanti / daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gandhodakavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti / daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣūtpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāni pravarṣanti / te ca puṣpāsteṣāṃ sattvānāmuparimurdhni puṣpacchatrāṇi tasthire / tathāgatasya coparimurdhni uparyantarīkṣe caturaśītiḥ kūṭāgārasahasrāṇi saṃsthitāni / teṣu ca caturaśītiṣu puṣpakūṭāgārasahasreṣu caturaśīti sahasrāṇyāsanānāṃ prajñaptāni saptaratnamayāni prādurbhūtāni / sarvatra cāsane tathāgato niṣaṇṇo dharman deśayati / atha khalvayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitaḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 161] Then at that time, the four wind-kings in the four directions were agitated and blew, casting out all the refuse, dust, and sand from the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. In the world-realms of the ten directions, rain of fragrant water fell. In the world-realms of the ten directions, blue lotuses, red lotuses, white lotuses, and white water-lilies rained down. And those flowers stood as flower-canopies above the heads of those beings. And above the crown of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the upper sky, eighty-four thousand mansions appeared. And in those eighty-four thousand flower-mansions, eighty-four thousand seats were prepared, made of the seven precious substances, and appeared. And on every seat, a <s>Tathāgata</s> sat teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Then this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) realm trembled in six ways.

body.text: [SaSū 162] atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadimānyevaṃrūpāṇi rājagṛhe mahānagare prātihāryāṇi; sandṛśyante / bhagavān āha - tadyathā kaścideva puruṣaḥ syāccañcalaścapalo 'haṃkāramamakārasthitaḥ sa ca daridro bhavet tasya rājā śīrṣaṃ parimārjayedatha sa puruṣo 'dhimānādyāvādrājadvāraṃ gatvā balasā taṃ rājakulaṃ praveṣṭuṃ icchedatha te rājāmātyapārṣadyāstaṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhṇīyurbahubhiśca prakāraistāḍayeyur
body.translated_text: [SaSū 162] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that such miraculous displays are seen in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Just as there might be a certain man—fickle, restless, established in ego and possessiveness—and he might be poor. If the king were to pat his head, then that man, out of conceit, going as far as the palace gate, would wish to enter the royal household by force. Then the king's ministers and courtiers would seize that man and strike him in many ways.'

body.text: [SaSū 163] atha tena kālena tena samayena sa rājā śṛṇuyād etaṃ prakṛtiṃ sa daridrapuruṣo balasābhyantaraṃ praveṣṭukāma iti / śrutvā cāsyaivaṃ bhaved avaśyamayaṃ mama ghātayitukāmaḥ tataḥ sa rājā ruṣṭastān pārṣadyānevaṃ vaded gacchantu bhavanta etaṃ puruṣaṃ parvatavivaraṃ nītvā jīvitādvyaparopayatha; sarvaparivāraṃ mātāpitṛputraduhitṛdāsīdāsakarmakarāṇāṃ ca vyasanamāpādayatha / atha te sarve jīvitādvyavaropitāḥ tasya (ca) sarve svajanabandhuvargāḥ paramaśokaśalyasamarpitā bhaveyuḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 163] 'Then at that time, at that moment, the king would hear this news: that the poor man wishes to enter the interior by force. And having heard, this thought would arise in him: surely this man wishes to kill me. Then the king, angered, would say to the courtiers: go, sirs, take this man to a mountain gorge and deprive him of life; and bring ruin upon his entire retinue—mother, father, sons, daughters, servants, slaves, and workers. Then they would all be deprived of life. And all his relatives and kin would be pierced with the utmost arrow of grief.'

body.text: [SaSū 164] evameva sarvaśūra tathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sattvānān dharman deśayati / tatra yathā sa puruṣo 'dhimānika evaṃ bālapṛthagjanāstathāgataṃ rūpavarṇaliṃgasaṃsthānato nimittamudgṛhya tathāgatakāyamiti saṃjānanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 164] 'Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Therein, just as that man is conceited, so too foolish ordinary beings, grasping at the sign of the <s>Tathāgata</s> based on form, color, mark, and shape, perceive [it as] the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 165] tatra te bahūn dharmaṃcchrutvādhimāne patanti nānāpralāpān pralapanti / ahaṃkāramamakāreṇābhibhūtāḥ (sattvāḥ) svayameva dharmaṃ na śṛṇvanti na prakāśayanti / yaḥ kaścit sūtraṃ vā gāthāṃ vāntaśo dṛṣṭāntaṃ vā teṣāṃ ārocayati / tatte na gṛhṇanti na śrotramavadadhanti / vayaṃ svayaṃ jānīmaha iti / tatkasya hetoryathāpīdamadhimānatvātte ca bāhuśrutyena pramādamāpadyante /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 165] 'Then, having heard many <s>dharmas</s>, they fall into conceit and prattle various nonsense. (Beings) overcome by ego and possessiveness do not themselves hear the <s>Dharma</s> nor do they reveal it. When someone proclaims to them a <s>sūtra</s>, a verse, or even a parable, they do not accept it, they do not lend an ear: "We ourselves know!" they say. Why is that? Because of their conceit. And they become heedless because of their [supposed] learning.'

body.text: [SaSū 166] ye bālapṛthagjanaiḥ sārdhaṃ samavadhānaṃ kurvanti / na te tathārūpaṃ dharmopasaṃhitaṃ vacanaṃ śroṣyanti / tettena bāhuśrutyena pramattā bhaviṣyanti / te tathārūpāḥ puruṣāḥ svakāvyāni sthāpayanti / svagranthāni dānāni sthāpayanti / te sarvalokaṃ cātmānaṃ ca visaṃpādayanti / vyarthaṃ ca rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ prabhūtaṃ paribhokṣyanti / bhuktvā ca na samyak pariṇamayiṣyaṃti / maraṇakālasamaye ca teṣāṃ mahāsantrāso bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 166] 'Those who keep company with foolish ordinary beings will not hear such <s>dharma</s>-connected words. They will become heedless because of their [supposed] learning. Such men establish their own compositions. They establish their own treatises and donations. They ruin the entire world and themselves. And they will wastefully consume abundant food of the kingdom. And having consumed it, they will not properly digest it. And at the time of death, great terror will arise in them.'

body.text: [SaSū 167] te ca sattvāstaṃ vakṣyanti / bahavastvayā vayaṃ śilpajñānaṃ śikṣāpitāḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ svamātmānaṃ na śaknuṣe parisaṃsthāpayituṃ / sa teṣāṃ evaṃ vadenna śakyaṃ mārṣā idānīmātmānaṃ parisaṃsthāpayituṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 167] 'And those beings will say to him: "You have taught many of us various crafts and knowledge; how is it that you cannot establish yourself?" He will say to them thus: "It is not possible, venerable ones, to establish oneself now."'

body.text: [SaSū 168] tatra te sattvā(stasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā) nānāprakāraṃ paridevayiṣyanti / yathā tasyaikapudgalasyarthena bahavo jñatṛsaṃghā jīvitādvyavaropitā anaparādhinaḥ svakarmapratyayena / evameva te sattvā maraṇakālasamaye teṣāṃ paridevatāṃ narakatiryagyoniparāyaṇaṃ ātmānaṃ samanupaśyantaḥ akalyāṇamitrahetoḥ evameva yuṣmākaṃ brāhmaṇānāmanyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānāmevaṃ vadāmi / mā yūyaṃ pramattā bhavathaḥ tadyathāpināmājātapakṣaḥ śakunirna śaknotyākāśe prakramituṃ devalokagamanāya / evameva yuṣmābhir(ahaṃkāramamakārasthitair)na śakyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ anuprāptuṃ na yuṣmākaṃ tathā ṛddhiḥ saṃvidyate / tatkasya hetoḥ karmaprakaraṇena yūyaṃ kukkuṭayonyā ivotpannāḥ na cireṇāyaṃ kāyo bhedanadharmā maraṇaparyavasāno bhaviṣyati / maraṇakālasamaye nirāsvādanatā paritasyanatā ca bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 168] Then those beings, having heard what was spoken (by him), will lament in various ways. Just as by the actions of that one person, many assemblies of kinsmen were deprived of life, though they were innocent, each by the condition of their own <s>karma</s>; even so, those beings at the time of death, seeing themselves as destined for the realms of hell and animal rebirth while lamenting for them, due to unwholesome companions — in the same way I say this to you, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, and <s>nirgranthas</s>: do not be heedless! Just as a bird whose wings have not yet grown cannot fly into the sky to reach the world of the gods, even so, for you who remain established in ego-clinging (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>), it is not possible to attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — you do not possess such supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). For what reason? By the workings of <s>karma</s>, you have been born as if in the womb of a hen. Before long, this body will be subject to the law of dissolution, ending in death. At the time of death, there will be tastelessness and anguish.

body.text: [SaSū 169] kimayaṃ asmābhirātmabhāvaḥ sandhārito ye vayaṃ na devasukhaṃ na manuṣyalokasukhaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyāma / nāpi nirvāṇapadasthā bhaviṣyāma; nirarthakamasmābhiḥ śarīramudbūḍhaṃ / kā gatirasmābhiḥ kaḥ parāyaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / kutropapattiḥ kutra (vā) nirodho bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 169] 'Why have we maintained this bodily existence, when we shall experience neither the happiness of gods nor the happiness of the human world? Nor shall we be established in the state of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; our bodies have been borne in vain! What is our destination? What will be our final goal? Where will our rebirth be? Where will our cessation be?'

body.text: [SaSū 170] atha (khalu) bhagavāṃs(punarapi) teṣāṃ anyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇānamantrayati / mā yūyaṃ mārṣā ratnamayājjaṃbūdvīpānnirāśā bhaviṣyadhve; mā yāyaṃ dharmaratnāt paribāhyā bhaviṣyatheti / pṛcchatha yūyaṃ mārṣāstathāgataṃ yadyadevākāṃkṣathāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ sarvābhiprāyān paripūrayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 170] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again addressed those other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: 'Do not, good sirs, become hopeless regarding this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> made of jewels! Do not become excluded from the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>! Ask, good sirs, the <s>Tathāgata</s> whatever you wish — I shall fulfill all your intentions.'

body.text: [SaSū 171] atha khalu te sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthā utthāyāsanebhyaḥ ekāṃsāni cīvarāṇi pravṛtyāṃjalayaḥ pragṛhya bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti (sma) / bahūni bhagavaṃ sattvāni rātrindivastathāgataḥ saṃsārā parimocayati / na ca sattvadhātorūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ yatte sattvā samānā utpādanirodhaṃ darśayanti //0//
body.translated_text: [SaSū 171] Then all those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, and <s>nirgranthas</s> rose from their seats, arranged their robes over one shoulder, and with palms joined together, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Many beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s> liberate from <s>saṃsāra</s> day and night. Yet neither decrease nor increase of the realm of beings is perceived. What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause? What is the condition, that those beings, being equal, display arising and cessation?'

body.text: (saṃghāṭe mahādharmaparyāye sarvaśūraparipṛcchā samāptā //0 // //)//
body.translated_text: (In the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> great <s>Dharma</s> discourse, the inquiry of <s>Sarvaśūra</s> is concluded.)

body.text: IV. bhaiṣajyasenaparipṛcchā /
body.translated_text: IV. The Inquiry of <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>

body.text: [SaSū 172] tatra khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati sma / mahāsannāhaṃ sannahyanti tīrthyā / mahākaukṛtyavinodanārthāya / mahādharmolkājvālanāya / mahāpraśnanidānaṃ paripṛcchanti / (śṛṇutha yūyaṃ kulaputrā ihānantāparyanta pṛthivīdhāturabdhātustejodhāturvāyudhāturato nāṃtataraḥ sattvadhātuḥ santi ca sattvāḥ ye sattvahitārthamutpādanirodhaṃ darśayaṃti) paścime tu kāle bhaviṣyanti daharā sattvā vṛddhā vā ye utpādanirodhaṃ kariṣyanti / santi bhaiṣajyasena vṛddhā sattvā daharā iva na kiṃcijjānanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 172] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'The <s>tīrthikas</s> gird themselves with great armor, for the purpose of dispelling great remorse, for the blazing of the great torch of <s>Dharma</s>, and they ask questions of great import. Listen, sons of good family: here the realm of earth, the realm of water, the realm of fire, and the realm of wind are infinite and boundless — the realm of beings is no less than these. And there are beings who display arising and cessation for the benefit of beings. But in the future age, there will be young (<s>dahara</s>) beings and old (<s>vṛddha</s>) beings who will manifest arising and cessation. There are, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, old beings who are like the young — they know nothing at all.'

body.text: [SaSū 173] tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyasena kaścideva puruṣaḥ śiraṃ śocayeta navakāni ca vastrāṇi pravṛṇuyāt sa ca gṛhādbahirniṣkrameta / tamenaṃ sattvā āmantrayanti / suprāvṛtāni te navakāni vastrāṇīti / atha kaścidevāparaḥ sattvo bhavet sa śiraḥ śocayeta purāṇakāni ca vastrāṇi (śocayitvā) prāvṛṇuyāt tāni ca śithilakāni bhavanti na ca śobhante / sa ca puruṣaḥ susnātaśirā bhavati vastraṃ cāsya na śobhate / evameva bhaiṣajyasena saṃti vṛddhā sattvā ye jaṃbūdvīpaṃ na śobhayanti / daharāstu sattvā utpādanirodhaṃ darśayanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 173] 'Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a certain man were to wash his head and put on new garments, and then go out from his house. Other beings would address him: "Your new garments are well-worn!" Now suppose another being were to wash his head and, having cleaned old garments, put them on — but they are loose-fitting and do not look beautiful. That man has a well-washed head, yet his garments do not look beautiful. Even so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there are old beings who do not adorn <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. But the young beings display arising and cessation.'

body.text: [SaSū 174] atha khalu te sarve 'nyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇā utthāyasanād bhagavantametadavocan - ko bhagavannasmākaṃ vṛddho vā daharo vā bhagavān āha - vṛddhā yūyaṃ punaḥ punarnarakatiryakpreteṣu duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ dṛṣṭvā tadadyāpi yūyaṃ tṛptiṃ nādhigacchatha;
body.translated_text: [SaSū 174] Then all those other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> rose from their seats and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Who among us, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is old and who is young?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You are the old ones. Again and again, having seen painful feelings in the hells, animal realms, and <s>preta</s> realms, even today you have not attained satisfaction.'

body.text: [SaSū 175] atha khalu te sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthāḥ sarve ca nāgarājāno bhagavantametadavocan - na bhūyo bhagavannutsahāma saṃsāre duḥkhāṃ vedanāmanubhavituṃ te cānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇā evamāhuḥ na santi daharā sattvā ye śaknuyurdharmatāṃ sākṣāt kartum //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 175] Then all those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and all the <s>Nāga</s> kings said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We are no longer able, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to endure painful feelings in <s>saṃsāra</s>.' And those other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> said: 'There are no young beings who are able to directly realize the true nature of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>).'

body.text: [SaSū 176] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - paśya bhadanta bhagavan kiyadduradhimocyā ime sattvāḥ bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena saṃprataṃ tathāgataḥ sarvalokapratyakṣaṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 176] Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Behold, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, how exceedingly difficult to inspire faith in are these beings!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> shall now make it visible to all the world.'

body.text: [SaSū 177] atha khalu catunavati koṭīsahasrāṇi navakānāṃ sattvānāṃ te tathāgatasya purataḥ sthitāḥ na ca tathāgataṃ bandanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti / tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadete sattvā bhagavantaṃ nālapanti na saṃlapanti na vandanti na ca bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena ye sattvā evaṃ vadanti na śakyaṃ navakaiḥ sattvairdharmatā sākṣāt kartum // ta ete bhaiṣajyasena navakāḥ sattvā yuṣmābhirdraṣṭavyāḥ te ca sattvā evaṃ āhurvayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan navakāḥ sattvā vayaṃ bhadanta sugata navakāḥ sattvā / bhagavān āha - eṣāṃ bho sattvānāṃ lokapratyakṣaṃ sāṃprataṃ svaśarīrāllokasya pramānaṃ darśayatha /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 177] Then ninety-four <s>koṭī</s>-thousands of young (<s>navaka</s>) beings stood before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, yet they did not salute the <s>Tathāgata</s>, did not speak to him, did not converse with him — they remained in silence. Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause? What is the condition that these beings do not speak to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, do not converse with him, do not salute him, and do not question the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> — those beings who say "It is not possible for young beings to directly realize the true nature of <s>Dharma</s>" — these, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are the young beings whom you should behold. And those beings spoke thus: "We, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, are young beings; we, Venerable <s>Sugata</s>, are young beings."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'O beings, now display from your own bodies the proof for the world, visible to all.'

body.text: [SaSū 178] tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena caturnavati koṭīsahasrāṇi navakānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāyasya bhedādantarikṣe sthitvā daśabhūmipratilabdhā abhūvan atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - sulabdhā lābhā bhagavannīdṛśāḥ sattvāḥ ye saṃsāre parikṣayāya paryadānāya vīryamārabhante / adyaiva bhagavannime sattvā utpannāḥ adyaiva bhagavannime sattvāḥ parimuktāḥ (adyaiva) sarve daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā dṛṣṭāḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 178] Then at that time, ninety-four <s>koṭī</s>-thousands of young (<s>navaka</s>) beings, upon the dissolution of their bodies, stood in mid-air and were found to have attained the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Well-gained are the gains, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of such beings who strive with vigor for the exhaustion and ending of <s>saṃsāra</s>! This very day, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these beings have arisen; this very day, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these beings are liberated; this very day they are all seen to be established in the ten <s>bhūmis</s>!'

body.text: [SaSū 179] atha khalu sarvabrāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthā nāgarājāno 'pi mārāśca pāpīyānaṃ saparivāraṃ upasaṃkrāntaṃ vicakṣuṣkaraṇāya; sarve ca te bhagavantametadavocanniha vayaṃ bhagavan tathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkrāntā vicakṣuṣkaraṇāya / te vayaṃ bhagavanniman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā prasādapratilabdhā abhūvan buddhe ca dharme ca / tatrāsmākaṃ bhagavan sarveṣāṃ evaṃ bhagavatyevaṃrūpaṃ buddhasukhaṃ pratilabhema; // evaṃrūpāśca tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loke bhavema;
body.translated_text: [SaSū 179] Then all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> kings, and even <s>Māra</s> the Evil One together with his retinue had approached for the purpose of gaining clear sight. And they all said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here we have approached the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the purpose of gaining clear sight. Having heard this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we have obtained faith in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>. May we all, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, obtain such <s>Buddha</s>-happiness in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>! And may we become such <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the world!'

body.text: [SaSū 180] bhagavān āhaivametadbhadramukhā evametadyathā yūyaṃ tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikamupasaṃkrāntāḥ tairyuṣmābhirimaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ (sūtraṃ) dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheścittānyutpāditāni / tena yūyaṃ bhadramukhāḥ kuśalamūlena na cireṇa kālenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyadhve / atha samantarabhāṣitā ca bhagavateyaṃ vāg
body.translated_text: [SaSū 180] The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, O fair-faced ones, so it is! Just as you have approached the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> <s>Dharma</s> discourse, you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). By that wholesome root (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), O fair-faced ones, you shall, before long, fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.' And simultaneously this word was spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: [SaSū 181] atha tāvadeva teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇānāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipraitlabdho 'bhūvat sarve ca daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisattvāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ sarve ca te bodhisattvā uparyantarīkṣe sapta tālān vaihāyasamabhyudgamya saptaratnamayāni kūṭāgārāṇi tathāgatasyopanāmayanti / sarve ca nānāvikurvādhiṣṭhānardhyabhisaṃkārān abhisaṃskurvanti / atha tāvadeva te sarve bhagavata uparimūrdhni sthitvā bhagavantaṃ nānāpuṣpairabhyavakiranti / tathāgatāṃśca manasi kurvanti / svakāye ca buddhasaṃjñāmutpādayantyanekāni ca devaputrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi (divyapuṣp[SaSū ai]s) tathāgatamabhyavakiranti (smaḥ) /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 181] Then, at that very moment, all of those non-Buddhist wanderers, mendicants, ascetics, <s>Nirgrantha</s> Jains, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> obtained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). And they all became <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). And all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, rising seven palm-tree heights into the sky above, offered pavilions made of the seven precious substances to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And they all performed various miraculous transformations and displays of supernatural power. Then, at that very moment, all of them, standing above the head of the Blessed One, showered the Blessed One with various flowers. And they contemplated the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And they generated the perception of a <s>Buddha</s> with regard to their own bodies. And countless <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) showered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with (divine flowers).

body.text: [SaSū 182] evaṃ ca vācamabhāśanta; mahālābhaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ mahākṣetraṃ lokanāthaḥ samādhibalādhānaprāptaḥ vijño vijñārthikaḥ yaḥ īdṛśān sattvān saṃsārādanupūrveṇopāyakauśalyena parimocayatyekena subhāṣitamātreṇa etāvanti sattvāni saṃsārāt parimucyante //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 182] And they spoke these words: 'Great is the gain! The <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> is a great field! The Protector of the World has attained the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — wise, seeking the wise — who liberates such beings from <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) progressively through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>)! By a single well-spoken word alone, so many beings are liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>!'

body.text: [SaSū 183] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo ya eta devaputrā evaṃ vānniścārayanti / bahūni cardhyabhisaṃskāraṃ kurvanti / bahubhiśca guṇavarṇastavaistathāgatamabhistavanti sma / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu kulaputra na hi te māṃ stunvanti / svakāyameva stunvanti / svakāyameva dharmarājāsane sthāpayiṣyanti / svakāyamevagradharmāsane pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyanti / svakāyādeva dharmaraśmin niścārayiṣyanti / sarvabuddhaparigṛhītāśca bhaviṣyantyanuttarāsyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherabhisaṃbodhāyābhisaṃbudhya ca dharman deśayiṣyanti (ca) //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 183] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that these <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) utter such words, perform many miraculous displays, and praise the <s>Tathāgata</s> with many laudatory praises of qualities?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, son of good family. They do not praise me — they praise their own bodies. They will establish their own bodies on the throne of a <s>Dharma</s>-king. They will set their own bodies on the throne of the supreme <s>Dharma</s>. From their own bodies they will emit rays of <s>Dharma</s>. And they will be embraced by all <s>Buddhas</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, and will teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 184] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - bahavo bhadanta bhagavan sattvāḥ bahavo bhadanta sugataḥ sattvā rātrindivaṃ parimucyante tadadyāpi sattvānāṃ kṣayo na bhavati / bhagavān āha - sādhu sādhu bhaiṣajyasena yastvaṃ tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyasena kaścideva puruṣo bhavedāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ prabhūtabhogaḥ bahudhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamanvāgataḥ bahudāsadāsīkarmakarapauruṣeyāni cāsya syuḥ bahūni ca dhanaskandhāni bhaveyuḥ bahūni ca kṣetrārāmāṇi saṃvidyeran bahūni ca dhanadhānyāni / tadyathā yavagodhumaśālitilamāṣamudgādīni sa ca puruṣo vasantakāle sarvāni tāni dhanadhānyāni vāpayeta / atha yāvadapareṇa kālasamayena sarvāṇi tāni dhanadhānyāni paripadyaran sa paripakvānīti viditvā sa yāvadabhyantaragṛhe praveśayeta; sa puruṣastāni dhanadhānyāni gṛhasyābhyantare pṛthak pṛthak sthāpayati / sthāpayitvā paribhuṃkte / yāvadvasantakāle (samaye) punareva tāni bījāni vāpayati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 184] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Many, venerable Blessed One, are the beings — many, venerable <s>Sugata</s>, are the beings — who are liberated day and night. Yet even now there is no diminishment of beings.' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, that you consider this matter worthy of asking the <s>Tathāgata</s>! Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! Just as, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there might be a certain man — wealthy, of great riches, of great enjoyments, of abundant possessions, endowed with much grain and many granaries and storehouses, having many male and female servants and hired workers, having many stores of wealth, having many fields and gardens, and having much grain and produce — such as barley, wheat, rice, sesame, black gram, mung beans, and the like — and that man in the spring season were to sow all those grains and produce. Then, after some time, when all those grains and produce would ripen, knowing them to be ripe, he would bring them inside the house. That man would store those grains separately within the house; having stored them, he would consume them. Then in the spring season he would sow those seeds again.'

body.text: [SaSū 185] evameva bhaiṣajyasena ime sattvāḥ pūrvaṃ śubhaṃ karma kṛtvā paścāt teṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ parikṣayāt punaḥ punarapi puṇyakṣetrameṣante kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti / kuśalamūlānyavaropayitvā tatra ca kuśaladharme pratipatya saṃpādayanti / pratipattisaṃpannā sarvadharmān vardhayanti / sarvadharmān vardhayitvā prītiprāmodyamutpādayanti / tena ca prītiprāmodyacittena bhaiṣajyasenānekāni kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi na nāśyante / evameva bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvo na kadācid vināśadharmā bhavati / saṃkṣiptena sarvadharmān prajānāti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 185] 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these beings, having previously performed wholesome <s>karma</s>, and then, after the exhaustion of those <s>karmas</s>, again and again seek the field of merit and plant wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). Having planted wholesome roots, they practice in that wholesome <s>Dharma</s> and accomplish it. Accomplished in practice, they increase all <s>dharmas</s>. Having increased all <s>dharmas</s>, they generate joy and delight. And through that mind of joy and delight, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they are not destroyed for many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the [awakening] mind is never subject to destruction. In brief, he knows all <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 186] āha / kathaṃ bhagavan prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati / bhagavān āha / bahūni bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati / tatkasya hetoryadā svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati / tadā sarvapāpakāni karmāṇi pariśodhayati / na śakyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena pāpakarmaṇā sattvena tīvraṃ duḥkhamapanayituṃ na ca pāpena svapnena dṛṣṭenāsya bhayaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 186] [<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>] said: 'How, Blessed One, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the [awakening] mind see dreams?' The Blessed One said: 'Many fearful things, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind see in his dreams. For what reason? When he sees fearful things in his dreams, at that time he purifies all evil <s>karmas</s>. It is not possible, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for a being with evil <s>karma</s> to remove intense suffering. But from an evil dream that is seen, no fear arises for him.'

body.text: [SaSū 187] bhaiṣajyasena āha - katamāni bhagavan prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati / bhagavān āha - agniṃ bhaiṣajyasena prajvalitaṃ paśyati / tatra tena bodhisattvenaivaṃ cittaṃ utpādayitavyaṃ sarvakleśāni me dagdhāḥ dvitīyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena udakaṃ paśyati luḍitaṃ saṃpraluḍitaṃ / tatra tena prathamacittotpādikena bodhisattvena na bhettavyaṃ / tatkasya hetoḥ evaṃ hi bhaiṣajyasena bodhisattvena sarvamohabandhanāni vinivartya sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati / tṛtīyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati mahābhayaṃ / āha - katamaṃ bhagavan
body.translated_text: [SaSū 187] <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said: 'What fearful things, Blessed One, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind see in his dreams?' The Blessed One said: 'He sees blazing fire, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. Therein, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> should generate the thought: "All my <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) have been burned!" Second, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, he sees water — agitated, greatly agitated. Therein, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind should not be frightened. For what reason? For thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned away all the bonds of delusion, accomplishes the exhaustion of all evil. Third, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind sees a great fear in his dream.' He said: 'What [is it], Blessed One?'

body.text: [SaSū 188] bhagavān āha - svaśarīre śīrṣaṃ muṇḍitaṃ paśyati / tatra tena bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādikena bodhisattvena na bhettavyaṃ tatkasya hetoḥ tenaivaṃ cittamutpādayitavyaṃ rāgadveṣamohāni me muṇḍitāni bhavanti / ṣaḍgatikaṃ ca me saṃsāraṃ parājitaṃ bhaviṣyati / na hi tasya narakāvāso bhaviṣyati / na tiryakṣu na preteṣu (vā) nāsureṣu (vā) na nāgeṣu na deveṣu pariśuddheṣu bhaiṣajyasena buddhakṣetreṣu prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ upapattiṃ pratigṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 188] The Blessed One said: 'He sees his own head shaved. Therein, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should not be frightened. For what reason? He should generate the thought thus: "My <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) have been shaved off. And my <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) of the six realms will be conquered. For him there will be no dwelling in hell, not among animals, not among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), not among <s>asuras</s>, not among <s>nāgas</s>, not among gods. In purified <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind takes birth.'

body.text: [SaSū 189] (bhaviṣyati) bhaiṣajyasena paścime kāle paścime samaye yadi kaścit sattvo bodhau cittaṃ pariṇamayiṣyati / tena mahatī paribhāṣaṇā draṣṭavyā / paribhūtavāsaśca bhaviṣyati / tatra(tena) bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādikena bodhisattvena na parikhedacittamutpādayitavyaṃ na vyavasitavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 189] '<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, in the last time, in the final period, if any being will dedicate his mind to awakening, he should expect to face great reviling. And he will dwell in [a state of] being despised. Therein, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first arising of the mind, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should not generate a mind of weariness nor lose resolve.'

body.text: [SaSū 190] bahavo bhaiṣajyasena mayā dharmā deśitāḥ mayā ca bhaiṣajyasenānekāni kalpaniyutaśatasahasrāni duṣkaracaryā cīrṇā na mayā bhaiṣajyasena rājyabhogārthāya vā vṛttibhogārthāya vā aiśvaryabhogārthāya vā duṣkaracaryā cīrṇāḥ svabhāvadharmāvabodhāya bhaiṣajyasena mayā duṣkaracaryā cīrṇāḥ na ca me tāvadanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā yāvanna mayāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutaḥ yasminstu bhaiṣajyasena kālasamaye mayāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāya śrutaḥ tatraiva me divase anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā gaṃbhīro yaṃ bhaiṣajyasena dharmaparyāyaḥ durlabho 'sya bhaiṣajyasena dharmaparyāyasya kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrairapi śravaḥ paramadurlabho bhaiṣajyasena tathāgatānāmutpādaḥ paramadurlabhā bhaiṣajyasenāsya dharmaparyāyasya dhārakaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 190] 'Many <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, have been taught by me. And I, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, have practiced difficult austerities (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>) for many <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. It was not for the sake of royal enjoyments, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, nor for the sake of livelihood enjoyments, nor for the sake of lordly enjoyments that I practiced difficult austerities. It was for the realization of the inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, that I practiced difficult austerities. And I did not fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening until I heard this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>. But on the very day, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, when I heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharma-paryāya</s>, on that very day I fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Profound, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>. Rare is the hearing of this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, even in <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. Supremely rare, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Supremely rare, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is a holder of this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 191] ye te iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti / sarve te nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante / kalpaśatasahasraṃ bhaiṣajyasena sattvā saṃsārāt paścānmukhaṃ kariṣyanti / pariṣuddhaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ pratilapsyante / nirodhamārgaṃ ca prajñasyanti / bhavyāś ca te niśrayaṃ prajñātuṃ / bhavyāḥ kuśalasthānaṃ prajñatuṃ / bhavyā abhijñākuśalasthānaṃ prajñatum bhavyāḥ kuśalasthānanirodhaṃ prajñātum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 191] 'Those who will hear this <s>dharma-paryāya</s> — they will all awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. For a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, beings will turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s>. And they will obtain a pure <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field). And they will know the path of cessation (<s>nirodha-mārga</s>). And they will be capable of knowing the foundation; capable of knowing the wholesome ground; capable of knowing the ground of the higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); capable of knowing the cessation of the wholesome ground.'

body.text: [SaSū 192] nirodhameva bhaiṣajyasena kimarthamucyate / āha / artha ucyate bhagavan dharmasthānam bhagavānāha - katamaṃ bhaiṣajyasena dharmasthānaṃ / āha / dharma ucyate bhagavannārabdhavīryatā / ārabdhaśīlatā / śīlasamanvāgamatā dharmanidhānamityucyate / idaṃ bhagavan dharmanidhānaṃ saṃbhavati / bhagavān āha - sādhu sādhu bhaiṣajyasena yas(tvaṃ) tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 192] '<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for what purpose is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) spoken of?' He said: 'The meaning spoken of, Blessed One, is the ground of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharma-sthāna</s>).' The Blessed One said: 'Which, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is the ground of <s>Dharma</s>?' He said: '<s>Dharma</s>, Blessed One, is called the state of exerting vigor, the state of undertaking moral conduct, the endowment with moral conduct — this is called the treasury of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharma-nidhāna</s>). This, Blessed One, is the arising of the <s>Dharma</s> treasury.' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! You who consider this matter worthy of asking the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 193] āha / kena kāreṇana bhagavan tathāgatā loka utpadyante / bhagavān āha - ye bhaiṣajyasena bāhuśrutyasamanvāgamaṃ prajānanti / te tathāgatānāmutpādaṃ prajānanti / te tathāgatānāmutpādaṃ jñātvā idaṃ tathāgatānāmutpādasukhasthānaṃ prajānanti / yadā ca tathāgatā loka utpadyante tadā sattvā sarvadharmān prajānanti / upāyakuśalān dharmān prajānanti / laukikalokottarān dharmān prajānanti / laukikalokottarāṇi jñānāni prajānanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 193] He said: 'For what reason, Blessed One, do <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise in the world?' The Blessed One said: 'Those, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, who understand the endowment of great learning — they understand the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Having known the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they understand: "This is the ground of the happiness of the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>." And when <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise in the world, then beings understand all <s>dharmas</s>; they understand <s>dharmas</s> of skillful means; they understand mundane and supramundane <s>dharmas</s>; they understand mundane and supramundane knowledges.'

body.text: [SaSū 194] āha jñānamevaṃ jñātvā katamaṃ nirvāṇaṃ prajānanti / bhagavānāha - dharmameva bhaiṣajyasena prajānanti / dharmameva jñātvā (evameva) bhaiṣajyasena dharmasaṃgrahaṃ prajānatāṃ prathamo lābha utpadyate / yathāśrutaṃ gṛhya dhārmikameva lābho bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 194] He said: 'Having thus known knowledge, which <s>nirvāṇa</s> do they understand?' The Blessed One said: 'They understand the <s>Dharma</s> itself, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. Having known the <s>Dharma</s> itself — just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> — for those who understand the collection of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharma-saṃgraha</s>), the first gain arises. Having grasped what was heard, the gain will be in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> alone.'

body.text: [SaSū 195] tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyasena kaścideva puruṣo vāṇijako bhavet sa lābhahetorgacchan parakyasvakasya suvarṇasya puruṣabhārasahasraṃ gṛhītvā gacchet tasya gacchatastau mātāpitarāvevamāhutuḥ śṛṇu kulaputra idaṃ suvarṇasya puruṣabhārasahasraṃ gṛhītaṃ parakyasvakasya ca; ta tvayedaṃ suvarṇaṃ sugṛhītaṃ kartavyaṃ na ca kiṃcidato vināśayitavyaṃ mahālābhaṃ kṛtvā suvarṇaṃ eva sugṛhītaṃ kuru tadasmākaṃ mahālābho bhaviṣyati / sukhaṃ ca jīviṣyāmaḥ sa ca putrastau mātāpitarāvevaṃ vadedevaṃ kariṣyāmi / ityuktvā sa vāṇijakaḥ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītvā gacchedatha sa vāṇijakaḥ pramādādyāvan māsamātreṇa sarvaṃ suvarṇaṃ vināśayedvilayaṃ kuryāt
body.translated_text: [SaSū 195] 'Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there were a merchant who, going for the sake of gain, took a thousand man-loads of gold belonging to others and his own, and went. As he was going, his mother and father said to him: "Listen, son of good family — this thousand man-loads of gold has been taken, belonging to others and your own. You must keep this gold well guarded; you must not let any of it be destroyed. Having made a great profit, keep the gold well guarded — that will be a great gain for us, and we shall live happily." And that son said to his mother and father: "So I shall do." Having said this, that merchant, taking the gold, went. But that merchant, through carelessness, within a mere month, destroyed all the gold and caused it to vanish.'

body.text: [SaSū 196] atha sa puruṣaḥ paramacintāmāpannaḥ śokaśalyenāviddhahṛdayaḥ sahrīravatrāpyena ca svagṛhaṃ na paraviśeta; tasya tau mātāpitarau śṛṇuyātāṃ evaṃ yuvābhyāṃ putreṇa tat suvarṇaṃ sarvaṃ vināśitamiti śrutvā nirāśībhūtau śokaśalyenābhyāhatahṛdayau vastrāṇi pāṭayataḥ śocataḥ krandataḥ evaṃ ca paridevataḥ duṣputro 'smākaṃ gṛhe putrarūpeṇotpannaḥ sakalaṃ eva gṛhaṃ vināśītavān asmākamanāthaṃ kṛtvā dāsau karmakarau kṛtau; tasya tau mātāpitarau cintāparigatahṛdayau nirāśau kālagatau tatastena putreṇa śrutaṃ matāpitarau me nirāśau kālagatau; so 'pi putro nirāśa eva kālagataḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 196] 'Then that man, having fallen into extreme anxiety, with a heart pierced by the arrow of grief, through shame and embarrassment would not enter his own home. His mother and father would hear: "Thus your son has destroyed all that gold." Having heard, they became despairing, with hearts struck by the arrow of grief, tearing their clothes, lamenting, weeping, and wailing thus: "A wicked son was born in our house in the form of a son; he has destroyed the entire household, made us destitute, and made us into slaves and servants." Those mother and father, with hearts overcome by anxiety, despairing, died. Then that son heard: "My mother and father, despairing, have died." That son too, despairing, died.'

body.text: [SaSū 197] evameva bhaiṣajyasena tathāgato 'pyetamarthaṃ bhāṣate / ye sattvā mama śasane na prasīdanti te nirāśībhūtā maraṇakālasamaye śokaśalyābhyāhatahṛdayā mahādharmaratnabahiṣkṛtāḥ kālaṃ kurvanti / yathā tau mātāpitarau nirāśau śocataḥ paridevataḥ suvarṇahetoḥ śokaśalyābhyāhatahṛdayau parakyasvakena suvarṇena śokaśalyaparigatau cintāmāpadya kālagatauḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 197] 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks of this matter. Those beings who do not have faith in my teaching — they become despairing, and at the time of death, with hearts struck by the arrow of grief, excluded from the great <s>Dharma</s> treasure, they die. Just as those mother and father, despairing, lamenting, weeping on account of the gold, with hearts struck by the arrow of grief — on account of the gold belonging to others and themselves, overcome by the arrow of grief, having fallen into anxiety, they died.'

body.text: [SaSū 198] evameva bhaiṣajyasena ye mama śasane na prasīdante paścān maraṇakālasamaye paritapyamānāḥ paridevanto duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti / pūrvakṛtāni ca puṇyāni paribhuktvā na bhūyo 'nyāni puṇyāni kurvanti sukṣetragatāni / tatra teṣāṃ puṇyaparikṣīṇānāṃ śokaśalyaparigatahṛdayānāṃ tena kālena tena samayena narakatiryagyoniyamalokopapattiṃ ghorāṃ dāruṇān dṛṣṭvā maraṇakālasamaye evaṃ bhavati / ko me trātā bhavedyadahaṃ naraka (gati) tiryakpretayamalokaviṣayaṃ na paśyeyan na ca tāṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 198] 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those who do not have faith in my teaching — afterward, at the time of death, burning, lamenting, they experience painful sensations. And having enjoyed the merit previously made, they do not make any further merit planted in a good field. Then, when their merit is exhausted, with hearts overcome by the arrow of grief, at that time, at that moment, seeing the terrifying and dreadful rebirth in the hells, animal realms, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>, at the time of death they think: "Who could be my savior, so that I would not see the domain of the hells, animal realms, <s>preta</s> realms, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>, and would not experience such painful sensations?"'

body.text: [SaSū 199] tasyaivaṃ pralapataḥ paralokamākramataḥ tau mātāpitarāvevamāhataḥ kiṃ kariṣyāma putraka; gāthābhiścāddhyābhāṣataḥ (54) grahītuṃ śakyate naiva vyādhirduḥkhaṃ mahābhayaṃ / nāsti te maraṇaṃ putra glānasya maraṇādbhayaṃ /
body.translated_text:
[SaSū 199] 'As he thus babbles, passing to the next world, his mother and father say: "What shall we do, dear son?" And they address him with verses:
(54) Disease, suffering, and great fear cannot be grasped [and removed]; there is no [escape from] death for you, son — for the sick one there is fear of death.',

body.text:
(55) mokṣo bhaviṣyate tubhyaṃ vyādherhi bhayabhairavāt
dhṛtiṃ kuruṣva he putra tataḥ siddhirbhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: (55) Liberation will come to you from the fearful terror of disease; take courage, O son — then success will come!

body.text:
putra āha -
(56) niruddhyate me vijñānaṃ kāyo me pīḍyate bhṛśam
sarve aṅgāni duḥkhanti mṛtyuṃ paśyāmi ātmanaḥ
(57) na paśyataścakṣuṣī me karṇau me na śṛṇonti ca /
śrotraṃ punarna lapsyāmi na kāyaḥ saṃsahiṣyati /
(58) aṅgamaṃgāni duḥkhanti kāṣṭhā iva acetanāḥ
visvādayasi me amba nāgataṃ maraṇaṃ tava;
body.translated_text:
The son said:
(56) My consciousness is being extinguished; my body is being crushed severely; all my limbs are in pain — I see my own death.
(57) My eyes do not see; my ears do not hear; I will not regain my hearing; my body will not endure.
(58) Limb by limb they are in pain, like logs, devoid of sensation — you taste [grief] for me, mother; death has not yet come for you.

body.text:
mātā āha -
(59) vaktuṃ nārhasi putraivaṃ mā me trāsaparāṃ kuru /
kāyaṃ tava jvarākrāntaṃ viprakārāṇi paśyasi /
body.translated_text:
The mother said:
(59) You should not speak thus, son — do not fill me with terror! Your body is seized by fever; you see distortions.

body.text:
putra āha -
(60) na paśyāmi jvaraṃ kāyerna ca vyādhirna duḥkhati /
paśyāmi maranaṃ ghoraṃ hataṃ kāyaṃ ca me bhṛśam
(61) paśyāmi ātmanā sarvaṃ kāyaṃ duḥkhaprapīḍitaṃ /
gacchāmi kasya śaraṇaṃ ko me trātā bhaviṣyati /
(62) mātāpitā vadet putra devakrodhaṃ hi te bhavet
devebhyo yajanaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ svastirbhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text:
The son said:
(60) I do not see fever in my body, nor disease, nor does it [merely] hurt — I see dreadful death, and my body is severely destroyed.
(61) I see with my own [awareness] my entire body oppressed by suffering; to whom shall I go for refuge? Who will be my savior?
(62) The mother and father say: 'Son, it must be the wrath of a god; having performed worship to the gods, then well-being will come.'

body.text:
putrā āha -
(63) kariṣyathā yūyameva yena svastirbhaven mama /
śīghraṃ śīghraṃ ca gatvā vai pṛcchathā devapālakam
body.translated_text:
The son said:
(63) Do it yourselves, by which well-being may come to me! Go quickly, quickly, and ask the temple priest!

body.text: [SaSū 200] atha tasya tau mātāpitarau devakukaṃ gatvā devasya dhūpaṃ dāpayanti / atha sa devapālakaḥ devasya dhūpaṃ datvaivaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate / devaste kruddhaḥ devasyopakāraḥ kartavyaḥ yajanaṃ kartavyaṃ / tatra paśurghātayitavyaḥ puruṣaśca ghātayitavyaḥ tataste putro vyādheḥ parimokṣyate / atha tau mātāpitarau tasyām velāyāmevaṃ cintayataḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmo daridrāścāsma / yadi devo na parasīdiṣyati tadasmākaṃ putraḥ kālaṃ kariṣyati / atha vā prasādaṃ kuryāttadvayaṃ paramadaridrāḥ paśuṃ puruṣaṃ cānayāma /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 200] Then his mother and father, having gone to the temple, offered incense to the god. And that temple priest, having offered incense to the god, spoke thus: 'The god is angry with you; service must be rendered to the god; a sacrifice must be performed. Therein, an animal must be slaughtered and a man must be slaughtered — then your son will be released from his disease.' Then those mother and father, at that moment, thought thus: 'What shall we do? We are poor! If the god will not be pleased, then our son will die. But if [the god] were to be pleased — we are extremely poor — [so] let us procure an animal and a person.'

body.text: [SaSū 201] atha tau śīghraśīghraṃ svagṛhaṃ gatvā yatkiṃcidgṛhe pariṣkāraṃ saṃvidyate tatsarvaṃ vikrīya; paśukrayārthe gacchataḥ atha tāvadanyataraṃ puruṣaṃ evaṃ vadeyuḥ dehi bhoḥ puruṣaḥ suvarṇamasmākaṃ yācitaṃ yadi śaknumo daśame divase punarapi dātuṃ tacchobhanamatha na śaknumo dātuṃ tadvayaṃ tava dāsā bhaviṣyāmaḥ karmakarāḥ tau ca taṃ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītvā gaccheyuḥ paśuṃ puruṣaṃ krotuṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 201] Then they, going quickly to their own home, sold whatever furnishings were to be found in the house — all of it — and went to purchase an animal. Then they would say to a certain man: 'Give us, good sir, gold on loan. If we are able to repay it on the tenth day, that is well; but if we are unable to repay, then we shall become your slaves and servants.' And having taken that gold, they went to purchase an animal and a person.

body.text: [SaSū 202] atha tābhyāṃ ca paśuḥ puruṣa krītaḥ sa ca puruṣo na jānīyādyan māmete jīvitādvyavaropayiṣyanti / atha tau mātāpitarau saṃmohamāpannau na bhūyaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviṣṭau / tau devakulaṃ gatvā taṃ devapalakamāmantrayanti / śīghramidānīṃ yajanaṃ kuruṣva /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 202] Then by them an animal and a person were purchased. And that person did not know: 'These people will deprive me of life.' Then those mother and father, having fallen into delusion, no longer entered their own home. Having gone to the temple, they addressed that temple priest: 'Perform the sacrifice now quickly!'

body.text: atha tau mātāpitarau svayameva taṃ paśuṃ ghātayataḥ taṃ ca puruṣaṃ jīvitādvyavaropayataḥ tataḥ sa devapālaka ārabdho yajñaṃ yajanāya medaṃ prajvālayati / tataḥ sa devo 'vatīrya evaṃ kathayati / tava putro mayā parigṛhītā iti / tatastau mātāpitarau prītiprāmodyena sphuṭāvāhatuḥ varaṃ putro jīvatu vayaṃ dāsā bhaviṣyāmaḥ tatastau mātāpitarau nivartya suyaṣṭāṃ devaṃ kṛtvā yāvat svagṛhaṃ gatvā tadā taṃ putraṃ kālagataṃ paśyanti / tatastau mātāpitarau mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena śokaśalyenāviddhahṛdayau nirāśībhūtau / tatraiva kālagatau / evameva bhaiṣajyasenākalyāṇamitrasaṃsargatā draṣṭavyāḥ
body.translated_text: Then those parents themselves slaughtered the animal and deprived that man of his life. Then that guardian of the god (<s>devapālaka</s>) commenced the sacrifice, lighting the sacrificial fat for the ritual. Then the god descended and spoke thus: 'Your son has been taken into my care.' Then those parents, bursting with joy and delight, [said]: 'Let our son live — we shall become [your] servants!' Then those parents, having turned back and duly worshipped the god, went home, and then they saw that their son had died. Then those parents, their hearts pierced by the arrow of great sorrow and mental anguish, became hopeless and died right there. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should be seen the association with unwholesome friends.

body.text: [SaSū 203] āha / pṛcchāmi (tāvad) bhagavan pṛcchāmi sugata; āha / pṛccha bhaiṣajyasena / āha / kutra bhagavan teṣāṃ sattvānāmupapattiḥ ko 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ āha / alaṃ bhaiṣajyasena kin tavānenārthena paripṛṣṭena / āha / pṛcchāmi bhagavan pṛcchāmi sugata; bhagavān āha / tatra bhaiṣajyasena mātā raurave mahānarake upapannā; pitā saṃghāte mahānarake upapannaḥ putrastapane mahānarake upapannaḥ devapālako mahāvicau mahānarake upapannaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 203] [<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>] said: 'I ask, Blessed One! I ask, <s>Sugata</s>!' He said: 'Ask, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>.' He said: 'Where, Blessed One, is the rebirth of those beings? What is their future state?' He said: 'Enough, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! What is the use of your asking about this?' He said: 'I ask, Blessed One! I ask, <s>Sugata</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'Therein, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the mother was reborn in the <s>Raurava</s> great hell; the father was reborn in the <s>Saṃghāta</s> great hell; the son was reborn in the <s>Tapana</s> great hell; the guardian of the god (<s>devapālaka</s>) was reborn in the <s>Mahāvīci</s> great hell.'

body.text: [SaSū 204] āha / anaparādhikasya bhagavan puruṣasya kutropapattiḥ ko 'syābhisaṃparāyaḥ / bhagavān āha - iha bhaiṣajyasenānaparādhikasya puruṣasya trāyastriṃśānan devanāṃ sahabhāvyatāyāmupapattirdraṣṭavyā; āha / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yat sa puruṣastrāyastriṃśatā devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyāmupapannaḥ bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena sa puruṣo maraṇakālasamaye jīvitādvyavaropyamāṇastathāgatasyopari cittaṃ prasādyaivaṃ vācamabhāṣataḥ namastasya bhagavate tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyetyekavārākṛtaṃ / sa tena bhaiṣajyasena kuśalamūlena ṣaṣṭiḥ kalpān trāyastriṃśatāṃ devānāṃ sukhamanubhaviṣyati / aśītiḥ kalpāṃ jātyā jātismaro bhaviṣyati / jātau jātau ca sarvaśokavigato bhaviṣyati / jātamātraśca sarvaduḥkhāni nirvāpayiṣyati / na hi te sarvasattvā śakyaṃ parinirvāpayitum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 204] He said: 'Where, Blessed One, is the rebirth of the innocent man? What is his future state?' The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the rebirth of the innocent man should be seen among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, in co-existence with them.' He said: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that that man was reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods in co-existence with them?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. That man, at the time of death, while being deprived of life, generated faith toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> and spoke these words: "Homage to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One" — having uttered this once. By that wholesome root (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for sixty <s>kalpas</s> he will experience happiness among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. For eighty <s>kalpas</s>, he will have recollection of past births in each birth. And in each birth, he will be free from all sorrow. And immediately upon being born, he will extinguish all sufferings. But those [other] beings cannot be made to pass into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 205] evamukte bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan na śakyaṃ sarvasattvāḥ parinirvāpayitum bhagavān āha - vīryaṃ bhaiṣajyasenārabdhavyam āha / katamo bhagavan vīryāraṃbhaḥ bhagavān āha / śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena vīryamucyate phalānāṃ darśanaṃ / yaduta srotaāpattiphalaṃ nāma vīryasthānaṃ / sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ nāma vīryasthānaṃ / anāgāmiphalaṃ nāma vīryasthānaṃ / arhatvaphalamarhannirodhaśca nāma vīryasthānaṃ / pratyekabuddhaphalaṃ pratyekabuddhaphalajñānaṃ nāma vīryasthānaṃ / bodhisattvabhūmiphalaṃ ca bodhisthānaṃ vīryasthānaṃ nāma / ime bhaiṣajyasena vīryasthānānāṃ nāmāni /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 205] When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'How, Blessed One, is it not possible for all beings to be made to pass into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Effort must be undertaken, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>.' He said: 'What, Blessed One, is the undertaking of effort?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! Effort is called the seeing of fruits — namely, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) is called a stage of effort; the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) is called a stage of effort; the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) is called a stage of effort; the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>, <s>arhat</s>-cessation, is called a stage of effort; the fruit of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and the knowledge of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> fruit is called a stage of effort; the fruit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages and the stage of awakening is called a stage of effort. These, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are the names of the stages of effort.'

body.text: [SaSū 206] āha / kathaṃ bhagavan srotaāpanno darśayitavyaḥ srotaāpattiphalañca / bhagavān āha / tadyathāpi nāma kaścideva bhaiṣajyasena puruṣa vṛkṣaṃ vāpayeta / vāpitasya vṛkṣasya tatraiva divase aṅkuraṃ viruhyeta / yatraiva divase aṅkuraṃ viruhyanta tatraiva divase tadaṅkuraṃ yojanamadhastādgacchete; dvitīyaśca puruṣa evameva vṛkṣaṃ vāpayeta; atha tatraivadivase vātakṣobhena tasya vṛkṣasya nāṅkurāni viruhyeranatha sa puruṣastasmāt sthānāt taṃ vṛkṣaṃ uddharetathānyataraśca puruṣaḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādaṃ kuryāt kimarthaṃ me bhūmiṃ khanasīti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 206] He said: 'How, Blessed One, should a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and the fruit of stream-entry be shown?' The Blessed One said: 'Just as, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a certain man might plant a tree, and on that very day the planted tree would sprout, and on the very day it sprouted that sprout would extend one <s>yojana</s> (league) beneath the ground; and a second man would likewise plant a tree, but on that very day, due to wind disturbance, the tree's sprouts would not grow — then that man would uproot the tree from that spot; and a certain other man would engage in quarrel, dispute, conflict, and argument, [saying]: "Why are you digging my land?"'

body.text: [SaSū 207] tena ca kālena tena samayena rājā aśrauśīdevaṃ dvau puruṣau parasparakalahabhaṇḍanavigrahajātau vivadataḥ tena ca rājñā tayordūtaḥ preṣitaḥ gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa tau dvau puruṣāvānaya; evaṃ deveti sa puruṣastasya rājñaḥ pratiśrutya tvaramāṇarūpaḥ pradhātvā tau puruṣāvetadavocat - rājā yuvayorāmantrayati / atha tāvadeva tatraiva puruṣa bhītastrasta dvitīyaśca puruṣo 'bhīto 'nutrastaḥ yena sa rājā tenopanītāvupanīya rājña purataḥ sthāpitāvatha sa rājā tayorevamāha / kimidaṃ bho yuvayoḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādo jātaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 207] At that time, at that moment, the king heard: 'These two men, having quarreled, disputed, conflicted, and argued with each other, are fighting.' A messenger was sent by the king to them: 'Go, good man, and bring those two men!' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' that man replied to the king, and hastening, he said to those two men: 'The king summons you both.' Then, right there, [one] man became frightened and terrified, while the second man was unafraid and unalarmed. They were led before the king and placed before him. Then the king spoke thus to them: 'What is this? How has this quarrel, dispute, conflict, and argument arisen between you two?'

body.text: [SaSū 208] atha khalu tau dvau puruṣāvutthāya taṃ rājānametadavocatāṃ śṛṇu mahārājāsmākaṃ na kiṃcit pṛthivīpradeśaḥ saṃvidyate / yācitake pṛthivīpradeśe vṛkṣo vāpitaḥ tatraiva divase vāpitastatraiva divase 'ṅkuraṃ patrāṇi puṣpāṇi phalāṇi ca prādurbhūtāni āmārdhaṃ pakvārdhaṃ ca / etena ca dvitīyena puruṣeṇa tatraiva divase tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe vṛkṣo vāpita / tasya ca vṛkṣasya nāṃkurāṇi rohanti / vātena kṣubhitena na patrāṇi na puṣpāṇi na phalāni prādurbhūtāni / na ca mahārāja yojanamadhastādasya mūlaṃ gacchati / sa eṣa puruṣo mayā sārdhaṃ vivadati tavāparādha iti / api (tu) ca deva svayameva parīkṣya jānīyān nātra mama kiṃcidaparādhaḥ saṃvidyate /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 208] Then those two men, rising, spoke thus to the king: 'Listen, great king! We have no piece of land of our own. On a borrowed piece of land, a tree was planted. On the very day it was planted, on that very day sprouts, leaves, flowers, and fruits appeared — half unripe, half ripe. But this second man, on that very day, planted a tree on that very piece of land, and his tree's sprouts did not grow; neither leaves, nor flowers, nor fruits appeared due to the agitation of wind. Nor, great king, does its root extend one <s>yojana</s> beneath the ground. This man is arguing with me, [saying it is] my fault. But, Your Majesty, examine it yourself and you will know — no fault of mine whatsoever is to be found.'

body.text:
[SaSū 209] atha khalu sa rājā triṃśatkoṭyo 'mātyānāmāhūyaikadhye 'saṃpātyaivamāha / kathayatha yūyaṃ / āmātyā āhuḥ kiṃ kathayāma mahārāja rājāha / kva yuṣmābhi dṛṣṭaṃ vā śrutaṃ vā yatraiva divase vṛkṣo vāpitastatraiva divase 'ṅkuraṃ viruhyate / patrāṇi puṣpāni phalāni ca jāyante / pakvardha-m-āmārdhāni niścayamidaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kartavyaṃ / atha khalu te amātya utthāyāsanāt taṃ rājānamevamāhuḥ asmākaṃ mahārāja niścayamidaṃ na śobhate kartuṃ na ca śakṣyāmo 'sya niścayaṃ vaktuṃ / vismayamidaṃ mahārāja eṣa eva puruṣastāvatpraṣṭavyaḥ vada bhoḥ puruṣa kiṃ satyametamarthaṃ yadvadasi / āha / satyaṃ mahārājaitamarthaṃ / rājāha /
(64) na śrutaṃ naiva ca puṣyāma duḥśrāddheyaṃ vacastava /

children.translated_text: That on the day a tree is sown, on that very day it sprouts,

children.text: (65) patrāḥ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dattaṃ dine tatraiva bhāṣasi /
children.translated_text: (65) leaves, flowers, and fruits are given — on that very day, you say!'
That man, with palms joined, then spoke to the king:

children.text: (66ab) gaccha svayam vāpaya taruṃ paśya ruhyati aṅkuram //
children.translated_text: (66ab) 'Go yourself, plant a tree, and see — it will sprout!'

body.translated_text:
[SaSū 209] Then the king, having summoned thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers and assembled them together, spoke thus: 'State [your judgment], you all.' The ministers said: 'What shall we say, great king?' The king said: 'Where have you seen or heard that on the very day a tree is planted, on that very day sprouts grow, and leaves, flowers, and fruits arise — half ripe, half unripe? A determination must be made by you.' Then those ministers, rising from their seats, spoke thus to the king: 'It is not proper for us, great king, to make this determination, nor are we able to pronounce a judgment on this. This is a marvel, great king! This very man should be questioned: "Speak, good man! Is this matter that you state true?"' He said: 'This matter is true, great king.' The king said:
(64) 'We have not heard, nor can we believe — incredible are your words!

body.text: [SaSū 210] atha khalu sa rājā tṛṃśatkoṭibhiramātyaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahirniṣkrāmati / tau ca dvau puruṣau cārakāvarodhaṃ kārayati / tataḥ sa rājā svayameva vṛkṣaṃ vāpayati / na ca sa vṛkṣo aṅkurāṇi dadāti na patrāṇi na puṣpāṇi na phalāni / atha sa rājā ruṣṭa evamāha / gacchantu bhavantaḥ śīghramānayantu dārupāṭakāni kuṭhārāṇi / yāvadānayitvā yastena puruṣeṇa vāpito vṛkṣaḥ sapatrāṇi puṣpaphalaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ taṃ vṛkṣaṃ roṣācchedayati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 210] Then the king, together with thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, went outside. And he had the two men placed under guard. Then the king himself planted a tree. But that tree produced no sprouts, no leaves, no flowers, no fruits. Then the king, angered, said thus: 'Go, you all — quickly bring axes and woodcutting tools!'
