Having brought them, the tree that had been planted by that [first] man — with leaves, flowers, and fruits appearing — that tree he cut down in anger.

body.text: [SaSū 211] taṃ caikaṃ vṛkṣaṃ cchinnaṃ dvādaśa vṛkṣāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ dvādaśa vṛkṣā cchinnāścaturviṃśati vṛkṣāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ saptaratnamayāḥ samūlāḥ sapatrāḥ sapahalāḥ sāṃkurāḥ atha tebhyāścaturviṃśati vṛkṣebhyaścaturviṃśati pakṣiṇaḥ kurkuṭāḥ prādurbhūtāni / suvarṇacūḍāni suvarṇatuṇḍāni saptaratnamayāni pakṣmāṇi / atha khalu sa rājā roṣābhibhūtaḥ svahastena kuṭhāraṃ gṛhya taṃ vṛkṣaṃ parāhanati / tataśca vṛkṣātparāhatādamṛtodakaṃ pravahati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 211] When that one tree was cut down, twelve trees appeared. When twelve trees were cut down, twenty-four trees appeared, made of the seven precious substances — with roots, with leaves, with fruits, and with sprouts. Then from those twenty-four trees, twenty-four birds — roosters — appeared, with golden crests, golden beaks, and plumage made of the seven precious substances. Then the king, overpowered by anger, seizing an axe in his own hand, struck that tree. And from the tree that was struck, nectar-water (<s>amṛtodaka</s>) flowed forth.

body.text: [SaSū 212] atha (khalu) sa rājā saṃvignamanā ājñāpayati / gacchatha tau puruṣau tataścārakābandhanān mocayadhvamevam deveti / tatkṣanameva pradhāvitvā tau puruṣau tataścārakabandhanān mokṣayitvā yena taṃ vṛkṣaṃ tenopanīyataḥ atha sa rājā papriccha / kim ayaṃ vṛkṣastvadvāpitaḥ eko bhūtvā cchidyamāno dviguṇaviddhyābhvardhamānaḥ yāvaccaturviṃśatudhā gataḥ madvāpitastu vṛkṣo nāṃkurāṇi na patrāṇi na puṣpāṇi na phalāni dattavān tataḥ sa puruṣa evamāha / yādṛśāni mahārāja mama puṇyāṇi na tava tādṛśāni puṇyāni saṃvidyante /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 212] Then that king, with an agitated mind, commanded: 'Go! Release those two men from their chains and bonds — thus, O lord!' Immediately, running out, they released those two men from their chains and bonds and brought them to where that tree was. Then the king asked: 'How is it that this tree planted by you, being one, when cut became twofold, and growing doubled again until it became twenty-four-fold, while the tree planted by me produced neither sprouts, nor leaves, nor flowers, nor fruit?' Then that man said: 'The merits that are mine, O great king — such merits are not found in you.'

body.text: [SaSū 213] atha khalu te triṃśadamātyakoṭyastasya puruṣasyobhau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpyaivamāhuḥ tvayā rājyaṃ kārayitavyaṃ nāyaṃ pūrvimako rājā śobhate / atha (khalu) sa puruṣastān amātyān gāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣata; //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 213] Then those thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, placing both knees on the ground before that man, said: 'You should exercise kingship — this former king is not worthy.' Then that man replied to those ministers with verses:

children.text: (66cd) rājyabhogaiśca me nārtho na dhānyena dhanena vā /
children.translated_text: (66cd) I have no need of the enjoyments of kingship, nor of grain, nor of wealth.
(67) My faith is in the <s>Buddhas</s>; may I become the best of bipeds!

body.text:
brajennirvāṇadhātau hi śānte yatra tathāgataḥ
(68) deśeya dharmaṃ yuṣmākaṃ nirvāṇapuragāminaṃ //
body.translated_text:
Going to the peaceful realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, where the <s>Tathāgata</s> [dwells] —
(68) I would teach the <s>Dharma</s> to you, leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: Having bound [himself] in cross-legged posture, he then made a vow:

children.text: (69) pūrvaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ rājño bandhanamāgataḥ
children.translated_text: (69) Previously I committed sin and came to the king's bondage;

children.text: idan tu kṛtvā praṇidhiṃ mama pāpakṣayo bhavet //
children.translated_text: but having made this aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), may my sin be destroyed!

body.text: [SaSū 214] atha khalu te caturviṃśati pakṣiṇakukkuṭakoṭyo vajratuṇḍena tūryāṇi parāhanati sma // atha khalu tena kālena tena samayena dvātriṃśati kūṭāgārasahasrāṇi prādurbhūtāni / ekaikaṃ ca kūṭāgāraṃ paṃcaviṃśatiyojanapramāṇaṃ prādurabhavat ekaikasmiṃśca kūṭāgāre paṃcaviṃśati pakṣiṇakukkuṭāḥ prādurbhūtāni / suvarṇacūḍāni suvarṇatuṇḍāni suvarṇamukhāni / te mānuṣyakaṃ vācaṃ niścārayanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 214] Then those twenty-four <s>koṭis</s> of bird-roosters struck musical instruments with their diamond beaks. Then at that time, at that moment, thirty-two thousand pinnacled mansions appeared. Each mansion appeared measuring twenty-five <s>yojanas</s> in extent. And in each mansion, twenty-five bird-roosters appeared — with golden crests, golden beaks, and golden faces. They uttered human speech:

body.text:
(70) asādhuste mahārāja yadbṛkṣa ccheditastvayā /
koṭīśatāni vṛkṣāṇāṃ caturviṃśat sthitāḥ punaḥ
(71) pāpena karmaṇānena aniṣṭhaṃ bhokṣyase phalam
[[na]] jānīṣe kīdṛśaḥ sattvo yenāyaṃ vāpito drumaḥ
body.translated_text:
(70) It was wrong of you, O great king, that the tree was cut by you! Hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of trees — twenty-four stand again.
(71) By this sinful <s>karma</s>, you will experience undesirable fruit. You do not know what kind of being it is by whom this tree was planted!

body.text:
rājāha -
(72) na jānāmi imaṃ arthaṃ vyakurudhavaṃ mahātapā /

children.text: kīdṛśo 'sau mahāsattvo yenāyaṃ vāpito drumaḥ pakṣiṇa āhuḥ
children.translated_text: What kind of great being is it by whom this tree was planted? The birds said:
(73) He is the illuminator of the world; he will arise as a guide,
a liberator of all beings from the bondage of <s>saṃsāric</s> existence.

body.translated_text:
The king said:
(72) I do not know this matter — explain it, O great ascetic!

body.text:
rājāha -
(74) katamo dvitīyaḥ sattvo yasya vṛkṣaṃ na rūhati /
kiṃ vā karma kṛtaṃ tena pāpamācakṣva me dvijāḥ
body.translated_text:
The king said:
(74) Who is the second being, for whom the tree does not grow? What sin was committed by him? Tell me, O twice-born ones!

children.translated_text: The birds said:

children.text: (75) devadatto hi mūḍho 'sau yasya vṛkṣaṃ na rūhati /
children.translated_text: (75) <s>Devadatta</s>, that deluded one — for him the tree does not grow.

children.text: na kṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ kiṃcid ruhyate sya kathaṃ druma //
children.translated_text: No wholesome [deed] was done [by him] — how could a tree grow for him?

body.text: [SaSū 214] atha khalu tena kālena tena samayena tṛṃśatkoṭya āmātyānāmiman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā sarve daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisattvā abhijñāpratilabdhāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ sa ca rājā daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitaḥ kuśaladharmābhisamayamanuprāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 214] Then at that time, at that moment, thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, having heard this <s>dharma-paryāya</s>, all became <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), having attained the higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). And that king, established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, attained the realization of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: [SaSū 215] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yattriṃśatkoṭyo janānāṃ daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā abhijñāpratilabdhā saṃvṛttāḥ bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena vyākariṣyāmi / atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāra; atha tāvadeva tasmin samaye bhagavato mukhadvārāccaturaśīti raśmiśatasahasrāṇi naścaranti smānekavarṇāni nānāvarṇānyanekaśatasahasravarṇāni / tadyathā nīlapītalohitāvadātamaṃjiṣṭhāsphaṭikarajatavarṇāni / tā anantāparyantāni lokadhātavo 'vabhāsya punareva pratyudāvṛtyā (taṃ) bhagavantaṃ tṛṣpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato mūrdhanyantardhīyanta /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 215] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition that thirty <s>koṭis</s> of people became established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> and attained the higher knowledges?' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, I will explain.' Then at that moment the Blessed One displayed a smile. And at that very moment, from the mouth of the Blessed One, eighty-four hundred thousand rays of light issued forth — of many colors, of various colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors — namely: blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver-colored. Those [rays], having illuminated infinite and boundless world-realms, returned again, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and disappeared into the crown of the Blessed One's head.

body.text: [SaSū 216] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ utthāyāsanādekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāyaḥ nāhetukaṃ nāpratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāduṣkurvanti / bhagavān āha - paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena caturdiśaṃ lokadhātau samantājjanakāyamāgacchantaṃ mamāntike / āha / nohīdaṃ bhagavan na paśyāmi / bhagavān āha - tena hi bhaiṣajyasena vyavalokaya paśya janakāyaṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 216] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, rising from his seat, draping his robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the display of a smile? Not without cause, not without condition do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile.' The Blessed One said: 'Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, in the four directions of the world-realm, a multitude of people coming all around into my presence?' He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One, I do not see.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, look and see the multitude of people!'

body.text: [SaSū 217] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vyavalokyādrākṣīt pūrvasyān diśyeko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatraikānte paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te ca na bhāṣante na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti na bhuṃjanti nottiṣṭhanti na caṃkramanti tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / dakṣiṇasyān diśi-m-eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti / na bhāṣante nottiṣṭhanti na caṃkramanti / tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsyanti / paścimāyāṃ diśyeko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti / na bhāṣanti nottiṣṭhanti na caṃkramanti / tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / uttarasyān diśi-m-eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti na bhāṣanti nottiṣṭhanti / na caṃkramanti tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / ūrdhvāyān diśyeko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti na bhāṣanti / nottiṣṭhanti na caṃkramanti / tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsyanti / adhastāddiśyeko vṛkṣo prādurbhūtaḥ saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ tatra ca paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni / te na jalpanti nālapanti na saṃlapanti na bhāṣanti nottiṣṭhānti / na caṃkramanti / tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 217] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, looking, saw: In the eastern direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, at one side, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not speak, did not talk, did not converse, did not chat; they did not eat, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence. In the southern direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not talk, did not converse, did not chat; they did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence. In the western direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not talk, did not converse, did not chat; they did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence. In the northern direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not talk, did not converse, did not chat, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence. In the upward direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not talk, did not converse, did not chat, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence. In the downward direction, a single tree had appeared, measuring seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There, twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of the multitude of people had assembled. They did not talk, did not converse, did not chat, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about — they abided in silence.

body.text: [SaSū 218] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśaṃ sacenme bhagavān avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭaḥ praśnavyākaraṇāya / evamukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena yadyadevākāṃkṣasyahan te tasya tasyaiva praśnasya paripṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣye /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 218] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I would ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to ask a question for [its] elucidation.' When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Ask, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, whatever you wish. I will satisfy your mind with an answer to each and every question you ask.'

body.text: [SaSū 219] evamukte bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kimetad bhagavaṃścaturdiśe lokadhātuṣu janakāyamāgatyāvasthito yāvadadhastā ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi paṃcāśat koṭyo janakāyamāgatyāvasthitaḥ te ca bhagavantaṃ nālapanti na saṃlapanti / na jalpanti na vadanti na bhāṣanti / nottiṣṭhanti na caṃkramanti / tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ bhagavān āha - gaccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena svayameva tāṃstathāgatān paripṛcchā; yato lokadhātāvete janakāyā āgatā / āha / kasya bhagavan ṛddhibalādhānena gacchāmi / tathāgatasyardhyānubhāvena uta svardhyā; bhagavān āha - svakena bhaiṣajyasena ṛddhibalādhānena gaccha / punarapi tathāgatasyardhyānubhāvenāgaccha;
body.translated_text: [SaSū 219] When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'What is this, Blessed One? In the world-realms of the four directions, a multitude of people has arrived and stands—up to fifty <s>koṭīs</s> of people from the downward and upward directions having arrived and standing. And they do not speak to the Blessed One, do not converse, do not talk, do not utter, do not declare. They do not stand up, they do not walk about. They abide in silence. What, Blessed One, is the cause? What is the condition?' The Blessed One said: 'Go, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, yourself inquire of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> from which world-realm these multitudes have come.' He said: 'By whose power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous ability) shall I go, Blessed One? By the <s>Tathāgata's</s> supernatural power, or by my own?' The Blessed One said: 'Go, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, by your own power of <s>ṛddhi</s>. And return again by the <s>Tathāgata's</s> supernatural power.'

body.text: [SaSū 220] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantaṃ tṛguptaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tatraivāntardhitaḥ atha khalvito lokadhātā ṣaṇnavati lokadhātukoṭīratikramya candrapradīpā nāma lokadhātuḥ tatra candrāvatikṣetro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha etarhi tiṣṭhati dhṛyate yāpayati / aśītikoṭī bodhisattvamahāsattvasahasraparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharman deśayati sma / tām lokadhātuṃ bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo 'nuprāptaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 220] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared right there. Then, having passed beyond ninety-six <s>koṭīs</s> of world-realms from this world-realm, there is a world-realm named <s>Candrapradīpā</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s> presently lives, endures, and sustains himself, surrounded by eighty <s>koṭīs</s> of thousands of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, attended upon, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> reached that world-realm.

body.text: [SaSū 221] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataścandrāvatikṣetrasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasābhivandya purata sthitaḥ sthitvā yena sa bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - āgato 'smi bhagavan ṣaṇnavati lokadhātukoṭīsahasrāṇyatikramya bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt sahāyā lokadhātoḥ na cāhaṃ bhagavaṃstāvanti sattvāni kvacit paśyāmi / yāvanti tatra dṛṣṭāni / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yat sahāyāṃ lokadhātau bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya purato bahujanakāyaḥ sannipatito daśadigabhyāgatastatrasthaḥ paśyāmyāsīttāni cehastho na paśyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 221] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, and stood before him. Standing there, joining his palms toward that Blessed One, he said this to the Blessed One: 'I have come, Blessed One, having passed beyond ninety-six thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of world-realms, from the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, the Buddha-field of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>. Yet I do not see anywhere as many beings as were seen there. What, Blessed One, is the cause? What is the condition? For in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, before the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, a great multitude of people had assembled, having come from the ten directions—I saw them standing there, yet standing here I do not see them.'

body.text: [SaSū 222] sa bhagavān āha - tatraiva bhaiṣajyasena saṃcaranti saṃtiṣṭhanti / āha / yathā kathaṃ punarbhagavan bhagavān āha - acetanavṛkṣasaṃbhūtāni sattvāni / āha / kena bhagavan dṛṣṭaṃ kena śrutaṃ yad acetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyante / sa bhagavān āha - na bhaiṣajyasena tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ (vā) na śrutaṃ (vā) yadacetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyaṃte / āha / na me bhagavan dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutaṃ yadacetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyante / sa bhagavān āha - icchasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena draṣṭuṃ tadahaṃ sāṃprataṃ darśayiṣyāmi / āha / icchāmi bhagavannicchāmi sugata;
body.translated_text: [SaSū 222] That Blessed One said: 'Right there, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they move about and stand.' He said: 'But how so, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'They are beings born from non-sentient trees.' He said: 'Who, Blessed One, has seen, who has heard, that humans are born from a non-sentient tree?' That Blessed One said: 'Have you, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, neither seen nor heard that humans are born from a non-sentient tree?' He said: 'I have neither seen nor heard, Blessed One, that humans are born from a non-sentient tree.' That Blessed One said: 'Do you wish, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, to see? I shall now show you.' He said: 'I wish it, Blessed One; I wish it, <s>Sugata</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 223] atha khalu bhagavāṃścandrāvatikṣetrastathāgatastasyāṃ velāyāṃ śatapuṇyavicitritaṃ svaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayati sma / tataśca bāhutaḥ koṭīśatasahasraṃ janakāyānāṃ prādurabhavatekaikaśca janakāyo bāhuśataṃ prasārya nānāgandhavilepanaistathāgatamabhyavakiranti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 223] Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, at that moment extended his own arm adorned with a hundred merits. And from that arm, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of people appeared. And each person, extending a hundred arms, scattered various fragrant ointments upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha sa bhagavāṃścandrāvatikṣetrastathāgato bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati / paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena eṣa janakāyastathāgataṃ nānāgandhamālyavilepanairabhyavakiranti / āha / paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata ; sa bhagavān āha - ete acetanā janakāyāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ eta acetanā manuṣyāḥ pratyājātāḥ // atha khalu teṣāṃ koṭīśatasahasrāṇāmekaikasya yadbāhuśataṃ te sarve vikīryante /
body.translated_text: Then that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these people scattering various fragrant garlands and ointments upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' He said: 'I see them, Blessed One; I see them, <s>Sugata</s>.' That Blessed One said: 'These are non-sentient multitudes that have appeared; these are non-sentient humans that have been reborn.' Then the hundred arms of each of those hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s>—they all disintegrated.

body.text: [SaSū 224] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavantametadavocat - kimidaṃ bhagavan kimidaṃ sugataḥ yan manuṣyāṇāṃ muhūrtamātreṇa bāhuśataṃ vikīrṇam yadi bhagavaṃcchatabāhavo na mucyante kaḥ punarvādo dvibāhukā manuṣyā mokṣyante / bhagavān āha - evameva bhaiṣajyasenācetanāḥ sattvā jāyante / acetanā niruddhyante / asmākamapi bhaiṣajyasena śarīramacetanabhūtaṃ manyitavyaṃ / āha / katame bhagavan sattvā ye daharāḥ katame vṛddhāḥ bhagavān āha - santi bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ sattvā santi vṛddhāḥ āha / katame bhagavan daharā katame vṛddhāḥ āha / ye te sāmprataṃvikīrṇā te vṛddhāḥ ye te vṛkṣebhyo nirjātāste daharā / āha / icchāmi bhagavan daharāṇi sattvāni draṣṭum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 224] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, having seen that, said this to the Blessed One: 'What is this, Blessed One? What is this, <s>Sugata</s>? That in merely a moment the hundred arms of these humans disintegrated! If, Blessed One, those with a hundred arms are not liberated, what then to say of two-armed humans—will they be liberated?' The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, non-sentient beings are born; non-sentient [beings] perish. Our body too, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should be considered as non-sentient.' He said: 'Which beings, Blessed One, are young, and which are old?' The Blessed One said: 'There are, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, young beings, and there are old ones.' He said: 'Which, Blessed One, are young and which are old?' He said: 'Those who just now disintegrated—they are old. Those who have come forth from the trees—they are young.' He said: 'I wish, Blessed One, to see the young beings.'

body.text: [SaSū 225] atha khalu sa bhagavāṃścandrāvatikṣetrastathāgato dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇitalaṃ prasārayati / atha daśabhyo digbhyaḥ koṭīśatasahasraṃ janakāyānāṃ āgacchanti / adhastādūrdhvāyān diśi paṃcāśat koṭī janakāyasyāgacchanti / āgatvā ca te janakāyā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya na ca tathāgatamālapanti na saṃlapanti tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti sma /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 225] Then that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, extended his right palm. Then from the ten directions, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of people came. From the downward and upward directions, fifty <s>koṭīs</s> of people came. And having come, those people bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, yet they did not speak to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, did not converse—they abided in silence.

body.text: [SaSū 226] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kimete bhagavan sattvāstathāgataṃ nālapanti na saṃlapanti tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti / bhagavān āha - na jānāsi bhaiṣajyasena acetanaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo nālapanti na saṃlapanti / (na) dharmaskandhaṃ prajānāti / tatkasya hetoḥ ihaikatyā bhaiṣajyasena daharā sattvāḥ notpādaṃ jānanti na nirodhaṃ jānanti / dṛṣṭvā ca na jarā na vyādhirna śoko na paridevaḥ na priyaviprayogo nāpriyasaṃprayogaḥ na priyādvinābhāvaḥ na maraṇaṃ nākālamṛtyu / nāpi tāni sarvakaṭukāni duḥkhāṇi dṛṣṭvā udyogamāpadyante kutaste jñāsyanti / punaḥ punaste bhaiṣajyasena śikṣayitavyāni /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 226] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Why is it, Blessed One, that these beings do not speak to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, do not converse, and abide in silence?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you not know, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>? The non-sentient portion of earth does not speak, does not converse. It does not comprehend the aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>. Why is that? Here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, certain young beings do not know arising, do not know cessation. And having seen [this world], there is for them no old age, no sickness, no sorrow, no lamentation, no separation from the beloved, no union with the unbeloved, no being apart from the dear, no death, no untimely death. Not even having seen all those bitter sufferings do they make effort—how then will they know? Again and again, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they must be trained.'

body.text: [SaSū 227] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kuto bhagavan daharā sattvā āgacchanti / kutaścyavanti / kutropapadyante / ye dharmaṃ na jānanti (na buddhyanti) / bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena yan mānuṣyakamātmabhāvaṃ pratigṛhṇanti / tanna rupyakāreṇa kṛtaṃ / na cīmarakāreṇa kṛtaṃ / na kāṣṭhakāreṇa kṛtaṃ / na kulālena kṛtaṃ / na rājabhayenotpadyate / strīpuruṣasaṃyogāt pāpena karmaṇā saṃyuktaṃ saṃbhavati / punaḥ punaśca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ śilpāni śikṣāpayanti / anantaṃ ca teṣāṃ kaṭukaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃbhavati / kaṭukā vedanāḥ tatra teṣāṃ pūrvakṛtānāṃ pāpakānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākamanubhavanti / ihaiva te bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ sattvā āgatā ya ete (nālapanti na saṃlapanti) nottiṣṭhanti ya īdṛśān duḥkhāṃ vedanāmanubhavanti / anena kāraṇena bhaiṣajyasena nālapanti na saṃlapanti / evaṃ te bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ sattvāḥ kuśalamajānānāḥ notpādaṃ jānanti na nirodhaṃ jānanti / na ca te mānuṣyakamātmabhāvaṃ pratilapsyante / ime ucyante bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ sattvā /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 227] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'From where, Blessed One, do the young beings come? From where do they fall? Where are they reborn? They who do not know the <s>Dharma</s>, who do not understand it.' The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. The human form that they take on—it was not made by a silversmith, not made by a fabric-maker, not made by a carpenter, not made by a potter. It does not arise from fear of a king. It comes into being from the union of man and woman, conjoined with evil <s>karma</s>. And again and again, crafts and skills are taught to those beings. And endless bitter suffering arises for them. Bitter sensations—there they experience the ripening of their previously done evil <s>karmas</s>. Right here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those young beings have come who do not speak, do not converse, do not stand up, who experience such painful sensations. For this reason, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they do not speak, they do not converse. Thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those young beings, not knowing what is wholesome, do not know arising, do not know cessation. And they will not obtain a human form. These, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are called young beings.'

body.text: [SaSū 228] āha / kathaṃ bhagavan daharāḥ sattvā utpadyante kathaṃ nirudhyante / bhagavān āha - tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyasena kaścideva puruṣa agniṃ kāṣṭhena parimārjayetta tasyānupūrveṇa taṃ kāṣṭhamagninā pradīpyeta / evameva bhaiṣajyasena mānuṣyātmabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ saṃjāyate / jātaṃ ca san vedanāṃ vedayati / āha / ko trābhijāto jātaḥ kaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ bhagavān āha - buddha eva bhaiṣajyasenābhijāto jātaḥ tathāgata eva parinirvṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 228] He said: 'How, Blessed One, do young beings arise, and how do they cease?' The Blessed One said: 'Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a man were to rub fire with a stick — gradually that stick would be kindled by fire. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, first the human self-existence is born; and having been born, one experiences sensations.' He said: 'Who therein is born as the truly born? Who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'It is the <s>Buddha</s> himself, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, who is the truly born. It is the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 229] tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyasena kasmiṃcidandhakāragṛhe timirāgāre rājñā puruṣo bandhanāvarodhaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt tatra sa puruṣo 'ndhakāragṛhe praviṣṭaḥ antargṛhe timiraṃ timirāgāraṃ paśyet athānyaḥ ka kaścit puruṣaḥ pūrvaduḥkhavedanābhirdṛṣṭaścintayennaṣṭa eṣa puruṣaḥ anabhyasitaḥ duḥkho jīvite vināśaṃ yāsyati / sa tatrāgnimānayitvā tatrābhyantargṛhe sukṣmamagnim cchorayet sa ca puruṣaścārakāvaruddhastamagniraśmiṃ paśyeddṛṣṭvā cāśvasto bhaved utsāhaṃ ca vardhayet sa cāgniḥ kenacideva hetunā prajvaleta; tena cāgninjvālena tadgṛhaṃ samantataḥ prajvalet sa ca puruṣastatraiva dahyet taṃ ca dagdhaṃ rājā śrutvā cintāyāsamāpadyeta / tasyaivaṃ bhavenna bhūyo 'haṃ svaviṣaye kaṃcit sattvaṃ cārakāvarodhaṃ kariṣyāmi / atha sa rājā teṣāṃ svaviṣayanivāsināṃ sattvānāmevaṃ samāśvāsayet mā yūyaṃ bhavantaḥ sattvā bhāyatha mā utrasatha; abhayaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhavatuḥ na mama viṣaye bhūyo daṇḍopacāraṃ (vā) bandhanāvarodhaṃ vā bhaviṣyati / na ca kasyacit sattvasya jīvitavināśaṃ kariṣyāmi / nirbhayā bhavantaḥ sattvā yūyaṃ bhavatha /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 229] 'Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a man were imprisoned by the king in a dark house, a chamber of darkness. That man, having entered the dark house, would see darkness, a dark chamber, within the house. Then some other man, having seen [him] with the sensations of former suffering, would think: "This man is lost; unaccustomed to suffering, he will perish in life." He would bring fire there and release a small flame inside the house. And that imprisoned man would see that ray of fire, and having seen it, would be reassured and would increase his courage. But that fire, by some cause, would blaze up; and by that flame of fire the house would blaze on all sides, and that man would be burned right there. And the king, hearing that he was burned, would fall into anxiety. He would think: "No more will I imprison any being in my realm." Then that king would reassure those beings dwelling in his realm thus: "Do not be afraid, good beings, do not be terrified! May you be without fear! In my realm there will no more be punishment or imprisonment. And I will not cause the destruction of life of any being. Be fearless, good beings!"'

body.text: [SaSū 230] evameva bhaiṣajyasena tathāgataḥ sarvakleśadagdhaḥ sarvavyādhipraśāntaḥ yathā sa puruṣo gṛhadāhāt svakāyaṃ dahati / (sarva)sattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya (ca) pratipanno bhavati / sattvān vadhabandhanāvarodheṣu parimocayedevameva tathāgato rāgadveṣamohamalaprahīṇaḥ sarvasattvānān dīpa iva loka utpannaḥ sattvān mocayati narakatiryakpretāsurakāyebhyaḥ daharāṃśca (sattvāṃ) vṛddhāṃśca sattvān mocayati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 230] 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has burned all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and pacified all diseases — just as that man burns his own body by the burning of the house — acts for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of (all) beings. He should liberate beings from slaughter, bondage, and imprisonment. Just so, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has abandoned the impurities of passion, hatred, and delusion, having arisen in the world like a lamp for all beings, liberates beings from the realms of hell, animals, <s>pretas</s>, and <s>asuras</s>, and liberates both young and old beings.'

body.text: [SaSū 231] atha tāvadevoparyantarīkṣādimā gāthā niścacārā; //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 231] Then at that very moment, from the sky above, these verses issued forth:

body.text:
(76) aho kṣetraṃ jinakṣetraṃ sukṣtremabhisaṃskṛtaṃ /
vuptāni yatra bījāni na vināśaṃ brajanti hi /
(77) buddhakṣetraṃ jinakṣetraṃ praśastaṃ jinaśāsanaṃ /
śāstā karotyupāyaṃ hi sarvasattvaparigrahe /
(78) sthito nirvānadhātau san dṛśyate dharaṇītale /
śāntaṃ kṛtvā sarvalokaṃ buddhaḥ śodheti dakṣiṇāṃ /
(79) moceti navakān sattvān moceti ca purāṇakān

children.translated_text: having liberated [them] gradually, all beings from the three realms.
(80) Those bound at the doors of hell, animals, and <s>pretas</s> have been liberated;

children.text: śāntiḥ kṛtā hi lokesmin paraloke sukhaṃ kṛtaṃ //
children.translated_text: peace has been made in this world, and happiness has been created in the next world.

body.translated_text:
(76) Oh, the field — the <s>Jina</s>'s (Conqueror's) field, prepared as an excellent field! Seeds sown therein do not go to destruction.
(77) The <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), the <s>Jina</s>'s field — praised is the <s>Jina</s>'s teaching! The Teacher employs skillful means for the embracing of all beings.
(78) Abiding in the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, [yet] he is seen upon the earth's surface; having made all the world peaceful, the <s>Buddha</s> purifies the offering.
(79) He liberates young beings, and he liberates ancient beings —

body.text: [SaSū 232] atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāra / āha ca -
body.translated_text: [SaSū 232] Then at that moment, the Blessed One displayed a smile. And he said:

body.text:
(81) sādhu darśanu sādhūnāṃ buddhānām sādhu darśanaṃ /
sādhu dharmaguṇaḥ kṣetraṃ saṃghasāmagridarśanam
(82) sādhu saṃghātanirdeśaṃ sarvapāpavināśanaṃ
ye śroṣyanti idaṃ sūtraṃ padaṃ prāpsyantyanuttaraṃ
body.translated_text:
(81) Excellent is the sight of the virtuous; excellent is the sight of <s>Buddhas</s>! Excellent is the field of <s>Dharma</s> virtues; [excellent is] the sight of the <s>Saṅgha's</s> harmony.
(82) Excellent is the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> teaching, the destroyer of all sin! Those who will hear this <s>sūtra</s> will attain the unsurpassed state.

body.text: [SaSū 233] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya / bhagavān āha - paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputraitāni daharāṇi sattvāni / āha / paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata; bhagavān āha - sarva ete bhaiṣajyasenādyaiva daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 233] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the display of a smile?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you see, son of good family, these young beings?' He said: 'I see [them], Blessed One; I see [them], <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'All of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, will this very day become <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).'

body.text: [SaSū 234] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'śītiryojanasahasrāṇyūrdhavamuparyantarīkṣe sthādathāśītirdevaputrakoṭīsahasrāṇi bhagavata upari puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti te ca daharāḥ sattvā dṛṣṭvā sarve 'ñjalayaḥ kṛtvā namaskurvanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 234] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> stood eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> upward in the sky. And eighty <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>devaputras</s> rained a shower of flowers upon the Blessed One. And those young beings, seeing this, all joined their palms and bowed.

body.text: [SaSū 235] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo antarīkṣastha evaṃ vāg bhāṣate / yena trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ śabdenāpūrayati / dvātriṃśan mahānarakopapannāḥ sattvāstaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti / dvātriṃśacca devanikāyāstaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti / trisāhasramahāsāhasraśca lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitaḥ caturaśītiśca nāgarājasahasrāṇi mahāsamudre saṃkṣubdāni / triṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi rākṣasānām imaṃ jaṃbūdvīpamāgatāni / paṃcaviṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi pretānāṃ yakṣānāṃ rākṣasānāmaḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyāmāgatāni bhagavataḥ purato mahāsannipātaḥ saṃsthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 235] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, standing in the sky, spoke thus, filling the great trichiliocosm with sound. Beings reborn in the thirty-two great hells heard that sound. And the thirty-two classes of gods heard that sound. And the great trichiliocosm trembled with six kinds of earthquakes. And eighty-four thousand <s>nāga</s> kings were agitated in the great ocean. Thirty <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) came to this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Twenty-five <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>pretas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> came to the royal capital <s>Aḍakavatī</s>. A great assembly was established before the Blessed One.

body.text: [SaSū 236] atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣān daharāṇāṃ sattvānān dharman deśayati / daśasu dikṣu lokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ svakasvakābhyo ṛddhibhirāgatāni / atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat - bahavo bhagavan bahavo sugata bodhisattvāḥ sannipatitāḥ sanniṣaṇṇāḥ bahūni ca bhagavan devanāgāni sannipatitāni sanniṣaṇṇāni / punaścānekāni rākṣasapretānyaḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyamāgatya sannipatitāni sanniṣaṇṇānyabhūvan dharmaśravaṇāya //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 236] Then the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those young beings. From the <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of world-realms in the ten directions, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> came by their respective miraculous powers. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Many, Blessed One, many, <s>Sugata</s>, are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> assembled and seated! And many, Blessed One, are the celestial <s>nāgas</s> assembled and seated! And furthermore, many <s>rākṣasas</s> and <s>pretas</s>, having come to the royal capital <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, were assembled and seated for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 237] tatra khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati / āgaccha kulaputra; atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ṛddhibalenordhvādavatīrya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocat - dharmaskandho (bhagavan) dharmaskandha iti / bhagavannucyate kiyatā bhagavan dharmaskandha ityucyate / bhagavān āha - dharmaskandha iti kulaputrocyate / yo brahmacaryaṃ paryeṣate brahmacaryaṃ paryeṣya sarvapāpādviramati / paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputrāmī daharā sattvā abrahmacaryād viramanti / āha paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata; āha / te nūnan dhāraṇīpratilabdhā bhaviṣyanti / sarvadharmasamanvāgatāśca bhaviṣyanti / āha / kenopāyena bhagavan bahūni sattvāni sannipatitāni / dharmaskandhaṃ śrotum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 237] Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Come, son of good family!' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, descending from above by his miraculous power, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: '<s>Dharmaskandha</s> (aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>), Blessed One — "<s>dharmaskandha</s>," it is said. To what extent, Blessed One, is it called "<s>dharmaskandha</s>"?' The Blessed One said: '"<s>Dharmaskandha</s>," son of good family, is said [of one who] seeks the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>); having sought the holy life, he refrains from all sin. Do you see, son of good family, these young beings refraining from unchastity?' He said: 'I see [them], Blessed One; I see [them], <s>Sugata</s>.' He said: 'Surely they will have attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (powers of retention). And they will be endowed with all <s>dharmas</s>.' He said: 'By what means, Blessed One, have many beings assembled to hear the <s>dharmaskandha</s>?'

body.text: [SaSū 238] atha khalu bhagavāṃ bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati / bahavo bhaiṣajyasena sattvāḥ santi / ye jātireva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti / jarā eva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti / vyādhireva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti / śokaduḥkhaṃ paridevaduḥkhaṃ priyaviprayogaduḥkhamapriyasaṃprayogaduḥkhaṃ maraṇaṃ tu sarvaduḥkhaṃ harate / kāyajīvitamidamucyate bhaiṣajyasena sarvaduḥkham
body.translated_text: [SaSū 238] Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'There are many beings, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, who do not hear that birth itself is suffering, that old age itself is suffering, that disease itself is suffering — the suffering of grief, the suffering of lamentation, the suffering of separation from the beloved, the suffering of union with the unbeloved — but death carries away all suffering. This bodily life, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is called "all suffering."'

body.text: [SaSū 239] atha khalu te daharāḥ sattvā imannirdeśaṃ śrutvā yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjalayaḥ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocan asmākamapi bhagavan marttavyaṃ / bhagavān āha - yuṣmābhirapi kulaputrāḥ sarvasattvaiśca martavyamiti / āha / kathaṃ bhagavan maraṇakālamākramati / bhagavān āha - maraṇakāle kulaputrāścarimavijñāne vijñānanirodho nāma vātaḥ vijñānavibhramo nāma vātaḥ vijñānasaṃkṣobhasaṃyukto nāma vātaḥ ime trayaḥ kulaputrā vātā maraṇakālasamaye carimavijñāne saṃluḍanti (saṃkṣubhanti) saṃkṣobhamutpādayanti / ta āhu / katamāni bhagavan trīṇi maraṇakālasamaye vijñānanirodhe vartamāne śarīraṃ nirghātayanti / bhagavān āha - śastrakaśca nāma mārṣāḥ sūcakaśca nāma mārṣāḥ ṣṭhīlakaśca nāma; ye śarīraṃ nirghātayaṃti / āha / kimetadbhagavaṃccharīraṇ nāma; bhagavān āha - ādīptakaśca nāma mārṣā dahanavāsakaśca nāma; meḍikaśca nāma; śṛṃgārikaśca nāma / śmaśānikaśca nāma; durbuddhikaśca nāma / bhāragurukaśca nāma; jātiparipīḍitaśca nāma; jātisaṃkṣubhitaśca nāma; jīvitaparibhāvikaśca nāma; maraṇapriyaviprayogakaśca nāma; ime mārṣā ucyante śarīranāmānaḥ

[SaSū 240] ta āhu / kathaṃ bhagavan mṛyate kathaṃ jīvati / bhagavān āha - vijñānaṃ nāmāyuṣmanto mriyate / puṇyaṃ nāmāyuṣmanto jīvati / śarīraṃ nāma mārṣā mṛyate snāyukoṭībhirbaddham caturaśītibhiḥ sirākūrvasahasrai romakūpairbaddham dvādaśabhiḥ sahasrairaṃgānāṃ baddhaṃ / ṣaṣṭyuttaraistribhiḥ śatairasthīnāṃ baddham caturaśītiḥ kṛmikulaśatānyabhyantare vasanti teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ praṇakānāṃ maraṇaṃ saṃvidyate / maraṇanirodhaṃ ca saṃvidyate tatra sarve te prāṇakā nirāśā bhavanti / yadā sa puruṣo mṛyate tadā sarvaprāṇakānāṃ vātasaṃkṣobhaḥ saṃluḍati anyonyaparibhākṣanārthāya tadā te duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti / anye punaḥ putraśokaṃ kurvanti / anye duhitṛśokaṃ jñātṛśokaṃ sarve eva te śokaśalyaviddhāḥ anyonyabhakṣaṇamārabhante / sarve te anupūrveṇa parasparaṃ bhakṣayanta; dvau prāṇakāvavatiṣṭhante / tau saptāhamabhiyudhyataḥ yāva saptāhe 'tikrānte tata ekaḥ prāṇako nirmathyate / eko mucyate / tat katama āyuṣmanta ucyate dharmaḥ tatkiṃ manyadhve yathā sarvaprāṇakānāṃ anyonyanirodhena maraṇaṃ /

[SaSū 241] evameva bālapṛthagjanā sattvā anyonyaviradhamāpdyante / te jātyā na bibhyanti / vyādhibhyo na bibhyanti / maraṇā na bibhyanti yathā (tau) dvau prāṇakau yudhyataḥ evameva bālapṛthagjanāḥ parasparaṃ yudhyante / atha maraṇakālasamaye ucyate sādhu puruṣaiḥ kiṃ tvaṃ bho puruṣa viśvāsamāpadyase / kiṃ tvayā manuṣyaloke na kiṃcidādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ / na jātyā[d ā]dīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ na jarayā na vyādherādīnavo dṛṣṭa / na maraṇādādīnavo dṛṣṭa / āha / dṛṣṭo me āyuṣmanta jātyā[d ā]dīnavo jarayā vyādherādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ sarvapaścān maraṇādādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ āha / kathaṃ na kṛtāni yat karaṇīyāni kuśalamūlāni / tat kathaṃ tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa na kṛtamubhayorlokayo hitasaṃvartakāni dharmaskandhakuśalamūlāni / dvitīyaṃ mārṣāḥ pṛcchāmi / kathaṃ tvayā na kṛtaḥ kuśalamūlasaṃbhāraḥ yastvaṃ parimuktaḥ syājjātyā jarayā vyādhermaraṇāt tat kathaṃ te na kṛtaṃ yoniśomanasikārapratyavekṣaṇāṃ kiṃ tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa śrutaṃ / pṛthivyāṃ gaṇḍyāṃ ākoṭanaśabdaṃ / na ca dṛṣṭā jāṃbudvīpakā manuṣyā dānāni dadantaḥ puṇyāni ca kurvantaḥ upavāsamupavasantaḥ tathāgatakṣetre kuśalamūlabījānyavaropayantaḥ gandhaṃ vā mālyaṃ vā dīpaṃ va na tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ vā dīyamānam na ca te dṛṣṭāstathāgatasya catasraḥ parṣadaḥ santarpyamānāḥ bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā imāṃścatasraḥ parṣadaḥ śāsane 'bhinivustāḥ evaṃ tasya hitāni vadantyālapanti ca / na hi devakṛtaṃ kiṃcit asādhustvayā bhoḥ puruṣa kṛtam imimaṃ jaṃbudvīpamāgatya;
[SaSū 242] tasya mṛtasya dharmarājā tasmin kāle taṃ puruṣaṃ anuśāsan tā gāthā bhāṣate -

(83) dṛṣṭvā tathāgatotpādaḥ śrutvā gaṇḍīparāhatām
śrutvā dharman deśayamānaṃ śantaṃ nirvāṇagāminaṃ /
(84) kasmāt te na kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ paralokasukhāvaham
bhokṣyase narake duḥkham aniṣṭhakarmaṇaḥ phalam
[SaSū 243] atha sa puruṣastaṃ dharmarājānaṃ gāthābhi pratyabhāṣata -

(85) bālabuddhirahaṃ āsīt pāpamitravaśānugaḥ
kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma kāmabhrāntena cetasā //

children.text: (86) kāmaśca me citastasya āgataṃ dāruṇaṃ phalam
kṛtā me prāṇināṃ hiṃsā sāṃghikaṃ ca vināśitaṃ /
dauṣṭhulyaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ mātā me paritāpitā //

body.text:
(88) aparādhaṃ vijānāmi svaśarīreṇa yat kṛtaṃ
raurave narake paśyāmyupapattiṃ sudāruṇe /
(89) saṃghāte vedanāṃ vetsye tathaiva ca pratāpane /
mahāvīcau ca kaṭukāmanubhaviṣyāmi vedanāṃ
(90) mahāpadme ca narake krandayiṣyāmi suduḥkhitaḥ
vārā śataṃ kālasūtre utpatsyāmi mahābhaye
(91) hatāśca nārakā sattvāḥ punaḥ paśyanti te bhayam
yojanānāṃ śataṃ bhūyaḥ pratipadyanti mahābhayam
(92) dvāran te na labhiṣyanti punaḥ kuṃbhe pratāpitāḥ

children.text: kṣūraṃ tu nāma narakaṃ sahasraṃ kṣūrasaṃbhavam
(93) śatam sahasraṃ koṭīnāṃ kṣūrāṇāṃ jāyate grataḥ
taistasya bhidyante gātraṃ karmabhi duṣkṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ //

body.text:
(94) vātakṣobhā mahāghorā sarvaṃ cchindanti tāṃ tanum
anubhāvyā mayā duḥkhā īdṛśā narake dhruvam
(95) drakṣyante sarvasattvā me kāyaṃ duḥkhaprapīḍitaṃ /
arthā parakyā ādattā mayā veśmasya kāraṇāt
(96) putrā duhitaro mahya bhrātā ca bhāginī tathā
mātā pitā caiva mama mitrajñātigaṇo 'pi ca
(97) dāsakarmakarāścaiva gāvo bhṛtyaḥ paśuṃ tathā /
bhrānto smyahaṃ kukāryeṣu rupyasauvarṇabhājanaiḥ
(98) vastraistathā susūkṣmaiśca bhrāntaḥ kārāpane gṛhe
suvicitraṃ gṛhaṃ kṛtvā naranārīsamākulaṃ /
(99) vīṇāstūryāḥ parāhatya rataṃ me durdamaṃ manaḥ
gātraṃ gandhodakairliptaṃ kṛtajño 'dyāpi naiva saḥ
(100) acetana śarīrastvaṃ bhrānto 'smi tava kāraṇāt
na vidyā te mama trātā kaścit sattvaḥ punarbhavet
(101) vātakṣobhe mahāghore śarīraparitāpane /
bhuktā rasā svāduvanto jihvayā vividhāstathā
(102) śīrṣe mālāśca bahavo baddhā śvitrāḥ suśobhanāḥ
rūpeṇa bhrāmitaścakṣuścakṣutrāṇaṃ na vidyate /
(103) pāpānāṃ cakṣuṣī heturmayā dṛṣṭvātu yatkṛtam
śrotrau hetuśca me bhūyaḥ bāhū vajraparāhatāḥ
(104) hastebhyaḥ kaṭakā baddhā aṅgulīyebhi yaṃtrikā /
grīvāyāṃ muktihārāṇi pādau cāpi svalaṃkṛtau
(105) jālāni kṛtvā tatraiva sauvaraṇaṃ saṃsthitaṃ tataḥ
gātrai ca vividhā ratnā sauvarṇakaṭakāstathā /
(106) udārai ramito bhogairmanasaṃbṛhaṇairapi /
sparśaṃ ca sukumāraṃ me tṛṣṇagrastena sevitaṃ /
(107) nānāstaraṇaśayyābhiḥ kāyaḥ krīḍāpito mayā/
snāto gandhodakairviśadairgandhaiścāpi pralepitaḥ
(108) karpūracandanairdivyairdhūpanaiścāpi dhūpitaḥ
kastūrikāsamāyukto vāso varṇakaraḥ kṛtaḥ
(109) gandhavārṣikatailena sumanācaṇpakādibhiḥ
makṣitaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ vastraṃ prāvṛtaṃ sūkṣmakāśikaṃ
(110) avatīrya hastipṛṣṭhādaśvapṛṣṭhe bhiruhya ca
rājāhamiti manyāmi jano me dhāvate grataḥ
(111) antaḥpuraṃ vijānāmi gīte nṛtye suśīkṣitaḥ

children.text: nirāparādhā mṛgayā hatā kāṇḍaiśca me mṛgā
children.translated_text: Innocent deer were killed by my arrows on the hunt.
(112) Such sin was committed by me, not knowing the next world.
The finest meats were eaten by me—hence this suffering is mine.

body.translated_text:
(94) Terrible wind-disturbances tear apart that entire body;
such sufferings must certainly be experienced by me in hell.
(95) All beings will see my body afflicted with suffering;
others' wealth was taken by me for the sake of building a house.
(96) Sons, daughters are mine, brothers and sisters too,
mother and father also, and the group of friends and relatives as well.
(97) Slaves and laborers, cows, servants, and cattle too—
I was deluded in wicked deeds by vessels of silver and gold.
(98) By very fine garments too I was deluded, in the house built as a prison;
having made a splendid house, crowded with men and women—
(99) Having struck <s>vīṇās</s> and musical instruments, my uncontrollable mind delighted;
the body was anointed with perfumed water, yet even now it is not grateful.
(100) O unconscious body, I was deluded on your account;
there is no knowledge in you, no savior for me—may no being come to exist again.
(101) In the terrible wind-disturbance that torments the body,
various delicious tastes were enjoyed by the tongue.
(102) Many garlands were tied on the head, beautiful and brilliant;
the eyes were deluded by form, yet there is no protection for the eyes.
(103) The eyes were the cause of sins—by what was seen, that I did;
the ears also were a cause—moreover my arms were struck as if by a thunderbolt.
(104) Bracelets were fastened on the hands, rings with mechanisms on the fingers;
pearl necklaces on the neck, and the feet too were well-adorned.
(105) Having made golden nets right there, gold was placed upon it,
and various gems on the limbs, and golden bracelets too.
(106) Delighted with excellent pleasures and those that nourish the mind,
gentle touch was indulged by me, seized by craving.
(107) With various bedding and couches the body was made to sport by me;
bathed with perfumed water, anointed with pure fragrances.
(108) Fumigated with divine camphor, sandalwood, and incenses,
mixed with musk, garments were made colorful.
(109) Anointed with seasonal fragrant oil, with jasmine, <s>campaka</s>, and such flowers,
white garments were wrapped in fine <s>Kāśī</s> cloth.
(110) Descending from elephant-back and mounting horse-back,
I think 'I am a king'—people run before me.
(111) I know the inner palace, well-trained in song and dance.

body.text:
(113) maraṇaṃ me na vijñātamāgamiṣyati dāruṇaṃ
bālabuddhirahaṃ āsīccharīraṃ poṣitaṃ mayā /
(114) āgataṃ maraṇaṃ me dya kaścittrātā na vidyate /
yūyaṃ hi jñātayaḥ sarve mukhaṃ me kiṃ nirīkṣatha /
(115) kasmād vastraṃ pāṭayadhvaṃ pralāpaiścāpi kiṃkṛte /
keśān kasmād vikiratha raktaṃ kiṃ vā kariṣyati
(116) pāṃsuṃ ca śīrṣe kṣipatha urastāḍaṃ karotha kim
jīvaṃ nāhaṃ vāritavyaḥ pāpāt kiṃ ruditena vaḥ
(117) śarīraṃ me vṛkabhojyaṃ kurkurāṇāṃ ca vāyasām
bhaviṣyate pakṣiṇāṃ ca vṛthā puṣṭaṃ ayan tanuḥ
(118) maraṇoragasaṃspṛṣṭo jāyate 'pi sudāruṇaḥ
tathopayojyaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ yathāsmān mucyate bhayāt
(119) yan me vaidyāḥ pradāsyanti bhaiṣajyaṃ na tadiṣyate
