(120) mṛyato mama dātavyaṃ mā memaṃ saṃprayacchatha /
poṣyamāṇaśarīro yamavaśyaṃ nāśameṣyati /
(121) pāpaskandhaṃ kimākṣipya yatpaścā duḥkhadāyakam
poṣito me pṛyaṃ kāyaḥ kṛtaghnatvaṃ kariṣyati /
(122) putrā duhitaraṃ kiṃ me cakṣuṣā sannirīkṣatha /
trāyadhvamasmād rogān me rudadhvaṃ kinnirarthakam
(123) yūyaṃ hi putra duhitṛ kṛtaghnā mama sāmpratam
yuṣmākaṃ poṣaṇārthāya parakīyaṃ mayā hṛtaṃ /
(124) sāprataṃ maraṇaṃ prāptaṃ nirāśaṃ mām karotha kim
jātidurgatisaṃtrasto maraṇena ca pīḍitaḥ
(125) vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ sparṣaṃ paramavedanāḥ
tṛṣṇāyā bhrāmyate bālaḥ prāpnoti kaṭukaṃ phalaṃ;
(126) śokabandhana mahya tu jātasya viṣame kule
alpapuṇyaṃ tu māṃ jñātvā śocayiṣyantyapare janāḥ
(127) dānaśīlaparibhraṣṭo dharmāccāpi parānmukhaḥ

children.translated_text: does not know rebirth, tormented by the poison of the serpent of afflictions.

children.text: (128) bhrāmyate vidyayā bālo yatra mokṣaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: (128) The fool is led astray by ignorance, where liberation is not found.

children.text: mokṣārthaṃ na vijānāti bhrāntaḥ pāpaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: He does not understand the purpose of liberation, and deluded, commits sin.
(129) The fool is led astray by afflictions, his mind always distracted.

body.translated_text:
(113) Death was not understood by me—terrible, it will come;
I was of childish intelligence, the body was nourished by me.
(114) Death has come to me today—no savior is found;
all of you are my relatives—why do you stare at my face?
(115) Why do you tear your garments? What is accomplished by lamentations?
Why do you scatter your hair? What will blood accomplish?
(116) Why do you throw dust on your heads? Why do you beat your chests?
I, while living, should not have been restrained from sin—what use is your weeping?
(117) My body will be food for wolves, dogs, and crows;
it will belong to birds as well—in vain was this body nourished.
(118) Touched by the serpent of death, even being born is terrible;
medicine should be applied such that one is freed from this fear.
(119) Whatever medicines the physicians will give me, that is not what is needed;
now the medicine of <s>Dharma</s>, which liberates from the serpent of afflictions—
(120) should be given to me as I die—do not give me that other!
This body that is nourished will necessarily come to destruction.
(121) Why heap up the mass of sin that later brings suffering?
This beloved body nourished by me will become ungrateful.
(122) Sons, daughter—why do you look at me with those eyes?
Save me from this disease—what use is your pointless weeping?
(123) You, sons and daughters, are now ungrateful to me;
for the sake of nourishing you, others' property was taken by me.
(124) Now death has arrived—why do you make me hopeless?
Terrified by the misfortune of rebirth and tormented by death,
(125) feelings, perceptions, mental formations, contact, and supreme sensations—
the fool is led astray by craving and obtains bitter fruit.
(126) The bondage of grief is mine, born in a troubled family;
knowing me to have little merit, others will grieve for me.
(127) Fallen from generosity and moral conduct, turned away from the <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text:
dahyate hyagninā dīptaḥ kāyo vividhabandhanaḥ
(130) vibhrānto bhramate kāyo yatra saukhyaṃ na vidyate /

children.translated_text: And that happiness which brings inner bliss is not known.
(131) The field that gives happiness to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma), the great remedy,
moral conduct and truth of the virtuous, the sacred sounds of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.translated_text:
Blazing, he is burned by fire, the body bound in various fetters;
(130) bewildered, the body wanders where happiness is not found.

body.text: [SaSū 244] atha khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayetadavocat - evaṃ ca bhaiṣajyasena sattvā maraṇakāle paridevanti / na na hi teṣāṃ kaścittrātā bhaviṣyatyanyatra sukṛtānāṃ karmāṇāṃ phalavipākaṃ ca gāthā cemā bhāṣate //
body.translated_text: [SaSū 244] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> and said: "Thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, beings lament at the time of death. For indeed there is no savior for them except the ripening fruit of well-performed deeds." And he spoke these verses:

body.text:
(132) kṛtvā tu pāpakaṃ karma narakeṣu patanti hi
bhuṃjante cīmaraṃ taptaṃ pīvante lohapānakam
(133) kāyebhyo varṣate 'ṅgāraṃ dagdhāḥ krandanti dāruṇam
dahyatyeṣāṃ taccharīraṃ narakesmin mahābhaye /
(134) na vijānanti saukhyāni dharmaṃ ca na vijānate
bālo bhramatyadharmeṇa saukhyaṃ nāpnoti kiṃcana;
(135) śraddhāśīlena saṃpannaḥ prajñāyukto mahātapāḥ
mitraṃ bhajati kalyāṇaṃ śīghraṃ bhoti tathāgataḥ
(136) vīryamārabhate śreyaṃ buddhalokopapattaye
deśetha kuśalaṃ dharmaṃ sarvasattvaparigrahaṃ
(137) maitraṃ cittaṃ samāpanno brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ
śrutvaivaṃ bhaiṣajyasena pratipattiparo bhavet
(138) vimuktidarśanaṃ buddhaṃ guṣṭaśabdaṃ vināyakaṃ /

lokasya mātāpitaraṃ bodhicittaṃ taducyate /
(139) kalyāṇamitrāṃ paramāṃ suduṣkaraṃ yo deśayet
[[iha]] dharma loke śṛṇvanti ye gauravādbuddhaśāsanaṃ

children.translated_text: they become <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones), the best of men.
(140) They become the protectors of the world, the liberators of all beings,
those who are reverential toward the peaceful <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields).

body.translated_text:
is the mother and father of the world; that is called <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening).
(139) The supreme virtuous friend—rare indeed is the one who would teach
the <s>Dharma</s> here in the world; those who hear the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching with reverence,

body.text: [SaSū 245] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kim idaṃ bhagavan pṛthivī kaṃpati saṃprakaṃpati / evamukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - vyavalokaya bhaiṣajyasena kiṃ paśyasi / vyavalokitaṃ bhaiṣajyasenena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / atha tāvadeva caturbhyo digbhyaḥ paśyati / pṛthivīvivaraṃ dadāti / pṛthivyā vivṛtāyāṃ paśyati / pṛthivīvivarebhyo viṃśati koṭyo manuṣyāṇāṃ jāyante / adhastāddiśi viṃśati koṭyo manuṣyānāṃ jāyante / ūrdhvāyāṃ diśāyāṃ paṃcaviṃśati koṭyo manuṣyānāṃ jāyante /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 245] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Why is it, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that the earth trembles and shakes greatly?" Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: "Look, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, what do you see?" The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> looked. Then at that very moment he saw from the four directions—the earth gave way with openings. When the earth opened, he saw—from the openings of the earth, twenty <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of human beings were born. From the direction below, twenty <s>koṭis</s> of human beings were born. From the direction above, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of human beings were born.

body.text: [SaSū 246] atha te daharāḥ sattvā vyavalokya bhagavantametadavocan katame bhagavanniha jātā / bhagavān āha - paśyatha yūyamime janakāyāḥ ta āhuḥ paśyāmo bhagavan bhagavān āha - ime janakāyā yuṣmākaṃ sakhāyā jātāḥ ta āhuḥ eteṣāmapi bhagavan sattvānāṃ maraṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti; bhagavān āha - evametan mārṣāḥ sarvasattvānāmapi maraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 246] Then those young beings, having looked at the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said: "Who, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is born here?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Do you see these groups of people?" They said: "We see them, <s>Bhagavān</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "These groups of people are born as your companions." They said: "Will death also come to these beings, <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Even so, good sirs, death will come to all beings."

body.text: [SaSū 247] atha te pūrvimakā sattvā daharāḥ ye prathamataramutpannāste yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocan - notsahāmo vayaṃ punarbhagavaṃ jātiṃ maraṇaṃ ca draṣṭum bhagavān āha - tatkiṃ yūyamutsahatha vīryavalālabdham ta āhuḥ tathāgataṃ saṃmukhaṃ paśyemaḥ tasya ca sakāśāddharmaśravaṇaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ manāpaṃ śṛṇuyāmaḥ tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghaṃ ca niṣaṇṇaṃ paśyemaḥ bodhisattvān mahardhikān mahānubhāvān paśyemaḥ īdṛśaṃ ca bhagavannotsahāmo jātiṃ maraṇaṃ ca draṣṭum
body.translated_text: [SaSū 247] Then those earlier young beings who had been born first, joining their palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'We cannot bear, Blessed One, to see birth and death again.' The Blessed One said: 'Then what can you bear? What strength of effort have you obtained?' They said: 'May we see the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face! May we hear from his presence the pleasant, agreeable hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>! May we see the assembly of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> disciples seated! May we see the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great miraculous power and great majesty! But such as this, Blessed One, we cannot bear to see birth and death.'

body.text: [SaSū 248] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo ṛddhibalenotthāyāsanāt sārdhaṃ taiḥ paṃcabhirbodhisattvaśataiḥ te sarve ṛddhyā utthāyoparyantarīkṣe caṃkramanti / paryaṃkañca badhvā dhyāyanti / teṣāṃ sarvakāyebhyaḥ siṃhā niṣkrāmanti / vyāghrā niṣkrāmanti / vyāḍā niṣkrāmanti / hastino niṣkrāmanti / mahāṛddhivikurvitāni darśayanti / parvateṣu ca paryaṃkaṃ badhvā niṣīdanti / viṃśatiryojanasahasrāṇyūrdhvamāruhanti / daśa koṭīsahasrāṇi candramasūryāṇi-m-avataranti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 248] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, rising from his seat by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous ability), together with those five hundred <s>bodhisattvas</s>—they all, rising by miraculous power, walked about in the sky above. And sitting cross-legged, they meditated. From all their bodies, lions emerged; tigers emerged; serpents emerged; elephants emerged. They displayed great miraculous transformations. They sat cross-legged upon mountains. They ascended upward twenty thousand <s>yojanas</s>. They descended into ten thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of suns and moons.

body.text: [SaSū 249] atha khalu te daharāḥ sattvā bhagavantametadavocan - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahāraśmyāvabhāsasya mahacca ṛddhivikurvitā loke prādurbhūtāḥ bhagavān āha - paśyatha kulaputrā etau candrasūryau prādurbhūtau / ta āhu / paśyāmo bhadanta bhagavan paśyāmo bhadanta sugata; bhagavān āha - eṣa bodhisattvaiḥ svakāyād raśmyāvabhāso ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ ca darśitaṃ sandarśayitvā sattvānān dharman deśayanti / bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukaṃpāyairmahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ihaiva te mānuṣyake kāye vīryabalamupadarśayitvā īdṛśam ṛddhibalamupadarśayanti / āha / deśayatu bhagavān raśmyāvabhāsaprādurbhāvāya dharmam
body.translated_text: [SaSū 249] Then those young beings said this to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause? What is the condition for this great radiant illumination and great miraculous transformations appearing in the world?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you see, sons of good family, these suns and moons that have appeared?' They said: 'We see them, venerable Blessed One; we see them, venerable <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'This radiant illumination and miraculous display have been shown by the <s>bodhisattvas</s> from their own bodies. Having shown them, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans. Right here, in this human body, having demonstrated the power of effort, they display such power of <s>ṛddhi</s>.' He said: 'May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the manifestation of radiant illumination.'

body.text: [SaSū 250] evamukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakaṃpitaḥ āha / paśyāmi bhagavaṃ paśyāmi sugata / tasya mama bhagavannevaṃ bhavatvahaṃ tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripṛccheyaṃ / bhagavān āha - pṛccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena yadyadevākāṃkṣasyahaṃ te tasya tasyaiva praśnasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi nirdekṣyāmi vibhajiṣyāmi / bhaiṣajyasena yadatītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasu tatsarvaṃ darśayiṣyāmi / āha / deśayatu me bhagavan kaukṛtyavinodanārthaṃ / ihāhaṃ bhagavan paśyāmi tathāgataṃ caturaśītibhirdevaputrasahasraiḥ parivṛtaṃ caturaśītibhiḥ koṭīsahasrairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaṃ; dvādaśabhiḥ koṭīsahasrairnāgarājñāṃ parivṛtaṃ / aṣṭādaśabhiḥ koṭīsahasrairbhūtānāṃ parivṛtaṃ paṃcaviṃśatibhiḥ koṭīsahasraiḥ pretapiśācaiḥ parivṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 250] When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) realm trembling in six ways?' He said: 'I see it, Blessed One; I see it, <s>Sugata</s>. It is my wish, Blessed One, to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter.' The Blessed One said: 'Ask, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, whatever you wish. I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question; I shall explain and analyze. <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, whatever pertains to the past, future, and present ages—all that I shall show you.' He said: 'May the Blessed One teach me for the removal of my remorse. Here, Blessed One, I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> surrounded by eighty-four thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), surrounded by eighty-four thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, surrounded by twelve thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>nāga</s> kings, surrounded by eighteen thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), surrounded by twenty-five thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) and <s>piśācas</s> (demons).'

body.text: [SaSū 251] bhagavān āha - nūnamete bhaiṣajyasena sattvāḥ ya iha parṣadi mamāntike sannipatitā sanniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya / ta ete bhaiṣajyasenādyaiva saṃsāraṃ paścanmukhaṃ kariṣyanti / adyaiva daśabhūmipratilābhino bhaviṣyanti / daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā nirvāṇadhātaumanuprāpsyanti / sarvasattvahitaiṣiṇaḥ jarāmaraṇaparimokṣaṇārthāya kṛtadharmāḥ sukhāvahāḥ kleśapāśaṃ nirjitvā prāpsyante buddhaśāsanāṃ / āha / kimete bhagavan sattvā bahūni sattvasthānāni nānāvicitraiḥ karmabhiṛ utpannāni / te bhagavantaṃ parivāryāvasthitāni
body.translated_text: [SaSū 251] The Blessed One said: 'Surely, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those beings who have assembled here in my presence, seated in this assembly for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>—they, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, today itself will turn their backs on <s>saṃsāra</s>. Today itself they will become attainers of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). Established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, they will enter the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Seeking the welfare of all beings, for the sake of liberation from old age and death, having fulfilled the <s>Dharma</s>, bringing happiness, having conquered the bonds of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), they will attain the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching.' He said: 'Are these beings, Blessed One, born in many states of existence through various and diverse <s>karmas</s>? They stand surrounding the Blessed One.'

body.text: bhagavān āha - śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>.'

body.text:
āha ca -
(141) mūḍhāḥ sattvā na jānanti kuto mokṣo bhaviṣyati /
bahavo navakāḥ sattvāḥ adya prāpsyanti dhāraṇim
(142) jñāsyante te sarvadharmān prāptaye daśabhūmināṃ
bhūmayo daśa prāpsyanti buddhakṛtyaṃ kariṣyataḥ
(143) vartiṣyanti dharmacakraṃ dharmavarṣaṃ pravarṣiṣūḥ
ramaṇīyaṃ śāsanaṃ mahyaṃ yena sattvāḥ samāgatāḥ
(144) devanāgāśca pretāśca asurāśca sudāruṇāḥ
daśabhūmipratiṣṭhante dharmaśabdaparāhatāḥ

children.translated_text: (145) 'I sound the <s>Dharma</s> drum; I fill the <s>Dharma</s> conch.'
'Today, for these new beings, strength of effort will arise.'

children.text: (146) dharmaṃ prāpsyanti adyeme yathā prāptaṃ tathāgataiḥ //
children.translated_text: (146) 'Today they will attain the <s>Dharma</s> as attained by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.translated_text:
And he spoke:
(141) 'Deluded beings do not know whence liberation will come;
many new beings today will attain <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention).'
(142) 'They will know all <s>dharmas</s> for the attainment of the ten <s>bhūmis</s>;
they will attain the ten <s>bhūmis</s> and perform the <s>Buddha's</s> work.'
(143) 'They will turn the <s>Dharma</s> wheel; they will rain the <s>Dharma</s> rain.
Delightful is my teaching, by which beings have gathered together.'
(144) 'Gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, and <s>asuras</s>, terrible ones—
established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, struck by the sound of <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 252] atha paṃcamātrāṇi sahasrāṇi daharāṇāṃ sattvānāmutthāyāsanebhyo yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadavocan -
body.translated_text: [SaSū 252] Then five thousand young beings, rising from their seats, joining their palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One:

body.text:
(147) gurubhāro bhagavan kāyo dāruṇaśca mahābhaya /
saṃsāre yena badhyāmaḥ paryantamavijānakāḥ
(148) mārgan tu na vijānāmo mārgameva na dṛśyate /
andhabhūtā vayaṃ nātha asmākaṃ kuru saṃgrahaṃ /
(149) adhyeṣāma vayaṃ vīra dharman deśaya nāyaka;

children.text: alpaprajñā vayaṃ jātā anabhijñāḥ sukhasya hi;
children.translated_text: 'Born with little wisdom are we, ignorant of happiness indeed.'

children.text: (150) dharman deśaya asmākaṃ duḥkhān mocaya dāruṇāt
children.translated_text: (150) 'Teach the <s>Dharma</s> to us; liberate us from terrible suffering!'
'Wherever we may be reborn, may there be the seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>!'

body.translated_text:
(147) 'Heavy is the burden of the body, Blessed One, terrible and fearful;
by which we are bound in <s>saṃsāra</s>, not knowing its end.'
(148) 'We do not know the path; the path itself is not seen.
We are blind, O Protector—gather us in your care!'
(149) 'We beseech you, O Hero; teach the <s>Dharma</s>, O Guide!'

body.text: [SaSū 253] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena te daharā sattvāstenopasaṃkrāmadupasaṃkramya tān daharān sattvāṅ gāthāyā adhyabhāṣatā -
body.translated_text: [SaSū 253] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> approached those young beings. Having approached, he addressed those young beings with a verse:

body.text:
(151) bhūṃjadhvaṃ bhojanaṃ yūyaṃ pivadhvaṃ rasamadbhutam
paścādviśāradā bhūtvā dharmaṃ śroṣyatha nirbhayaṃ /
body.translated_text:
(151) 'Eat your food, all of you; drink this wondrous juice.
Afterward, becoming confident, you shall hear the <s>Dharma</s> fearlessly.'

body.text:
ta āhuḥ -
(152) bhadanta sthavira kastvaṃ najānīmo vayaṃ tava;
prāsādikastvaṃ paśyāmaḥ śāntarūpaṃ mahāyaśaḥ
(153) muktaṃ narakatiryakṣuḥ pretalokān mahābhayāt
śāntaste sarvapāpāni yathā jagati śobhase
(154) paśyāma haste karakaṃ saptaratnasamanvitam
sūtraṃ ratnāmayaṃ kāye tejarāśau viveṣṭitaṃ /
(155) prativoḍhuṃ na śaktā sma śāntavākyasya te vaca /
bhaktena kāryaṃ nāsmākaṃ pānena svādunā na ca /
(156) bhaktāduccāra saṃbhavati pānān mūtraṃ tathaiva ca /
śoṇitaṃ ca rasādbhavati raktān māṃsaṃ ca saṃbhavet
(157) nāsmākaṃ bhojanaṃ kāryaṃ pānān caiva sausaṃskṛtaṃ;
vastrāṇi naiva sūkṣmāṇi paṭṭāpaṭṭakasaṃhitā /
(158) kaṭakāśca na sauvarṇāḥ kāryā muktilatā na ca;
aṅguliyairnaiva kāryaṃ sarve te nityadharmiṇaḥ
(159) jīvitairarthikāśca sma na ca gacchema durgatim
arthikā dharmadānena na devānāṃ sukhairapi;
(160) kalyāṇamitratā kāryā na rājyaṃ cakravartināṃ /
cakravartī mariṣyanti tyaktvā dvīpān suśobhanāṃ /
(161) na putrāḥ pṛṣṭhato yānti na bhāryā na ca dhītarāḥ
saptaratnā nivartyante nāpi yāsyanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
(162) saṃnnipātya bahujano na ca yāsyanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
purataśca na dhāvante vaśaṃ bhūyo na vartati /
(163) ekajanmikarājāno bhrāmitā nityayā bahu;
kṛtvā pāpāni karmāṇi rauravaṃ prapatanti te /
(164) caturdiśaṃ paryaṇvitvā saptaratnairmahardhikaiḥ
yāsyate kva ca sā ṛddhiryadā vatsyati raurave /
(165) mṛtā ṛddhiṃ na śaknonti yatra bhūmirna vidyate
sthavira śṛṇuṣva asmākaṃ gaccha yena tathāgataḥ
(166) kāṃkṣāma darśanaṃ tasya mātāpitroryathaiva hi /
nāsmākaṃ vidyate mātā na pitā bhrātarau na ca
(167) saiva lokagururmātā pitā caiva tathāgataḥ
saiva candraśca sūryaśca kṣemamārgapradarśakaḥ
(168) mocakaḥ sa hi saṃsārād yena bhūyo na jāyate /
sa nāvātarako oghāt kleśoghācca mahābhayāt
(169) tena pratāritāḥ sattvāḥ na bhūyo vinivartitā
saddharmo deśitastena agrabodhīya kāraṇāt
(170) nāsmākaṃ bhojanenārtho na rājyaphalakāṃkṣiṇaḥ
na devalokagamanaṃ kāryaṃ narakabhīrubhiḥ
(171) sukhaṃ mānuṣyakaṃ janma dṛśyate yatra sarvavit
alpāyuṣāśca dṛśyante duṣkṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ svakaiḥ
(172) rajyante kāmabhogaiste vindanti maraṇaṃ na ca;
jānanti na ca bhāyante nirodhotpādavāṃcitāḥ
(173) sukṣmān dharmān na jānanti sūkṣmaṃ kāryaṃ na kurvante /
śāntaṃ dhātuṃ na jānanti avidyākrāntacetasaḥ
(174) cyavanto na ca khidyante jāyantaśca punaḥ puna
dīrgharātraṃ duḥkhahatā nityatā daṇḍatāḍitāḥ
(175) parakīyaṃ hariṣyanti ghātyante bandhane tathā /
paṃcabandhanabaddhāste pūrvapāpena coditāḥ
(176) nirāśāśca mariṣyanti śokaśalyasamarpitā /
niruddhyamāne vijñāne karuṇaṃ paridevate /
(177) ko nu trātā bhaveyurme sarvān bhogān dadāmyahaṃ /
suvarṇarupyasphaṭikaṃ dāso 'pi ca bhavāmyahaṃ /
(178) sarvaṃ karma kariṣyāmi dāsayogyaṃ ca yadbhavet
na rājyabhogairme kāryaṃ na dhānyena dhanena ca /
(179) svaśarīreṇa me kāryaṃ pāpakārī na mucyate
evaṃ hi sthavirāsmākaṃ na kāryaṃ bhojanaṃ bhavet
(180) rājāno 'pi mariṣyanti yairbhuktaṃ mṛṣṭabhojanam
devaputrā mariṣyanti pītvā vai pānamuttamam
(181) nānārasamāyuktaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ pānabhojanam
ānīya purato rājā jihvayā spṛśati bhojana /
(182) rasagṛddhā hi rājānaḥ pāpaṃ kurvantyanalpakaṃ /
rajyantyanityehi rasehi yatra sāraṃ na vidyate /
(183) pānaṃ na kāryaṃ asmākaṃ na ca kāryaṃ hi bhojanaṃ /
dharmatā īdṛśī kāryā duḥkhān mucyema yadvayam
(184) tṛṣṇābandhananirmuktaṃ tṛṣṇākleśavimokṣanam
sarvabandhananirmuktaṃ taṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
(185) vayaṃ hi śaraṇaṃ yāmo lokanāthaṃ maharṣiṇam
vandanāya vayaṃ yāmaḥ sattvānāṃ priyadarśanam
(186) nāmaṃ tava na jānāmo nāmamācakṣva śobhanaṃ /
body.translated_text:
They said:
(152) Venerable elder, who are you? We do not know you; we see you as gracious, of peaceful form, of great renown.
(153) Freed from the hells, animal realms, and the worlds of <s>pretas</s>, from great fear; all your sins are pacified—how you shine in the world!
(154) We see in your hand a vessel adorned with the seven jewels, a <s>sūtra</s> made of jewels on your body, enveloped in a mass of radiance.
(155) We are unable to bear the words of your peaceful speech. We have no need for food, nor for sweet drink.
(156) From food arises excrement, from drink arises urine likewise; blood arises from vital fluid, and from blood flesh may arise.
(157) We have no need for food, nor for well-prepared drink; nor for fine garments, nor for silk and cotton fabrics.
(158) Nor should golden bracelets be made, nor liberation-garlands; nor should rings be used—all these are subject to impermanence.
(159) We desire life itself, and we would not go to the lower realms; we desire the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, not even the pleasures of the gods.
(160) Spiritual friendship (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>) should be cultivated, not the kingdoms of <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs). <s>Cakravartins</s> will die, having abandoned their beautiful continents.
(161) Sons do not follow behind, nor wives, nor daughters; the seven treasures turn back and will not follow behind.
(162) Having assembled many people, they will not follow behind; they do not run before, and no more do they remain under one's control.
(163) Kings of a single birth, wandered greatly through perpetuity; having done sinful <s>karmas</s>, they fall into <s>Raurava</s> hell.
(164) Having traversed the four directions with the seven treasures of great power, where will that prosperity go when one dwells in <s>Raurava</s>?
(165) The dead cannot [take their] prosperity where there is no ground. Elder, listen to us—go to where the <s>Tathāgata</s> is!
(166) We long for the sight of him, just as for mother and father. We have no mother, no father, no brothers.
(167) He alone is the world-teacher, mother and father—the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He alone is the moon and sun, the guide showing the path of safety.
(168) He is the liberator from <s>saṃsāra</s>, by whom one is not born again. He is the ferry-man from the flood, from the flood of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of great fear.
(169) By him beings have been carried across, never to return again. The true <s>Dharma</s> was taught by him for the sake of supreme awakening.
(170) We have no need for food, nor do we desire the fruits of kingship; nor should there be going to the world of the gods for those who fear hell.
(171) Happy is human birth, where the all-knowing one is seen; and those of short life are seen, by their own evil <s>karmas</s>.
(172) They are attached to sensual pleasures, yet they encounter death; they do not know and they are not afraid, deceived by cessation and arising.
(173) They do not know the subtle <s>dharmas</s>, they do not perform subtle deeds; they do not know the peaceful element (<s>śānta dhātu</s>), their minds overcome by ignorance.
(174) Falling away, they are not distressed; being born again and again, struck by suffering for a long night, ever beaten by punishment.
(175) They will steal another's [property]; they are slain and bound likewise. Bound by the five bonds, impelled by former sin.
(176) Hopeless, they will die, pierced by the arrow of grief. When consciousness is obstructed, they lament pitifully.
(177) 'Who will be my savior? I will give all my possessions! Gold, silver, crystal—I will even become a slave!'
(178) 'I will do all work, whatever is fit for a slave. I have no need for the enjoyments of kingship, nor for grain, nor for wealth.'
(179) 'I have need only for my own body—an evildoer is not liberated.' Thus, elder, for us there should be no food.
(180) Even kings will die, who have eaten fine meals; even <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) will die, having drunk the finest drink.
(181) Food and drink prepared with various flavors— the king brings it before him and touches the food with his tongue.
(182) Kings greedy for tastes commit no small sin; they are attached to impermanent tastes where there is no essence.
(183) We should not have drink, nor should we have food; such is the nature of <s>Dharma</s> that should be practiced—may we be freed from suffering!
(184) Free from the bond of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), liberated from the affliction of craving, freed from all bonds—we have gone for refuge to that <s>Buddha</s>.
(185) We indeed go for refuge to the Lord of the World, the great sage; we go to pay homage to him who is a pleasing sight for beings.
(186) We do not know your name—tell us your auspicious name!

body.text:
bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattva āha -
yūyaṃ hi śrotumicchadhvaṃ nāmaṃ sarvajanasya ca /
(187) vṛtaḥ koṭīśatasahasrairnavakaiḥ sattvaistathāgataḥ
ta āhuḥ tava tu śrotumicchāmo nāmaṃ sarvaguṇodbhavaṃ /
(188) gaṃbhīraṃ śrūyate nāma yastvaṃ buddhānā śrāvakaḥ āha /
bhaiṣajyaseno nāmnāhaṃ sattvānāṃ bhaiṣajyo hyahaṃ
(189) yuṣmākaṃ deśayaiṣyāmi sarveṣāmauṣadhaṃ varaṃ /
sarvavyādhipraśamanaṃ sarvavyādhihate jane /
(190) rāgo vyādhirmahāvyādhirloke naśyati dāruṇaḥ

children.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is a disease, a great and terrible one, by which the unwise wander.
(191) Beings go to hell, and likewise to the realms of animals and <s>pretas</s>;

children.text: dveṣagrastā ime bālāsteṣāṃ śāntiḥ kathaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: these fools, seized by <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred)—how shall there be peace for them?

body.translated_text:
The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said:
You indeed wish to hear the name of all people.
(187) The <s>Tathāgata</s> is surrounded by nine hundred <s>koṭī</s>-hundred-thousands of new beings.
They said: We wish to hear from you the name that is the source of all virtues.
(188) A profound name is heard—you who are a disciple of the <s>Buddhas</s>! He said:
<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> is my name; I am the medicine for beings.
(189) I will teach to you the supreme medicine for all, the pacifier of all diseases, for people struck by all diseases.
(190) <s>Rāga</s> (passion) is a disease, a great disease that destroys terribly in the world.

body.text:
ta āhuḥ -
(192) mucyema sarvaduḥkhātaḥ śrutvā dharmamimaṃ śubhaṃ /
muktaśca sarvaduḥkhebhyo bālabuddhirajānakāḥ
(193) śroṣyāmahe dharmadānaṃ pāpakarmavivarjitāḥ
sarvapāpaṃ vivarjitvā prahīṇabhayabhairavāḥ
(194) drakṣyāma śīghraṃ saṃbuddhaṃ sarvavyādhipramocakaṃ /
vaidyarājaṃ mahāvaidyaṃ duḥkhitānāṃ cikitsakaṃ /
(195) gaccha sthavira śīghraṃ tvaṃ vandanāya tathāgataṃ /
vandasva cāsmadvacanā brūhi lokavināyakaṃ /
(196) praśāmaya imaṃ vyādhiṃ praśamayāgniṃ sudāruṇam
kāyo yaṃ jvalitaḥ sarvo dahyamāno na śāmyate /
(197) duḥkhārditānāmasmākaṃ kāryuṇyaṃ kuru subrata;
kāyabhāro mahābhārastīkṣṇabhāraḥ sudāruṇaḥ
(198) dveṣamohasamākrānta udvahanti janāḥ sadā;
punaḥ punarbahaṃtyete mokṣabhāraṃ ajānakāḥ
(199) martavyaṃ na vijānante trāso notpadyate tha ca /
mokṣamārgaṃ ajānānā mokṣamārgamapaśyakāḥ
(200) asmākaṃ maraṇaṃ nāsti kadāciditi susthitāḥ
saṃbhrāntā na vijānanti paśyanto mātaraṃ mṛtā;
(201) pitaraṃ na smarantyanye nityaṃ ca vyādhipīḍitāḥ
kleśakarmapraluḍitāḥ kathaṃ bhūṃjāma bhojanaṃ /
(202) duḥkhāntaṃ na vijānāmaḥ śramāmo 'tha nirarthakaṃ /
asmākamīdṛśān duḥkhāṃ jātyavidyānidānataḥ
(203) mahābhayaṃ gurubhāraṃ saṃjñāsaṃskāravedanā /
tṛṣṇāyā bhrāmyate bālo yo dharmaṃ na vijānate /
(204) jāto loke hyanarthāya kāyabhāraparivṛta
snānānulepanaiḥ kāryaṃ śucirvastraṃ suśobhanaṃ;
(205) mṛṣṭaṃ ca bhojanaṃ kāryaṃ yaccharīre manoramaṃ /
paṃcatūryāmanojñaṃ ca śrotraṃ yācayate tathā /
(206) saptaratnasamutthāne rūpe rajyanti cakṣuṣī /
sarvaṃ rasaṃ ca mṛṣṭaṃ ca jihvā yācayate 'pi ca /
(207) sparśaṃ ca mṛdukaṃ sūkṣmaṃ kāyaḥ prārthayate sadā /
māṃsadvayaṃ śarīreṇa niṣpīḍya ratī jāyate /
(208) kāyo hyacetano hyeṣa ratiṃ kastatra vindati /
pādau me ramatastatra prāvṛtaṃ carma sundaraṃ /
(209) bhavanti maraṇatrāṇa na vastraṃ na vilepanam
bhaveccharīraṃ na trāṇaṃ kiṃ punarvastralepanaṃ /
(210) puruṣa ucyate kāyameti śvāsaṃ mahābalaṃ
tīkṣṇaṃ balaṃ pratisaṃkhyā taṃ taccharīre mahāguṇaṃ /
(211) krīḍayā bhrāmitaḥ pūrvamaśvahastiparivṛtaḥ
mokṣadharmamajānāno rato 'haṃ pāpakarmaṇi /
(212) krīḍyā kārāpitaṃ pāpaṃ paralokamajānatā;
punaḥ punaśca jāto 'haṃ punarmaraṇamāgataḥ
(213) śokaḥ punaḥ punardṛṣṭaṃ paridevitabandhanaṃ /
mātṝṇāṃ maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭāśca pitaro mṛtā /
(214) jñātayo bhaginī caiva putrā bhāryā mṛtāpi ca /
śūnyāḥ sarve hi saṃskārāḥ ko hi rajyet sacetanaḥ
(215) viśvāsaṃ hi mayā jñātaṃ lobhagrastena cetasā;
śāntaṃ dharmaṃ nopalabdhaṃ maraṇaṃ nābhinanditaṃ /
(216) tena dānaṃ na dattaṃ me lobhenāvṛtacetasā;
kaḥ syā lobhasamo pāpo yo 'dyāpi na nivartate /
(217) saṃbhrāntā hi vayaṃ jātāḥ saṃbhrāntaṃ sakalaṃ jagat
saṃbhrāntāḥ śabdaṃ śṛṇumo asaddharmaparigrahaṃ /
(218) mokṣaṃ dhyānāśca margāmaḥ śarīraṃ nodvahāmahe /
buddhā bhavema lokārthe śāstāro guravo jage /
(219) buddho mātāpitā loke buddho mārgapradarśakaḥ
pravarṣate dharmavarṣaṃ jaṃbudvīpe samantataḥ
(220) mūḍhā sattvā na jānanti dharmāṇāṃ saṃgrahaṃ kathaṃ /
bodhau cittaṃ nāmayitvā labhyate dharmasaṃgrahaḥ
(221) śunyatāḥ sarvasasṃkārāḥ śunyā bhogā dhanaṃ tathā /
paśyāma śunyamātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā jātā nirāśatā;
(222) sthavira bhaiṣajyasena-m-asmākaṃ vacanaṃ śṛṇu;
dūraṃ ca te visarjema bodhisattvānā kāraṇāt
(223) bodhisattvā na khidyante vīryavanto mahātapāḥ
smṛtvā saṃsāradoṣāṇi kurvante guṇasaṃgrahaṃ;
(224) gacchasva yena śāstāsau pṛccha cāsmāka kāranāt
pratilabdhasukhaḥ śāstā mā kiṃcit khidyate jinaḥ
(225) parājitastvayā māraḥ sabalaśca savāhanaḥ
śīghramujvālitaṃ dharmaṃ sarvasattvasukhāvahaṃ /
(226) na cāsmābhiḥ śruto dharmo yena buddhā bhavemahe /

children.translated_text: 'Go quickly, Elder, for the sake of our welfare!'
(227) 'We shall not cross over until we see the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
the bearer of the thirty-two marks; we all stand with reverence.'

body.translated_text:
They said:
(192) 'May we be freed from all suffering, having heard this auspicious <s>Dharma</s>!
Freed from all sufferings, we of childish understanding, ignorant ones,
(193) shall hear the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, free from sinful deeds,
having abandoned all sin, with fear and terror eliminated.
(194) May we quickly see the fully awakened <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, the liberator from all ailments,
the king of physicians, the great physician, the healer of the suffering!
(195) Go quickly, Elder, to pay homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>!
Pay homage on our behalf, and speak to the Guide of the World:
(196) "Pacify this disease, quench this terrible fire!
This entire body is ablaze, burning and finding no peace.
(197) Show compassion to us who are afflicted by suffering, O one of good vows!
The burden of the body is a great burden, a sharp burden, terrible indeed.
(198) Overcome by hatred and delusion, people always carry it;
again and again they bear it, ignorant of the burden of liberation.
(199) They do not know that they must die, and yet no fear arises in them;
not knowing the path to liberation, not seeing the path to liberation.
(200) 'Our death will never come' — thus they stand complacent;
bewildered, they do not understand, even seeing their mother dead.
(201) Others do not remember their father, constantly afflicted by disease,
tormented by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s> — how can we eat our food?
(202) We do not know the end of suffering; we toil pointlessly.
Such sufferings of ours arise from birth and ignorance as their cause.
(203) Great fear, heavy burden, perception, formations, and feeling —
the fool wanders through <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), one who does not know the <s>Dharma</s>.
(204) Born in the world to no purpose, encircled by the burden of the body,
bathing and ointments must be done, clean garments beautifully adorned;
(205) fine food must be provided, whatever is pleasing to the body,
and the ear likewise craves delightful music of the five instruments.
(206) The eyes delight in forms arising from the seven jewels,
and the tongue too craves all flavors, both delicious and refined.
(207) The body always desires soft and subtle touch;
by pressing together two pieces of flesh with the body, pleasure arises.
(208) Yet this body is unconscious — who finds pleasure there?
My feet delight there, wrapped in beautiful skin.
(209) Neither clothing nor ointment can be a protection against death;
the body itself is no protection — how much less clothing and ointment!
(210) A person is called a body, breathing with great force;
sharp is that force of discernment, that great quality in the body.
(211) In play I was led astray before, surrounded by horses and elephants,
not knowing the <s>Dharma</s> of liberation, I delighted in sinful deeds.
(212) Evil was done through play by one ignorant of the next world;
again and again I was born, and again death came upon me.
(213) Grief was seen again and again, the bondage of lamentation;
the death of mothers was seen, and fathers too were seen dead.
(214) Relatives and sisters, sons and wives also died;
empty are all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) — what conscious being would take delight?
(215) Trust was known by me, with a mind seized by greed;
the peaceful <s>Dharma</s> was not attained, death was not welcomed.
(216) Therefore no gift was given by me, with a mind covered by greed;
what sin equals greed, which even now does not cease?
(217) Bewildered indeed were we born, bewildered is the entire world;
bewildered, we hear sounds, the embrace of false <s>dharmas</s>.
(218) May we seek liberation and the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations); may we not carry this body!
May we become <s>Buddhas</s> for the sake of the world, teachers and masters in the world!
(219) The <s>Buddha</s> is mother and father in the world, the <s>Buddha</s> is the shower of the path;
he rains the rain of <s>Dharma</s> throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s> on all sides.
(220) Deluded beings do not know how to gather the <s>Dharmas</s>;
by inclining the mind toward awakening, the gathering of <s>Dharma</s> is obtained.
(221) Empty are all <s>saṃskāras</s>, empty are enjoyments and wealth;
we see the self as empty, and having seen this, despondency has arisen.
(222) Elder <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, hear our words!
We send you far away, for the sake of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
(223) <s>Bodhisattvas</s> do not grow weary, heroic in effort, great in austerity;
remembering the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, they accumulate virtues.
(224) Go to where that Teacher is, and ask on our behalf!
The Teacher has attained happiness — may the Conqueror not be troubled in any way.
(225) <s>Māra</s> has been defeated by you, with his army and his mount;
swiftly blaze forth the <s>Dharma</s>, bringing happiness to all beings!
(226) We have not heard the <s>Dharma</s> by which we might become <s>Buddhas</s>."'

body.text:
bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattva āha -
(228) ūrdhvaṃ tāvannirīkṣadhvaṃ kiṃ paśyadhvaṃ hi sāṃprataṃ;
(229) avalokayanti te ūrdhvaṃ sthitā paṃca anūnakāḥ
śatāstrayaḥ sahasrāṇi kūṭāgārāḥ samantataḥ
(230) saptaratnasamārūḍhā ratnajālasvalaṃkṛtāḥ
padmaṃ praphullaṃ madhye ca divyagandhapramuñcanaṃ /
(231) pṛcchanti sthaviraṃ tatra kimetadiha dṛśyate
kūṭāgārā ratnajālāḥ padmakesarasaṃsthitāḥ

children.translated_text: <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said:
(232) 'These are your abodes. Go for the seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>!'
'Pay homage to the Light of the World, who is the supramundane Teacher!'

body.translated_text:
The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said:
(228) 'Look upward now! What do you see at this moment?'
(229) They looked upward, standing, the five thousand complete,
and saw hundreds of thousands of mansions all around,
(230) mounted upon the seven jewels, adorned with nets of jewels,
with a fully blooming lotus in the center, releasing divine fragrance.
(231) They asked the Elder there: 'What is this that is seen here —
mansions, nets of jewels, established upon lotus filaments?'

body.text:
ta āha -
(233) tatra mārgaṃ na jānīmo na paśyāmastathāgataṃ /
yatra mārgaṃ na jānīmaḥ kva gacchāma vandituṃ /
body.translated_text:
They said:
(233) 'We do not know the path there; we do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
Where we do not know the path, where shall we go to pay homage?'

body.text:
bhaiṣajyasena āha -
(234) vandanāya ca gantavyaṃ śāstāramamṛtaprabhaṃ /
anantamākāśamiva parāmārṣṭuṃ na śakyate /

children.text: (235) sthāne tiṣṭhatyasau śāstā yathā tiṣṭhanti meravaḥ
children.translated_text: (235) 'That Teacher abides in his place, just as <s>Merus</s> stand firm,
like <s>Sumeru</s> indeed, and like the depth of the great ocean.'
(236) 'From the dust of the three-thousandfold world, not from knowledge does the <s>Buddha</s> arise;'
'The Light of the World is honored by <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions.'

body.translated_text:
<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said:
(234) 'One must go to pay homage to the Teacher of immortal radiance;
like infinite space, he cannot be grasped.'

body.text:
ta āhuḥ -
(237) vilokaya lokanātha pūrayāsmakamāśayaṃ /
cittena vandito 'smābhiḥ śāstā labdhāstataḥ phalaṃ /
body.translated_text:
They said:
(237) 'Look upon us, O Lord of the World, and fulfill our aspiration!
The Teacher has been honored by us with our minds; from that, we have obtained the fruit.'

body.text:
bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattva āha -
(238) na gandhai rajyate śāstā na mālyairna
vilepanaiḥ hetuṃ gṛhṇāti sattvānāṃ yena mucyanti saṃskṛtāt
(239) saṃgrāmaṃ na kurute tasya māraḥ paramadāruṇaṃ;
damito hi mano yena buddhaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
(240) mṛtyorna yāsyati vaśaṃ kṣipraṃ prāpsyati dhāraṇī
cittaprasādaṃ kṛtvāsau śāstāraṃ paśyate tataḥ
body.translated_text:
The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said:
(238) 'The Teacher is not attached to fragrances, not to garlands, not to
ointments; he grasps the cause of beings by which they are freed from the conditioned.
(239) <s>Māra</s>, supremely terrible, does not wage war against the one
who has tamed his mind and gone to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge.
(240) He shall not fall under the power of death; quickly he shall attain <s>dhāraṇī</s>;
having generated faith of mind, he then sees the Teacher.'

body.text: [SaSū 254] atha khalu bhagavān kalaviṅkarutasvaramanojñaghoṣastathāgataḥ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāra; atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya yadbhagavato mukhadvārāccaturaśīti raśmiśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti / taiśca raśmibhiriyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrā lokadhāturavabhāsena sphuṭābhūt sarve ca dvātṛṃśan mahānirayā sphuṭā abhūvan dvātṛṃśatiśca devabhavanānyavabhāsitāni / tāśca raśmayo nānāvarṇāḥ tadyathā nīlapītalohitāvadātamaṃjiṣṭhāsphaṭikarajatavaraṇāḥ etāśca raśmayo bhagavato mukhadvārānniścarya trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sattvānāṃ sarvamukhopadhānaṃ kṛtvā punareva pratyudāvṛtya bhagavantaṃ saptakṛt pradakṣiṇākṛtya bhagavato mūrdhanyantaradhīyanta;
body.translated_text: [SaSū 254] Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kalaviṅkarutasvaramanojñaghoṣa</s>, displayed a smile. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, rising from his seat, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the display of a smile, that from the mouth of the Blessed One eighty-four hundred thousand rays emerge? By those rays, this great trichiliocosm was pervaded with light, and all thirty-two great hells were illuminated, and thirty-two divine palaces were illuminated. And those rays were of various colors, namely: blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver-colored. These rays, having emerged from the mouth of the Blessed One, having touched the faces of all beings in the great trichiliocosm, returned again, circumambulated the Blessed One seven times, and disappeared into the crown of the Blessed One's head.'

body.text: [SaSū 255] atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kañcideva pradeśaṃ sacenme bhagavān avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭaḥ praśnavyākaraṇāya; // evamukte bhagavāṃ bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena yadyadevākāṃkṣasyahaṃ te tasya tasyaiva (pṛṣṭasya) praśnasya vyākaraṇena cittamāradhayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 255] Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I would ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to ask a question for its elucidation.' When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Ask, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, whatever you wish. I will satisfy your mind with an answer to each and every question you ask.'

body.text: [SaSū 256] evamukte bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - tṛṃśatkoṭīsahasrāṇi bhagavannavakānāṃ sattvānāṃ prādurbhūtāni te tathāgatasya sūkṣmān dharmadeśanāmavagāhanti / sūkṣmaṃ bhagavan bṛddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ paribhāṣanti parivadanti paripīḍayanti / na yūyaṃ bṛddhāḥ sattvā dharmaṃ jānītha nityaṃ yūyaṃmadharme cākuśale ca rajyatha / tad bhagavān mṛṣṭā manāpā vāgbhāṣante tatkena kāraṇena bhagavantamevaṃ vāgbhāṣante / bhagavān āha - na vijānāsi bhaiṣajyasena kena kāraṇenaite sattvā evaṃ vāgbhāṣante / tathāgatasyaibhirmṛdukaṃ sukukāraṃ bhāṣitaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tenaite bhaiṣajyasena sarvadharmāṇāṃ arthamavabhotsyante sarvaguṇasamanvāgatāśca bhaviṣyanti / sarve ca dhāraṇāmavagāhiṣyanti / adya-d-agreṇa daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyanti / adya mahādundubhiśabdaṃ prakariṣyanti / adya mahādharmaprakārasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena imāni kūṭāgārāṇi // bhaiṣajyasena āha - paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata / bhagavān āha - adyeme bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ sattvāḥ eṣu kūṭāgāreṣvabhiruhya dharmābhisamayamanuprāpsyanti / adyeme sarvakuśaladharmapāripūriṃ kariṣyanti / adya mahādharmadundubhiṃ parāhaniṣyanti / anekeṣāṃ ca devanikāyānāmadya dharmābhisamayo bhaviṣyati / bahūnāñca nairayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ vinipātasaṃprasthitānāṃ tathāgatajñānanirdeśaṃ śrutvā sarvasaṃsāraparāṅmukhaparājayo bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 256] When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Thirty <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of young beings have appeared, Blessed One. They comprehend the <s>Tathāgata's</s> subtle <s>Dharma</s> teaching. They reproach, revile, and oppress the old beings, Blessed One, [saying]: "You old beings do not know the <s>Dharma</s>; you are always attached to <s>adharma</s> and unwholesomeness." Yet, Blessed One, they speak smooth, pleasant words. For what reason, Blessed One, do they speak thus?' The Blessed One said: 'You do not understand, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for what reason these beings speak thus. Having heard the <s>Tathāgata's</s> gentle, well-spoken <s>Dharma</s>, these beings, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, will comprehend the meaning of all <s>dharmas</s> and will become endowed with all virtues. All will penetrate <s>dhāraṇī</s> (powers of retention). From today onward they will become established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). Today they will produce the sound of the great drum. Today they will become endowed with the great expanse of <s>Dharma</s>. Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these mansions?' <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said: 'I see them, Blessed One; I see them, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Today, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these young beings, having ascended these mansions, will attain the realization of the <s>Dharma</s>. Today they will accomplish the fulfillment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Today they will strike the great <s>Dharma</s> drum. And for many hosts of gods, today there will be realization of the <s>Dharma</s>. And for many beings in the hells, those who have set out on the path of downfall, having heard the <s>Tathāgata's</s> instruction of knowledge, there will be the defeat of turning away from all <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 257] tasyām ca velāyāṃ vṛddhasattvairnavānavatibhiḥ koṭīśasraiḥ (sarve) srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptaṃ te ca sarvadharmasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / sarve te bhaiṣajyasena sarvaduḥkhaparivarjitā bhaviṣyanti / sarve te bhaiṣajyasena sarvatathāgatadarśanaṃ niṣpādayiṣyanti / sarve te bhaiṣajyasena mahādharmasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / avalokaya bhaiṣajyasena caturdiśaṃ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 257] And at that time, by ninety <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of old beings, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>) was attained by all. And they will become endowed with all <s>dharmas</s>. All of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, will become free from all suffering. All of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, will accomplish the seeing of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. All of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, will become endowed with the great <s>Dharma</s>. Look, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, in the four directions!

body.text: [SaSū 258] avalokayati bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ samantā caturdiśaṃ sa paśyati pūrvasyān diśi paṃcāśat koṭyo gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / dakṣiṇasyān diśi ṣaṣṭi koṭī gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / paścimasyāṃn diśi saptati koṭī gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / uttarasyān diśyaśīti koṭyo gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / adhastāddiśi navakoṭīsahasrāṇi gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi koṭīśatasahasraṃ gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānāmāgacchanti / te cāgatāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhagavataḥ purataḥ pādau śiraśābhivandyaikānte taśuḥ
body.translated_text: [SaSū 258] The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> looked all around in the four directions. He saw: from the eastern direction, fifty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. From the southern direction, sixty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. From the western direction, seventy <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. From the northern direction, eighty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. From the downward direction, nine <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. From the upward direction, a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousand of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river were coming. And those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, having arrived, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.

body.text: [SaSū 259] ekāntasthitānāṃ daśadigbhyāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānām mahāsattvānāmatha bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kimetad bhagavan khaga-m-antarīkṣe kṛṣṇarūpaṃ lohitarūpaṃ (ca) paśyāmi / bhagavān āha - kimidaṃ bhaiṣajyasena / na saṃjānāsi yadetadantarīkṣe kṛṣṇarūpaṃ lohitarūpaṃ ca paśyasi / āha / na jānāmi bhagavan na jānāmi sugata / bhagavān āha - eṣa tathāgata eva jānāti / māro 'yaṃ bhaiṣajyasena vicakṣuskaraṇāyehopasaṃkrāntaḥ icchasi bhaiṣajyasenaitān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān draṣṭuṃ ya ete khagāntarīkṣe vyavasthitāḥ āha / icchāmi bhagavannicchāmi sugata /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 259] When the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who had come from the ten directions were standing to one side, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What is this, Blessed One? I see a dark form and a red form in the sky above.' The Blessed One said: 'What is this, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>? Do you not perceive what you see as a dark form and a red form in the sky?' He said: 'I do not know, Blessed One; I do not know, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Only the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows this. This is <s>Māra</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, who has come here to blind [your vision]. Do you wish, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, to see these <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are stationed in the sky above?' He said: 'I wish it, Blessed One; I wish it, <s>Sugata</s>.'

body.text: [SaSū 260] atha bhagavāṃstān bodhisattvān darśayitvā bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayati sma / īdṛśānāṃ bhaiṣajyasena koṭīśatagaṃgānadīvālikāsamāni bodhisattvānā āgatāni / āha / ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadete bodhisattvā etāvanta ihāgatā / bhagavān āha - daharāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ pratyayena bhaiṣajyasena saṃprataṃ sarvasattvā dharmadhyānasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena ya ete bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nānārūpā āgatā ṛddhibalādhānena / āhāvalokitāni mayā koṭīśatagaṃgānadīvālikāsamā lokadhātavastatra mayā koṭīniyutaśatasahasragaṃgānadīvālikāsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dṛṣṭāḥ svakasvakena ṛddhibalena tiṣṭhanti nānārūpā nānāvarṇā nānābalasaṃsthānāstiṣṭhanti / āryadharmavihāreṣu te bodhisattvastiṣṭhanti / dharmavihāreṣu te bodhisattvaparivārāstiṣṭhanti /
body.translated_text: [SaSū 260] Then the Blessed One, having shown those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Such as these, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> have come.' He said: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause? What is the condition that so many <s>bodhisattvas</s> have come here?' The Blessed One said: 'On account of the young beings, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>—now all beings will become endowed with <s>Dharma</s> meditation. Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who have come in various forms by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous ability)?' He said: 'I have surveyed <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousands of world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. There I have seen <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, standing by their respective powers of <s>ṛddhi</s>, in various forms, various colors, in various configurations of power. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> abide in noble <s>Dharma</s>-abodes. Those <s>bodhisattva</s> retinues abide in <s>Dharma</s>-abodes.'

body.text: [SaSū 260] idamavocadbhagavān āttamanāḥ sarvaśuro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarve ca navapurāṇakā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ abhyanandat
body.translated_text: [SaSū 260] Thus spoke the Blessed One. Elated, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, all the new and old <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, the entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

body.text: Colophon B: // 0 // saṃghāṭaṃ nā[ma] mahāyānasūtraṃ mahādharmaparyāyaṃ //0//
body.translated_text: Colophon B: The <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>, a great <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma).

body.text: Colophon D: // 0 // āryasaṃghāṭaṃ nāma dharmmaparyāyaṃ samāptam //0//
body.translated_text: Colophon D: The noble <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), is completed.
